igcse-tuition.heroSubtitle: IGCSE tuition in the UAE is a scheduling problem before it is a teaching problem. Your child sits a dated series — Cambridge in June or November, Pearson Edexcel in May or June and November — and the entry that fixes that date closes months earlier. This page counts the year backwards from the first paper: what the month you start still buys, what the entry form locks shut, what results day opens and what it closes a fortnight later. Lessons are one-to-one and live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a UAE school day.

igcse-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at both tiers. Each profile names the syllabus codes that person has actually taught and the series they have taken candidates through. Tell us the subject, the board and the date of the first paper, and we will say plainly who is free at your hour.

intro.heading: The date is already fixed. Everything else is still a choice.
paragraphs: An IGCSE course in the UAE ends on a day somebody else chose. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson runs Edexcel International GCSE in May or June and again in November. Your child's school picked one of those, entered them for it, and most families find out by accident halfway through Year 11. Every useful decision about tuition sits downstream of that date: how many subjects, how many hours a week, which tier, whether to begin now or wait for the mock results in January.

So this page is organised around the calendar rather than around subjects. Each section answers one question with a date attached. When does the entry close? When does the tier stop being reversible? How many teaching weeks are left if you begin in February? When do results arrive, and what shuts fourteen days later? UAE families lose more marks to a closed window than to a weak topic, because a weak topic can be taught in four sessions and a closed entry cannot be reopened at any price.

The dates below come from the boards themselves. Cambridge's published key dates for the March series put the examination period at 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and its November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after reading the wrong zone's timetable, which is why the first thing to confirm is a centre and a zone, not a tutor.

Verifiability is not the same across boards. Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly and revise them in public. We restate no IB examination or results date anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date here would be worse than no date at all. Where your child sits IB components alongside or instead of IGCSE, confirm every window with the school's programme coordinator and work from that.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video. Nobody arrives at a UAE address; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate trade rather than a limitation. A family in Khalifa City gets the tutor who has taught Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended through four series, instead of whoever happens to be free inside a twenty-minute drive at five in the afternoon. Working through a marked script on a shared screen is also better than working across a kitchen table, because both people are looking at the same line of the same answer at the same moment.

What this page will not do is quote you our hourly rate dressed up as market research. The AED figures here are market figures, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. IB Gram's own commercial conversation happens after a trial lesson and after someone has read your child's last set of marks, which is the only point at which a number means anything.
bullets: Confirm three things before buying any hours: the board, the series and the centre's Cambridge zone.
Cambridge final entries for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, about ten weeks before the first paper.
Pearson November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results reached them on 20 August 2026.
The Ministry of Education counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and excludes Arabic and Islamic Education from that five.
A tutor giving paid private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.
Delivery is live, online and one-to-one; home visits are an India-only service.

igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE is not one programme with one clock. A UAE school may run a two-year Cambridge course from Year 10, a Pearson course with its own series pattern, a Year 9 foundation year that decides the option block, or a compressed entry for a child who arrived mid-course. These four shapes carry different deadlines, and the plan has to match the shape.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, two-year course
programmes.description: The common British-curriculum route in the UAE: eight to ten subjects begun in Year 10 and examined at the end of Year 11, with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0510 English as a Second Language. Most subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with tier entry decided by the school on forecast evidence. Cambridge examines in June and November, and the final entry sits months ahead of the paper.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the June series is the default, and a November entry is usually a retake or an early entry. Because Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, two Dubai schools can hold different timetable versions for the same series, so the timetable to plan revision against is the one for your child's own centre.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international qualification, entered under codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4EA1 English Language A. Examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, which gives a family two usable doors in a twelve-month period rather than one. Grading is reported on its own scale, and the specification for a subject can differ from the Cambridge equivalent in both content and paper structure.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools enter some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson, which means one child can hold two timetables and two sets of deadlines. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so a plan should reference the live official timetable rather than a date copied from a tuition website.

programmes.name: Pre-IGCSE foundation year
programmes.description: The year in which the option block is chosen and, quietly, the grade ceiling is set. Nothing is examined externally, which is exactly why it is the cheapest year in which to fix a maths or literacy weakness. A student who enters Year 10 unable to rearrange an equation will meet that same gap in physics, chemistry and additional mathematics, three times over, with a deadline attached.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools run the option-choice conversation in the spring term of Year 9, and families often attend it without knowing that the Ministry of Education counts five accredited subjects for equivalency and excludes Arabic and Islamic Education from that count. Knowing the rule before the form is signed is worth more than a term of tuition afterwards.

programmes.name: Private candidate and retake entry
programmes.description: A route for home-educated students, for a subject a school will not enter, for an early entry, and for a leaver who needs one more grade for a university file. The candidate registers through an examination centre that accepts private entries for that syllabus and series. Centre fees and cut-off dates are set by the centre, not the board, and must be confirmed in writing with that centre before any teaching plan is built.
programmes.countryNote: Not every UAE centre accepts private candidates for every syllabus, and coursework or practical components are the usual sticking point because a centre can only assess what it is approved to assess. Settle the entry question first; a UAE IGCSE private candidate with no confirmed centre has a revision plan pointing at nothing.

igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed with their syllabus codes because a code is the only unambiguous way to confirm what your child is actually entered for. Ask the school for the code, not the subject name. The notes below say where marks go missing in UAE classrooms, which is usually a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge / 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Two papers at each tier, non-calculator and calculator work split differently by board. Marks go missing on the Extended-only material: algebraic fractions, functions, vectors and the harder trigonometry. The other common loss is method marks thrown away by a candidate who writes an answer with no working, which costs more over a whole paper than any single topic.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge / 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Content is manageable; the marks sit in graph work, unit handling and the practical paper or alternative-to-practical component. Candidates lose marks describing an experiment without naming the controlled variable, and lose more on multi-step calculations where the rearrangement happens in their head. Both are teachable in a handful of sessions if they are diagnosed early enough.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge / 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The reliable mark-losers are moles arithmetic, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables that candidates try to memorise rather than reason through. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition, so it responds quickly to structured practice. Extended-tier candidates should be working through full past papers under time by January, not in April.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge / 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and therefore deceptive: students who know the material still lose marks to command terms. Describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer shape, and an explanation offered where a description was asked for scores nothing. Data-response and experimental-design questions are where the top grades are separated.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: A double or single award covering three sciences in less time, common for students carrying nine or ten subjects. The risk is that one of the three strands goes untaught in the student's head while the other two carry the grade. A tutor should be auditing all three strands separately, not treating the subject as one block.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Widely sat across the UAE and often underestimated. Reading comprehension marks hinge on lifting the right words from the passage, and the writing papers are marked against a register and audience brief that students routinely ignore. Speaking components are assessed internally, so the school's own calendar governs them.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Marks live in structure and evidence, not vocabulary. Directed-writing tasks fail when a student answers the topic rather than the brief, and analysis questions fail when a quotation is presented without comment. Progress here is slower than in maths and should be bought earlier in the course for that reason.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading into A-Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches. Calculus, logarithms and kinematics arrive fast, and a student who was comfortable at Extended can still be caught out because the pace assumes fluency rather than familiarity. Good preparation here removes most of the usual shock in the first post-16 term.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Essay and data-response marks follow a visible structure: definition, application, analysis, then evaluation that actually weighs something. Students who learn the definitions and stop there cap themselves in the low grades. Case-study material rewards practice on real past questions far more than note-making.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory of data representation are the mark-heavy areas, and the programming component punishes students who code by instinct without a written plan. Specialist availability for this syllabus is thinner than for maths or physics, which is one reason distance should not be the thing deciding who teaches it.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Arabic (0544)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Taken for its own sake and sometimes as a bridge to the mandatory ministry subjects, which run on a separate internal calendar. Worth knowing before planning around it: the Ministry of Education does not count Arabic among the five subjects it requires for equivalency, so an Arabic grade is valuable, but it is not one of the five.

igcse-tuition.regionsTitle: Where your child sits the papers, emirate by emirate
igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: Delivery is the same wherever you are, because it is online. What changes by emirate is who holds the school's file, which inspection archive you can read before trusting a subject, and what an examination fortnight looks like in practice. Those three things are worth knowing before the plan is written.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA inspects Dubai's private schools and publishes the reports, so a subject-level judgement can be read before you decide which subject to buy hours in. Dubai held 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, the largest IGCSE cohort in the country.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff, as reported in the press, bar a teacher from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so an evening arrangement with a class teacher is the wrong first thought here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort and a correspondingly thin local specialist pool for syllabuses like 0478 Computer Science or 0606 Additional Mathematics. This is the clearest case for online delivery: an Al Ain family should not be choosing between two available tutors.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai schools, so a 4pm session is unrealistic on a school night and the workable slot is usually after 7pm.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, which means there is no local inspection archive to read in the way Dubai parents read KHDA reports. Ask the school directly for subject results by paper, and plan from that.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Distance from Dubai limits nothing about a live online session, but it does limit which centres are practical for a private candidate entry, so confirm the centre before anything else.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory, on the east coast, with the smallest British-curriculum cohort of the seven emirates. Families here are frequently told a subject specialist is unavailable. The honest position is that a specialist is available online or not at all, and we will say which before you book.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally. The practical issue for IGCSE candidates here is examination logistics rather than teaching: journeys to a centre in a neighbouring emirate on consecutive examination mornings need planning in the entry term, not in the examination fortnight.

schoolClusters.note: This cluster produces the largest IGCSE entry in the country and the widest spread of tier practice: some schools enter almost everyone at Extended, others stream carefully from Year 10. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, so cohort sizes in individual year groups are still moving.

A smaller, more concentrated British-curriculum cluster under ADEK. Families here more often sit a mixed entry, with some subjects under Cambridge and some under Pearson, which doubles the number of deadlines a parent has to track and is the single most common source of a surprise in the examination fortnight.

Schools across SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge and federal Ministry of Education territory. The practical constraints are the commute and the local specialist pool rather than the teaching itself, which is why online evening sessions dominate here and why entry logistics for private candidates deserve an early phone call.

igcse-tuition.modesIntro: Tuition shapes are named here by the phase of the year they belong to, because an hour bought in September is doing a different job from an hour bought in April. Every format below is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the recording of the session available to the student afterwards.

modes.title: Year 10 maintenance block
modes.description: One hour a week on one subject, running term-time, with the work set between sessions mattering more than the session itself. This is the cheapest form of help in the whole course because nothing has to be undone yet. The job is fluency: a student who can rearrange an equation in Year 10 does not pay for that gap three times in Year 11.

modes.title: Post-mock recovery block
modes.description: Six to eight weeks from January, built directly on the marked mock script rather than on a syllabus checklist. The script says where the marks went; the block spends its hours there and nowhere else. This is the point in the year at which the most grade movement per hour is still available, because there is time to teach as well as to practise.

modes.title: Twelve-week examination-term intensive
modes.description: Two hours a week per subject across the final term, counted in full past papers rather than in topics. Twelve weeks at two hours is twenty-four hours, which is roughly eight complete papers attempted, marked and reworked. Beyond three subjects this format stops helping, because the time it demands between sessions collides with the school's own revision programme.

modes.title: Post-results retake block
modes.description: A short, dated block for a candidate re-entering in the next series, planned from the statement of results rather than from a general sense that things went badly. The statement shows which component failed, and a retake plan that ignores that breakdown usually reproduces the same grade. Entry for the next series has to be confirmed before teaching starts.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when the examination date is already set
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition in the UAE buys teaching time against a fixed deadline. The date your child sits the first paper is set by Cambridge or Pearson, the entry that locks it is submitted by the school months earlier, and no amount of money moves either. What tuition can move is how many of the available marks the student is in a position to collect on the day. That is the whole product, and it is worth saying in those words because most pages in this market will not.

Parents searching this phrase are usually at one of four points in the year. Some are in Year 10 and want nothing to go wrong. Some have just read a January mock report and are alarmed. Some are eight weeks out and want to know whether it is too late. Some are holding a statement of results and deciding about a retake. The same subject, the same tutor and the same hourly rate produce completely different outcomes at those four points, and a page that gives one answer to all four is not telling anyone the truth.

The honest version runs roughly like this. In Year 10, an hour a week on the weakest subject is the best value available in the whole two-year course. After the January mocks, a six to eight week block built on the marked script moves more grades per hour than anything else, because there is still time to teach rather than only to drill. Eight weeks out, the job stops being teaching and becomes triage: the two or three highest-mark topics, paper technique and timing. Five weeks out it is purely technique, and anyone promising more than that is selling something.

Everything that follows is dated. Where a date comes from a board, the board is named. Where a figure comes from a provider in this market, that provider is named and the month we read it is stated. Where something cannot be verified, this page says so instead of filling the gap.
bullets: Year 10: fluency work, one hour a week, the cheapest fix in the course
January, after mocks: a six to eight week block built on the marked script
Eight weeks out: triage by mark weight, not syllabus coverage
Five weeks out: timing, command terms and full papers only

sections.heading: The month you begin, and what a weekly hour can still change
paragraphs: The single most useful number in an IGCSE plan is the count of teaching weeks left, not the count of weeks left. UAE term breaks, National Day, Eid and the school's own revision timetable remove a surprising amount from the calendar, and a family that counts calendar weeks consistently overestimates what it has bought. The table below counts teaching weeks to a June first paper, which is the common UAE case.

What changes with the month is not the hourly rate but the kind of work the hour can hold. In September there is room to teach a topic properly, then come back to it a month later and find out whether it stuck. By March there is no second pass: a topic is taught once, practised in a paper, and whatever remains unlearned stays unlearned. That is why a September hour and a March hour buy different things even when they cost the same.

The right-hand column is the part most families get wrong. Doubling sessions late in the year does not double the learning, because the work between sessions is where most of it happens and an exhausted Year 11 student has a fixed amount of that work in them. Two one-hour sessions a week per subject is the practical ceiling, and three is only reasonable in the final month on a single subject, with the school's own revision programme accounted for.

One more thing the table cannot show: the later you start, the more of the first session goes on diagnosis rather than teaching. In September that is a cheap half-hour. In April it is a tenth of everything you have left, which is a real argument for buying a trial lesson early even if the weekly block starts later.

sections.heading: The taught-hours ledger: how much time one IGCSE subject actually gets
paragraphs: Before buying an hour it is worth knowing how many hours the subject already has. The arithmetic is simple and no competitor page does it. KHDA calculates instructional time for the mandatory UAE subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit, which is also the usual period length in British-curriculum schools here, so a parent can count their child's provision straight off the timetable.

Four periods a week is 160 minutes. Across roughly 35 teaching weeks that is about 93 hours a year, or 185 across the two-year course, shared with every other student in the room. A core subject on five periods gets about 230 hours over two years. Those are the real numbers behind a grade, and they explain why one well-aimed hour a week is not a marginal addition: 70 hours of one-to-one teaching across two years is around a third again on top of an option subject's classroom time, and all of it is diagnostic rather than delivered to a room.

The ledger also shows where the time is not. None of those classroom hours is spent watching your individual child make an individual mistake and correcting it on the spot. Whole-class pace is set somewhere near the middle of the room, which is efficient for the school and invisible for the student at either end of it. That gap is the honest case for one-to-one tuition, and it is a different case from the one usually made.

Run the arithmetic on your own child's timetable before you decide which subject to fund. A subject on three periods a week with a demanding specification is a better target than a subject on six, even when the current grade in the three-period subject looks slightly better.

sections.heading: How many subjects to put under tuition, and when to stop adding
paragraphs: A UAE Year 11 student commonly sits nine or ten IGCSEs alongside the mandatory ministry subjects. Families under pressure respond by adding tuition subjects one at a time until the week stops working, usually in February. The decision deserves arithmetic rather than instinct, because each added subject costs not only its hour but the work set between sessions.

The second column of the table is the one that matters. A single tuition subject is about two to three hours of a student's week once the set work is counted. Three subjects is six to eight hours, on top of a full school day, the school's own revision programme and the ministry subjects. Four is nine or more, and at that point the tuition is competing with sleep, which reliably costs more marks than the tuition gains.

If funding is limited, pick by mark weight and by reversibility rather than by the lowest grade. A maths or science gap compounds, because the same algebraic weakness shows up in three subjects. An essay-subject weakness improves more slowly and is the worse choice to start in March. And a subject where the student has simply not been taught a late topic is a four-session fix that should be bought early and then stopped, not carried all year.

The cost column uses Bestimate's published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session in its Dubai 2026 rate table, which puts a mid-market weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Those are market figures from that source, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Entry, tier and withdrawal: the windows that shut before the paper
paragraphs: Several decisions in an IGCSE course stop being decisions on a date. The Cambridge IGCSE entry deadline is the clearest example: final entries for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, about ten weeks before the examination period opened on 3 February 2027. After that date the subject list is the subject list. Tier entry follows a similar logic, set by the school on forecast evidence, with forecast grades for that series due on 27 February 2027.

This is where IGCSE Core and Extended becomes a calendar question rather than a teaching question. Extended carries the higher grade ceiling and the extra content; Core caps the grade but reduces what has to be covered. A school moves a student between tiers on evidence it already holds, so the useful work is producing that evidence in the autumn term, not arguing about it in March. A tutor's job here is to show, on marked work, what the Extended-only topics are currently costing in marks.

Withdrawal and deferral are less discussed and more often the right answer. A student carrying ten subjects and failing to prepare for any of them properly may be better entered for eight. Because the Ministry of Education counts five accredited subjects for equivalency, dropping from ten to eight generally leaves the university file intact, while dropping to four does not. That arithmetic should happen in the entry term, with the school, in writing.

One warning about sequencing. Nothing in the table below can be arranged by a tutor. Entries, tiers, withdrawals and deferrals are school and centre decisions. What a tutor can do is produce the evidence and the honest assessment that the conversation needs, early enough for the conversation to still be possible.

sections.heading: Sitting the papers as a private candidate in the UAE
paragraphs: Some UAE families need an entry their school will not make: a home-educated student, a subject dropped from the option block, an early entry, or a leaver who needs one more grade. The route is an examination centre that accepts private entries for that syllabus and that series. It works, and it is routinely the thing nobody explains until it is too late to arrange.

Three practical constraints govern it. First, a centre accepts private candidates syllabus by syllabus and series by series, not in general, so the question is always about one code and one date. Second, the centre's own cut-off sits before the board's final entry date, often by weeks, because the centre has to collate and submit. Third, components assessed inside a centre, including practical work and coursework, can only be taken where that centre is approved to assess them, which is the usual reason a private entry falls over.

Fees are set by the centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, they vary, and this page will not invent a figure for them. Ask the centre for its entry fee per syllabus, its late-entry position and its cut-off date in writing, and do it before any teaching plan is built. An IGCSE private candidate in the UAE with a revision plan and no confirmed centre has nothing.

A retake sits inside the same framework. A student still enrolled is usually re-entered by their school. A leaver needs a centre, and needs it quickly, because the next series' entry date arrives soon after results. Our part is the teaching and an honest view of whether the retake is the better use of the money; the entry is yours and the centre's.

sections.heading: Results day, and the two clocks that start on it
paragraphs: Results arrive on a published day and two short windows open behind them. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge released March-series results on Direct on 13 May with certificates in late June. Those are the boards' own figures, and they show the gap between a statement of results and a certificate.

The first clock is the enquiry about results, run through the centre and never by a family directly, with a deadline set by the board shortly after release. A review of marking can move a mark in either direction, and anyone who tells you otherwise is guessing. The decision is worth making on evidence: if one component sits far below the others and the student's own account of the paper matches, the case is stronger than a general sense of disappointment.

The second clock is re-entry. The next series' entry date arrives quickly, and a retake decision made in week three is a different thing from one made in week eight. Read the component breakdown before deciding anything. A grade lost on one paper is a different problem, and a much cheaper one, than a grade lost evenly across every component.

Universities in the region generally work from the statement of results while the certificate is in production, and the Ministry of Education equivalency file is opened on the same evidence. The practical sequence is: read the breakdown, decide about an enquiry inside the board's window, decide about re-entry before the next entry date, and start the equivalency paperwork in parallel rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: IGCSE tutor rates in AED, and what the month does to the number
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for this kind of query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. So here is the market, in dirhams, with every figure attributed to whoever published it and the month we read it stated. None of these is an IB Gram rate.

The bands are wide for a reason. A budget online hour and a specialist hour are not the same product, and the difference is not polish but diagnosis: whether the tutor can look at a marked Extended paper and name the three things costing marks. For a Year 10 fluency block, the lower bands are genuinely enough. For a February triage plan on Extended Chemistry, they are not, and paying twice for the wrong hour is the expensive mistake in this market.

Timing moves the bill more than the headline rate does. The same subject, started in September at one hour a week, is cheaper over the whole course than a February block at two hours a week, and it produces a better result. The rate itself does not need to rise near a series for the cost to rise; the number of hours does. Any family being told that late hours cost more per hour should ask what else changed.

For context, Dubai's school fees were frozen for 2026-27, confirmed by KHDA on 22 May 2026 under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tuition is not covered by that and nothing restrains it, which is one more argument for buying fewer, earlier, better-aimed hours instead of a large block in the final term.

sections.heading: Live online one-to-one against a visiting tutor, with an entry date running
paragraphs: Parents who search for IGCSE help in the UAE are often picturing somebody at the dining table. It is a reasonable thing to want, the market supplies it, and this page should answer it properly rather than steer around it. Visiting tutors in this market charge roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table at 180 to 350, and travel is priced into that figure whether or not it is itemised.

IB Gram does not supply it in the UAE. One-to-one IGCSE lessons online are what we deliver here, over live video, with visiting tutors offered only in India. We say that in the first screen of every UAE page rather than at the bottom of a terms document, because a family that books on a wrong assumption has wasted a week it did not have.

The case for online is specific rather than general. A UAE family's real constraint is the size of the local specialist pool: Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606 and the harder Extended science syllabuses are thin on the ground in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah, and perfectly available on a screen. A thirty to sixty minute drive each way across Dubai at six in the evening is also, in examination term, an entire extra session a week that nobody is teaching in.

Where online genuinely loses, this page should say so. A young student who needs somebody physically present to stay on task is better served in a room. So is a family with no quiet space and no reliable connection. For a Year 10 or Year 11 candidate working through a marked script, the screen is equal or better, because both people annotate the same page at the same moment.

sections.heading: Which authority holds your child's file, and who permits the tutor
paragraphs: Two separate regulatory questions get mixed together in this market. The first is who oversees the school. The second is who permits the individual to charge for lessons. They sit with different bodies, and conflating them is how a tuition website ends up describing its tutors as regulator-endorsed, which no school regulator in this country does for individuals.

School oversight is emirate by emirate. In Dubai, KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, as does Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, and SPEA by one.

The tutor question sits with MoHRE. Private tuition in the UAE is permitted through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists a two working day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

Two things follow for a parent. Ask a tutor to show the permit rather than asking whether they have one. And do not try to arrange evening lessons with your child's own class teacher: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff, as reported in the press, bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to the same effect. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership of any kind, and any page telling you otherwise about any provider is worth closing.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run on a different calendar
paragraphs: A UAE IGCSE plan that only counts Cambridge and Pearson deadlines is missing three graded subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies.

These subjects are assessed on the school's internal calendar rather than a board's, which is precisely why they collide badly. A school assessment in Arabic lands in the same fortnight as a Cambridge mock and nobody planned for it, because it was not on the list of dates the family was tracking. Put the school's internal assessment calendar next to the board timetable at the start of the year, on one page, and the collisions become visible months early.

The rules around delivery are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited.

What that last rule means for tuition is worth stating plainly: support in these subjects works on the school's own material and the ministry curriculum, not on an alternative scheme a tutor prefers. And when the equivalency file is counted, the Arabic and Islamic Education grades sit outside the five accredited subjects the ministry requires, so they matter for the school report and not for that count.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some pages in this market sell finished assessed work. One of them lists a price for a completed Internal Assessment. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and the student is the one who carries the consequence. It is worth knowing that the market contains this before deciding who to hire.

The line is not blurry once stated. A tutor may teach the skills a component needs, explain the assessment criteria, talk through a plan, ask questions about a draft the student has produced, mark a practice attempt, and say clearly where it falls short and why. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft into its final form, or hand over work for submission. The test a parent can apply is simple: could the student explain every sentence and every decision to their subject teacher without help? If not, it is not their work.

Practical science is the honest edge case for online delivery. Where a syllabus examines practical skills through a written or alternative-to-practical component, that component is entirely teachable on a screen, because it assesses experimental reasoning, variable control, graph work and evaluation rather than manual technique. Where a component requires assessed laboratory work, the school or the centre must deliver it and no tutor substitutes for that. We say which case applies before a block is booked.

A last point on materials. Board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and we link them from their official pages rather than redistributing copies. A tutor charging you for a document the board publishes without charge is a signal about everything else in that arrangement.

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file, opened before results day
paragraphs: The deadline nobody counts backwards from is the one at the end: the Ministry of Education equivalency a UAE student needs for a local university file. It is not something a tutoring provider performs, guarantees or speeds up, and it is not something tuition is required for. It is, however, something the option block in Year 10 can quietly make harder.

For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one page ranking for these queries tells UAE parents the number is six.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Maths test. For the IB route, no points threshold appears in any source this project could verify, so none is published here. Confirm every figure on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before planning against it.

Practically, open the file on the day the statement of results arrives rather than when the certificate does, since regional universities generally work from the statement first. And run the subject count during the Year 9 option conversation, which is where an eight-subject timetable with four countable passes is accidentally created.

process.title: Tell us the date, not only the subject
process.description: The first message we want names the board, the syllabus code, the series and the date of the first paper, plus the school and emirate. That is enough to say how many teaching weeks remain and what is realistically available in them. A plan built without the date is a guess, and in February a guess is expensive.

process.title: A trial lesson built on a marked script
process.description: One lesson at no charge, one per family, before anything is booked, and we ask for a recent marked paper to work from rather than a syllabus list. The session is a diagnosis: the tutor should finish it able to name what is costing marks. If they cannot, that is useful information about the match.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards in weeks
process.description: You receive the plan in writing: weeks to the first paper, what each block covers, which topics are deliberately left out and why, and what the student is expected to do between sessions. Leaving things out on purpose is the part that makes a late plan work, so it is written down rather than implied.

process.title: Weekly sessions online, with the reschedule rule agreed first
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually after 7pm on a school night. The reschedule rule, the notice period and what happens during Ramadan and term breaks are settled before the first paid hour, because that is the conversation families most often have too late.

process.title: Two scheduled reviews: at the mock, and six weeks out
process.description: The plan is checked against the mock result and again six weeks before the first paper, both times against marked evidence rather than impressions. Either review can end the arrangement. Six weeks out, if a subject is not moving, the right advice is usually to move the hours to a different subject and say so.

whyPoints.title: Dates with the page they came from
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page is attributed to that board's published key dates or timetable, and we link the live official timetable rather than restating a date that can be revised. No IB session date appears here at all, because we could not verify one against the IB's own site.

whyPoints.title: AED figures attributed, never presented as ours
whyPoints.description: Each rate in the tables above names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the main pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. Our own number comes after a trial lesson and a look at recent marks, not from a table on a landing page.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: The match is made on the code your child is entered for: 0580 rather than 'maths', 4PH1 rather than 'physics'. Specialists for codes like 0478 and 0606 are thin in several emirates, and online delivery is the reason an Al Ain family is not choosing between the only two people nearby.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches the skills, explains the criteria, questions a draft the student wrote and marks practice attempts. No tutor supplies text for submission or rewrites a draft into its final form. The market contains providers selling completed coursework, and the student is the one who carries that risk.

whyPoints.title: The permit position stated, not glossed over
whyPoints.description: Paid private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years. We tell you to ask to see it. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

whyPoints.title: Online, and said so on the first screen
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are live, online and one-to-one. Visiting tutors are a service we run only in India, and that is stated at the top of every UAE page rather than discovered during a booking call. A family that books on a wrong assumption loses a week, and in Year 11 a week is a real cost.

faqs.question: We are starting in January. How many teaching weeks are actually left before a June paper?
faqs.answer: About eighteen, once UAE term breaks, Eid, the school's own revision timetable and the examination lead-in are taken out. Count teaching weeks rather than calendar weeks, because the difference is usually five or six weeks and it changes the plan. Eighteen weeks at one hour a week is enough to teach two weak topics properly per subject, build timing discipline on full papers, and fix one structural problem such as working shown or command-term reading. It is not enough to cover a syllabus a student has largely not learned. If that is the situation, the honest conversation is about which subjects to prioritise.

faqs.question: How many taught hours does one IGCSE subject get in a UAE school week?
faqs.answer: Count it off the timetable. British-curriculum schools here commonly run 40-minute periods, the same lesson unit KHDA uses to calculate instructional time for the mandatory UAE subjects. Four periods is 160 minutes a week, which over roughly 35 teaching weeks is about 93 hours a year and around 185 across the two-year course, shared with everyone else in the room. A five-period core subject gets about 230 hours over two years. One weekly tuition hour adds around 70 hours across the same period, roughly a third again, and all of it is spent on your child's own errors.

faqs.question: Can a subject be withdrawn after the school has submitted the entry?
faqs.answer: Before submission it is a conversation with the school. After the board's final entry date it becomes a centre and board matter, and the practical answer is usually no. This is why the entry term is the moment to decide whether a student carrying ten subjects should be entered for eight. Since the Ministry of Education counts five accredited IGCSE subjects for equivalency, moving from ten to eight normally leaves the university file intact while reducing an unmanageable load. Ask the school for its internal deadline, which sits earlier than the board's, and have the conversation before that.

faqs.question: Our son is entered for Extended and is not coping. When can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Tier entry is the school's decision, taken on forecast evidence, and it sits with the entry process rather than with teaching. For Cambridge's March 2027 series, final entries fell on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades were due 27 February 2027, which shows how early the evidence has to exist. So the useful work is in the autumn term: marked papers that show what the Extended-only topics are costing. Moving to Core caps the achievable grade but reduces what must be covered, and the subject still counts towards the ministry's five if the grade clears the floor. Raise it with the school early, with marked work in hand.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge administrative zone mean for the timetable we should be reading?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the series timetable. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Practically, this means two schools in the same city can hold different timetable versions for the same series. Ask your child's school for its centre number and zone, then plan revision against that zone's timetable from the board's own site, not against a date copied from a tuition website.

faqs.question: Is there an examination centre in the UAE that will take my daughter as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Centres in the UAE do accept private candidates, but not universally: acceptance is syllabus by syllabus and series by series, so the question is always about one code and one date. The centre's own cut-off falls before the board's final entry date, often by weeks. The common failure point is a component the centre is not approved to assess, which is usually coursework or assessed practical work. Ask the centre for its entry fee per syllabus, its cut-off date and its position on your specific components, in writing, before any teaching plan is built around the entry.

faqs.question: What does the Pearson series pattern change about when we buy hours?
faqs.answer: Pearson runs Edexcel International GCSE examinations in May or June and again in November each year, so a family has two usable doors in a twelve-month period rather than one. That changes the arithmetic of a weak subject: deferring one subject to November can be better than entering it underprepared in June, provided the entry is arranged before the deadline. It also changes retakes, since the November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Check the provisional timetable on Pearson's own site, because dates can be revised before a series is confirmed.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE tuition in the UAE delivered online, or does somebody come to the villa?
faqs.answer: Ours is delivered online. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, usually after 7pm on a school night, with the session available to rewatch afterwards. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram runs only in India, and we state that up front rather than at the end of a booking call. The UAE market does supply visiting tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in. If a physical presence is what your child needs to stay on task, that market exists and we will say so rather than talk you out of it.

faqs.question: The last paper is finished. Is there anything worth doing before results day?
faqs.answer: Two things, neither of them revision. First, write down what happened in each paper while it is fresh: which questions ran out of time, which topics appeared, where the student knew they guessed. On results day that note is the difference between an evidence-based decision about an enquiry and a general feeling. Second, if the next step is a sixth-form or Diploma course, the summer is the cheapest time to close a known gap, particularly the jump from Extended maths into Advanced Level or IB Analysis and Approaches. Everything else can wait until the statement of results arrives.

faqs.question: Our daughter's statement of results shows one paper far below the others. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It usually means something specific went wrong rather than that the subject was not learned, and the two situations call for different responses. A single component far below the rest points at timing, a misread question type, or one untaught topic that happened to carry heavy marks. Losses spread evenly across every component point at content. The first is a short, targeted block. The second is a longer one. It is also the stronger case for an enquiry about results, which runs through the centre within a short window after release, and which can move a mark in either direction.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we put under tuition at the same time without it backfiring?
faqs.answer: Two is comfortable, three is the practical ceiling in examination term, and four is where it usually starts costing marks. The reason is the work between sessions rather than the sessions themselves: one tuition subject is about two to three hours of a student's week once set work is counted, so three subjects is six to eight hours on top of a full school day, the school's revision programme and the mandatory ministry subjects. Beyond that the hours come out of sleep. If funding is limited, choose by mark weight and by what compounds, which is normally maths or a science rather than an essay subject.

faqs.question: Do UAE tuition rates actually rise as the examination series gets closer?
faqs.answer: The published hourly bands in this market do not visibly move with the calendar: providers quote the same figures in September as in April, from Tutopiya's AED 33 to 52 at the budget end to BartyED's AED 650 at the top. What rises is the number of hours a late plan needs. A February start at two sessions a week costs more over the course than a September start at one, and produces less. So if anyone quotes you a higher per-hour figure because examinations are close, ask what changed about the lesson. Usually nothing did.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my son's past-paper attempts, or is that the school's job?
faqs.answer: Both, and they are doing different things. The school marks to report progress against a cohort. A tutor marks to find the pattern: the same unit error in three questions, the explanation given where a description was asked for, the eight minutes lost on question two that cost question six. That diagnosis is most of what one-to-one time is for. Note that board papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, so we work from their official pages rather than redistributing copies, and nobody should be charging you for a document the board publishes openly.

faqs.question: Which school subjects sit on the school's own deadline calendar rather than Cambridge's?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and which are assessed internally. That is exactly why they collide with a board timetable: an internal Arabic assessment lands in the same fortnight as a mock and nobody saw it coming, because it was not on the list of dates being tracked. Internally assessed components of IGCSE subjects, such as speaking in English as a Second Language, behave the same way. Put the school's internal assessment calendar beside the board timetable at the start of the year.

faqs.question: Does a tutor giving paid lessons to a UAE family need a permit, and does it cost us anything?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit. Private tuition runs on a MoHRE work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two working day completion time. Because it carries no fee, nobody can legitimately pass a permit cost on to you. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any quoted figure as unverified.

igcse-tuition.closingHeading: Start from the date, then buy the hours
igcse-tuition.closingBody: Send us four things: the board, the syllabus code, the series and the date of the first paper, plus the school and emirate. We will reply with the number of teaching weeks left, what is realistically available in them, and whether a specialist for that code is free at your hour. If nobody is, we will say so rather than offer you a near-match. The first lesson is at no charge, one per family, and we would rather spend it on a recent marked paper than on a syllabus checklist. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; visiting tutors remain an India-only service.

intro.heading: Near me is the wrong filter for an IGCSE year; the calendar is the right one
paragraphs: A search for IGCSE tuition near me is a search for reassurance. The assumption underneath it is that distance decides quality, and that a tutor twenty minutes away must know your child's course better than one on a screen. In the UAE that assumption breaks early. Your child's school may be licensed by KHDA in Dubai, by ADEK in Abu Dhabi or Al Ain, by SPEA in Sharjah, by the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, or supervised by the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The paper sat in June, though, is set in Cambridge or by Pearson, and the deadline that decides whether it is sat at all closed months earlier.

Three things in an IGCSE year really are local. The examination centre is one: your child has to walk into a room, on a date, with a candidate number. The equivalency and attestation counter is another, because the Ministry of Education asks for documents handled in person or through its own channels rather than by a tutoring company. The third is the clock itself, which is why every session IB Gram arranges is timed to Gulf Standard Time and to the evening a UAE family actually has free after the school run, Maghrib and dinner.

The tutor is not on that list. A family in Al Reef who insists on proximity is choosing from the adults who live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Reef. A family that drops the proximity filter is choosing from specialists in Physics 0625, Additional Maths 0606, Business Studies 0450 or Pearson 4MA1 wherever they teach. For a Year 10 child who needs steady support that distinction is mild. For a Year 11 child nine weeks from a paper, it decides whether the hours are spent on the right command terms or on general encouragement.

What changes with distance from the paper is not the subject but the job. Twenty-four weeks out, a tutor can still rebuild a topic from the ground up and can argue for a tier change before the entry form is signed. Ten weeks out, the syllabus is the syllabus and the work is past-paper technique, mark-scheme literacy and the two or three topics the mocks exposed. Three weeks out, almost nothing new should be taught; the hours belong to timing, question selection and the mechanical errors that cost a grade. A good IGCSE revision plan is written in weeks, not in topics.

So this page is organised as a calendar rather than as a sales pitch. It sets out the three assessment windows Cambridge and Pearson publish, one academic year on a single planner, the same year counted backwards in weeks, what results day actually delivers and when, what IGCSE tuition in the UAE costs as a function of how late you start, and the Ministry paperwork that should be opened before results arrive. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and the comparison table further down makes the case for the model on its merits.

igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Four programmes sit under one roof in most UAE British-curriculum schools, and each has a different date attached to it. Knowing which one your child is inside tells you how much of the year is still movable and how much is already fixed by a form someone has signed.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE courses carry four-digit syllabus codes: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a Second Language 0510, Business Studies 0450, Economics 0455, Computer Science 0478. Most subjects are examined across two or three written papers, and the sciences add either a practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Grading runs 9 to 1 on newer syllabuses and A* to G on others, and a single certificate can carry both scales. The code, not the subject name, is what a tutor needs to prepare correctly.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one. UAE schools do not all sit in the same zone, so two children in neighbouring emirates can face the same subject on different mornings. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre belongs to before building any IGCSE revision plan around a date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE courses use codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics, 4PH1 for Physics and 4CH1 for Chemistry. Some subjects are available in a modular pattern, where units are sat and banked across more than one series, rather than as a single terminal block. Science practical skills are examined in writing rather than in a laboratory on several specifications. Exams are available in May/June and November each year, so a child who starts late in Year 11 has a second genuine door rather than a lost year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them. The practical consequence for a UAE family is that no tutoring company should be restating Pearson dates from memory. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. We quote that because Pearson published it; for any other series we send you to qualifications.pearson.com and plan around the window your own centre confirms in writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: Lower Secondary covers the three years before the IGCSE block, and Cambridge Checkpoint tests sit at the end of it in English, Mathematics and Science. Checkpoint is not a public qualification and no university will ever see it. What it does is produce an external, comparable mark at the exact moment option choices are being made, which is why a weak Checkpoint Mathematics result and a later Core tier entry in Mathematics 0580 are so often the same story told twice.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Several UAE schools use the October window for Year 9 so that results arrive before option forms go out, and others use May so that results close the year. Which window your school uses changes when a Year 9 family should act: an October Checkpoint leaves one term to fix a gap before options, and a May Checkpoint leaves the summer. Nobody tells parents this, so ask.

programmes.name: What follows: A Level, IB Diploma or a UAE university file
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the entry currency for everything after Year 11. A sixth form will set subject-specific minimums for A Level, an IB Diploma coordinator will read the Mathematics and science grades before agreeing to a Higher Level choice, and the Ministry of Education will count accredited subjects and grades for equivalency. A Core tier entry that caps a grade in Year 10 therefore reaches forward three years, which is why tier decisions belong in the same conversation as the exam calendar.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private-school sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment and the IB at 7%. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK-curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places. A UAE family can therefore move between a British Year 11 and an IB Diploma inside the same city, and the IGCSE grades on the certificate are what makes that move possible or awkward.

igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families most often ask about by the time mocks are marked. Each entry names the code, the component that carries the marks and the specific place a grade usually leaks away. Tell us the code and the series and we match a specialist against both.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended candidates meet functions, transformations of graphs, histograms with unequal intervals and set notation that Core candidates never see. Marks leak on method shown, on premature rounding and on not reading whether an answer is wanted to three significant figures. Tier entry decides the grade ceiling, so it belongs in the autumn conversation, not the spring one.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism is where most UAE candidates lose a grade, usually because circuit reasoning is memorised rather than derived. The practical component is examined either as a practical test or as a written alternative-to-practical paper that tests apparatus description, variables and sources of error. That paper can be taught over video; a laboratory afternoon cannot, and we say so rather than pretend otherwise.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the arithmetic marks, organic chemistry carries the recall marks, and qualitative analysis carries the ones candidates assume they will remember. The reliable gain is in mark-scheme literacy: knowing that an explanation question wants a cause and a consequence, not a restated observation. Six weeks of focused past-paper work usually moves this subject more than six weeks of re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology rewards precise vocabulary and punishes paraphrase. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams are the recurring loss points, along with data questions where candidates describe a graph instead of explaining it. Extended candidates meet additional detail in genetics and in human physiology. Command terms matter here more than in any other science, because describe, explain and suggest each want a different shape of answer.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with oral endorsement
subjects.description: Reading and writing are examined alongside listening, and the speaking component is separately endorsed. The commonest loss is in the summary task, where candidates copy sentences rather than compress them, and in directed writing, where register and audience are ignored. For families newly arrived in the UAE, this is often the subject that decides whether the other eight feel manageable.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Two papers covering reading comprehension, directed writing and composition, with an optional coursework route on some centres' specifications. Marks are lost in the analysis question, where candidates list devices instead of showing effect, and in composition, where planning is skipped. This subject improves slowly and steadily, which makes it a poor candidate for a three-week rescue and a good one for a full year of weekly work.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students aiming at A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. It introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities a year early. Candidates who were comfortable in Extended often stall here because the course expects algebraic fluency rather than method recall. It is the single best preparation for the first term of a sixth form maths course.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both are case-study subjects where marks come from applying a concept to the stimulus material rather than defining it. Candidates lose evaluation marks by listing advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement. Four-mark and six-mark questions have fixed shapes, and learning those shapes is a measurable gain. Numerical questions in Economics are straightforward once candidates stop skipping them.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Computer Science splits into theory and a problem-solving paper with pseudocode and trace tables. Candidates lose marks for pseudocode that would not run and for trace tables filled in from the answer backwards. ICT carries practical components with file-handling conventions that are easy to teach and easy to fail. Both are frequently short of specialist teachers in smaller UAE schools.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: These run beside the IGCSE timetable in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education and first-language Arabic. Support here has to work inside the school's own prescribed content, because using different or additional material without prior Ministry permission is not allowed.

igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: Where you are, and what it changes about the dates
igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Your emirate decides which authority holds your child's school file, which centre they sit in and how long the school run eats into a weekday evening. It does not decide which specialist can teach them. These notes are about the first three things.

regions.name: Dubai: Jumeirah, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Dense British-curriculum belt, mostly licensed by KHDA, with school days ending between 14:30 and 15:30. Sessions from 16:30 work; 17:30 works better in exam term, after the first wave of fatigue has passed and before late homework starts.

regions.name: Dubai: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Apartment living and long lifts make an early evening slot fragile. Families here tend to want a fixed weekly time that survives travel, which suits live video better than a visiting arrangement that collapses the first week someone is away.

regions.name: Dubai: Arabian Ranches, Mudon and Dubailand
regions.note: Villa communities with longer school runs on the Al Qudra and Emirates Road corridors. A 16:00 start is unrealistic for most Year 11 students here in term time, and a 18:00 or 19:00 slot in the last ten weeks is the one that actually gets kept.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi island, Al Reem and Saadiyat
regions.note: Schools answer to ADEK rather than KHDA, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own students. That rules out the convenient option many families ask about first, which pushes the search beyond the immediate neighbourhood.

regions.name: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef
regions.note: Commutes across the bridges make a fixed after-school hour hard to protect. Weekend mornings are often the only reliable two-hour block in exam term here, and they are also the slot a specialist in another time zone can cover without friction.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with fewer British-curriculum options than the capital. Families here feel the specialist shortage most clearly in Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478, which is exactly where dropping a proximity filter pays.

regions.name: Sharjah and Ajman
regions.note: Sharjah's private schools answer to SPEA, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education instead. Two neighbouring emirates, two different files, and sometimes two different exam zones.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education there; Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain sit with the Ministry of Education. Centre choice is narrower, so confirm early where the papers will actually be sat and plan travel for the exam fortnight, not for the lessons.

schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools here enter candidates for both Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, sometimes within the same year group for different subjects. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; the names are context for the exam calendar, not a claim of any relationship.

ADEK holds these school files, and ADEK's ethics rules are the reason a capital-city family cannot simply hire the subject teacher their child already has. Mock timetables here often sit a fortnight later than in Dubai, which shifts the whole post-mock repair window.

Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah have fewer British-curriculum centres between them than Dubai has in two communities. Confirm the centre, the zone and the subject codes in writing before October, because a late correction here is expensive in a way a late correction in Dubai is not.

igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Four shapes of support, chosen by how many weeks are left rather than by preference. All four are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and all four start with a trial lesson so you can hear the teaching before committing hours.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, dated backwards from the entry deadline
modes.description: The default for a Year 10 or early Year 11 student. One session a week, with the term mapped against the school's own assessment dates and the board's deadlines, so the tier conversation happens before the entry form is signed rather than after. The first four sessions are diagnostic: we find out which topics are genuinely absent rather than merely shaky.

modes.title: The ten-week exam block
modes.description: Two sessions a week through the final stretch, built almost entirely from past papers under timed conditions. New content stops; mark-scheme technique starts. The target is the two or three topics the mocks exposed plus the question types that reliably cost marks, and the final fortnight is given to timing, question selection and the mechanical errors that turn a 6 into a 5.

modes.title: The mock-to-paper bridge
modes.description: A short diagnostic block of four to six sessions immediately after mocks are returned. Mock scripts are the best free data a family will ever get, and most of it is wasted because nobody reads the script with the student. We work through the paper question by question, separate knowledge gaps from technique gaps, and hand back a prioritised list the family can act on with or without us.

modes.title: Holiday and Checkpoint catch-up
modes.description: Short intensive runs in the winter or spring break, or in the weeks before a Checkpoint window in March, May or October. Breaks are the only time in a UAE school year when a Year 9 or Year 10 student has daytime hours and no competing homework, which makes them the cheapest place to rebuild a foundation topic properly instead of patching it.
