sections.heading: What proximity can decide about an IGCSE year, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Searching for IGCSE tuition near me produces a list sorted by distance, which is a sensible way to buy a plumber and a poor way to buy a Physics 0625 specialist. The list answers a question about convenience. The grade is decided by a different set of variables: which board, which tier, which papers, how many weeks remain and whether anyone has read the mock script. Distance appears nowhere in that set.

There are things in a UAE IGCSE year that genuinely must be local, and it is worth naming them so the proximity instinct can be satisfied where it belongs. The examination centre is the first. Your child sits the papers in a room, at a desk, with a candidate number, on a date set by the board and administered by a centre. If you are new to the country, or home-educating, or your school will not enter a particular subject, finding that centre is the most urgent local task you have, and it has a deadline months before the exam.

The second is the Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation route. That is a documents process run by the authorities, not something a tutoring company performs on your behalf, and it involves certificates, translations and in-person or official channels. The third is the clock. A tutor three time zones away who can only teach at 11pm Gulf Standard Time is useless regardless of how good they are, which is why we schedule against the UAE evening rather than against a tutor's convenience.

The tutor's address is not on the list. Once lessons are delivered over live video, the pool stops being the adults within a twenty-minute drive and becomes the people who have taught that syllabus code to that tier. For a family in Al Ain short of an Additional Mathematics 0606 teacher, or in Fujairah short of Computer Science 0478, that is not a marketing point. It is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available graduate.
bullets: Local and non-negotiable: the examination centre, the attestation route, the time zone
Local and useful: knowledge of your school's own mock and coursework dates
Not local at all: the syllabus, the mark scheme, the papers, the specialist

sections.heading: The four clocks a UAE IGCSE household is running at once
paragraphs: Most families discover too late that they are not following one calendar but four, and that the four disagree. The board's clock sets entries, exam windows and results. The school's clock sets mocks, internal coursework deadlines, forecast grades and reports. The Ministry's clock sets the mandatory subjects that must be timetabled and the equivalency documents a university file will eventually need. The family's clock holds Ramadan, Eid, the winter and spring breaks, summer travel and, often, a relocation.

The damage is almost always caused by treating the school's clock as the only one. A Year 11 family hears the mock dates in October, works towards them, and does well. What they have not seen is that the entry deadline for the series may already have passed, that the tier their child was entered for was decided by a teacher in the spring, and that the board's own deadline for forecast grades sits weeks before the first paper. By the time the mock results arrive, two of the four clocks have already stopped accepting input.

Running the four side by side is not complicated; it is just nobody's job. The practical version is a single sheet with four columns, filled in during the first week of September, with the board dates taken from cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, the school dates taken from the assessment calendar the school publishes, the Ministry items taken from the official equivalency guidance, and the family items taken from your own diary. Every tutoring decision for the next ten months reads off that sheet.

This is also the honest answer to why we build a plan before we sell hours. An hour bought in March is a different product from an hour bought in September, because the number of clocks still accepting input has fallen from four to one.

sections.heading: September to August: one UAE academic year on a single planner
paragraphs: A UAE school year for a British-curriculum student runs from late August or early September to the end of June, with a winter break around mid-December, a spring break in March or April and a long summer. Inside that frame, the board milestones arrive at a steady and predictable rhythm that almost no family is shown in advance. The planner below is the version we fill in with a Year 11 household in the first session, and the version a Year 10 household should be looking at a year earlier.

The dates in the planner are deliberately given as windows rather than as fixed days, with two exceptions where a board has published the detail. Cambridge's key dates for the March 2027 series state an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are published and can be relied on as published; everything else should be confirmed against your own centre.

What the planner makes visible is the gap between the months that feel urgent and the months that matter. October and November feel calm to a Year 11 family and are in fact the most consequential, because the Cambridge IGCSE final entry deadline and the tier decision land there. March and April feel frantic and are mostly mechanical, because by then the content is fixed and only technique is still moving. Families who shift two hours a week from April into October buy themselves a far better year for the same money.

We also mark the months where nothing should be bought. There is little value in paying for weekly sessions through the last fortnight of June once papers are finished, and little value in intensive hours during the week of Eid. Saying so costs us revenue and buys the plan credibility.

sections.heading: Counted backwards in weeks from paper one
paragraphs: The planner above is the year as the institutions see it. This is the same year as a student experiences it, counted backwards from the morning of the first paper, because that is the only number that genuinely predicts what tutoring can achieve. A family asking whether six weeks is enough is asking the right question; the answer depends entirely on what they want six weeks to do.

Twenty-four weeks out, almost everything is still open. A topic can be rebuilt from the beginning, a tier entry can still be argued with the school, and a second subject can be added without the first suffering. Sixteen weeks out, the content is still movable but the tier usually is not, and the sensible plan narrows to the topics that carry the most marks. Ten weeks out, the syllabus is fixed and the work becomes almost entirely technique: timed papers, mark-scheme literacy and the two or three topics the mocks exposed.

Six weeks out, the honest conversation is about triage. There is time to fix a pattern of mechanical errors, to drill one weak topic properly, and to rehearse the paper under timed conditions four or five times. There is not time to learn a year of organic chemistry. Three weeks out, nothing new should be taught at all; the gain available is in question selection, timing and not losing marks already earned. One week out, the useful intervention is sleep, a paper rotation and somebody calm to ask questions to.
Telling a family that six weeks will not deliver a transformation is the part of this job that loses sales. It is also the only way the remaining six weeks get spent on something that works.

sections.heading: Three assessment windows a year, and the Checkpoint tests nobody mentions
paragraphs: A family who believes there is one IGCSE exam series a year will plan for a cliff edge. There is more than one door. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and publishes key dates for a March series used by some zones. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and in November each year. That is three realistic windows for most subjects.

The consequence is that a late start is not automatically a lost year. A child who arrives in the UAE in January, or who was moved onto the wrong tier, or who was ill through a June series, has a November route. Some Pearson specifications are modular, with units sat and banked across more than one series, which spreads the load rather than concentrating it. None of this is secret, and none of it appears on any competitor page we have read.

Checkpoint deserves its own mention because it is the most misunderstood assessment in a British-curriculum UAE school. It is not a public qualification. No university will see it. What it provides is an external mark at the precise moment Year 9 option forms and tier expectations are being formed, and it is therefore the cheapest early-warning system a family has. A Checkpoint Mathematics result in the lower bands in October and a Core tier entry in Mathematics 0580 fourteen months later are usually the same problem, caught once and then ignored.

The practical instruction is short. Ask your school, in writing, which board, which series and which Checkpoint window applies to your child, and ask which of the six Cambridge administrative zones your centre sits in. Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: Results, remarks and retakes: the fortnight that decides the next year
paragraphs: Results day is treated as the end of the process and is actually the start of a short, crowded window in which three separate decisions have to be made. Whether to request a review of marking. Whether to enter a retake, and for which series. Whether the grades as they stand are enough for the sixth form place, the IB Diploma subject choices and the eventual Ministry of Education equivalency file. Each has its own deadline, and the deadlines are days apart rather than months.

The published dates give a family a reliable shape to plan against. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results for the June 2026 series went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's key dates for the March 2027 series put results on Direct on 13 May with certificates in late June. Read against a school year that restarts in late August, that means a June-series family gets roughly one week between the grade and the first day of sixth form.

The practical move is to decide the decision rules before the grades arrive. Write down, in July, what grade in which subject would trigger a remark request, what would trigger a November retake, and what would require a conversation with the sixth form about a changed subject. Families who do this act within the window. Families who do not spend the window arguing about whether to act, and the window closes.

A retake is a teaching problem as well as an administrative one. A November entry after a June result leaves a short, well-defined block of weeks, which is exactly the kind of work live one-to-one sessions do well: the content is known, the gap is diagnosable from the original paper, and the target is a specific grade boundary rather than a general improvement.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs when you buy it late
paragraphs: Every page in this market quotes an hourly rate and stops. The hourly rate is the least interesting number available, because the thing a family actually pays is the rate multiplied by however many teaching weeks are left when they finally start. A household that begins in September and a household that begins in April can pay the same per hour and get completely different years, and the second one usually pays more per grade.

Market rates in the UAE, as published by the providers themselves and by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, run roughly as follows. Budget online and university-student tutors sit between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150. A visiting tutor in the home, travel included, runs roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350. IGCSE, IB and A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are other companies' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list.

The table below does the arithmetic nobody publishes. It uses a single mid-market figure of AED 200 an hour purely as a constant, so the only variable is the start month, and it counts teaching weeks rather than calendar weeks, excluding the winter and spring breaks and the week of Eid. The point is not the total. The point is that the September household buys thirty-four teaching weeks of gradual work for roughly what the March household pays for eleven weeks of triage, and that an IGCSE tuition cost in AED is a function of the date on which you decide.

For our own hours we publish no rate card on this page. The sequence is a free trial lesson, then a plan with a stated number of sessions against the weeks remaining, then a figure. That order exists because a quote given before anybody has seen the mock script is a guess.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one when the date cannot move
paragraphs: This page targets a phrase about proximity, so the comparison deserves a straight answer rather than a dodge. A tutor sitting at the kitchen table has real advantages. Younger children concentrate better with an adult physically present. Equipment can be shared. A parent can overhear the session. For a Year 7 or Year 8 student with no exam pressure, those advantages are worth paying the travel premium for, and the UAE market charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for it.

What changes the calculation is a fixed date. Once a paper is scheduled and the weeks are finite, the governing variable becomes reliability. A visiting arrangement carries travel risk twice a week: Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00, a school run that overran, rain, a tutor whose other client in another community ran late. Each cancelled session in a ten-week block is ten per cent of the plan, and it cannot be re-run because the paper does not move. A video session carries no travel risk and can be rescheduled to a Saturday morning rather than lost.

The second change is the size of the pool. A proximity search in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain returns the adults who live there. A search without it returns people who have taught Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 to the tier your child is entered for. IB Gram does not place tutors at UAE addresses at all; tuition for families in the Emirates is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits are offered only in India. We would rather say that in plain words than take a booking we cannot honour.

The table sets the two models against each other on the things that actually differ. Several rows favour the visiting tutor. Publishing those rows is the point; a comparison in which one column wins every line is an advertisement, not a comparison.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the term breaks that sit inside a revision block
paragraphs: A UAE revision plan drawn on a blank grid will be wrong by three or four weeks, because the grid does not know about Ramadan, Eid, the winter break, the spring break or the family trip someone booked in February. Those weeks are not lost by accident. They are lost because nobody counted them when the plan was written, so the plan quietly assumed teaching weeks that never existed.

Ramadan changes the shape of a day rather than cancelling it. School hours shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and the usable study window moves to the hours after Iftar. For a Year 11 student with a June series, this matters enormously in some years and barely at all in others, depending on where Ramadan falls relative to mocks and papers. The workable answer is to keep the same number of weekly sessions but move them later, treat the afternoon as unusable, and accept that the week of Eid produces nothing and should not be paid for.

The two school breaks are the opposite problem: they are genuinely useful and almost always wasted. A winter or spring break gives a Year 9 or Year 10 student daytime hours with no competing homework, which is the only realistic time to rebuild a foundation topic from the beginning rather than patch it. Three sessions a week for two weeks in December, spent properly on one topic, outperforms twelve scattered sessions in April. The same logic applies before a Checkpoint window in March, May or October.

Alongside all of this, the Ministry-mandated subjects keep their own weekly claim on the timetable. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are not optional extras a family can quietly drop during exam term to make room for IGCSE revision, and a plan that assumes otherwise will collide with the school in March.
bullets: Count teaching weeks, not calendar weeks, before agreeing a number of sessions

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file, opened before results day
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns an IGCSE certificate into a document a UAE university file can use, and it is the one almost every tutoring page in this market ignores entirely. It is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring company performs or guarantees, and the only sensible position for us is to describe the requirements accurately, cite the source and point you to the official channel.

For the British track, the Ministry's clarification reported in July 2026 sets out that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. That last detail matters: one ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published requirement.

The American track is specified differently, with English proficiency shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold in that reporting, and this page will not invent one; check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly before relying on any figure you read anywhere.

The timing point is the reason this section sits on a calendar page. A June-series family receives grades in August and often needs a university or sixth form file within days. Certificates, translations and attestation take time that does not exist in that week. The document trail should be started in Year 11, in parallel with revision, so that results day is a matter of adding one more page to a file that already exists. Tutoring is not required for any of this, and nobody should tell you it is.

sections.heading: Who regulates the school, who permits the tutor, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Two separate permissions sit behind an IGCSE year in the UAE, and parents routinely merge them. The first governs the school. Private schools in Dubai answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education there and the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge does the same, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The second governs the individual giving the lesson. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, the official service page lists a two-working-day completion time and an application route through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you, including by us.

One consequence catches families off guard. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. The teacher who already knows your child is often the one person who may not take the work. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of its own to advertise: we are an independent tutor-matching platform, with no approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and any company telling you otherwise is describing something it cannot show you.

The academic-honesty line is just as clear. A tutor teaches, explains, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not supply sentences for a coursework portfolio, does not hand over a finished piece, and does not sit beside a student typing an answer for them. Work submitted for assessment has to be the student's own, and a provider offering anything else is selling a malpractice risk that lands on the child rather than on the seller. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference the official sources and send you to them.

process.title: Send three things, not a paragraph
process.description: The board, the syllabus codes and the number of weeks to the first paper. Add the school's assessment calendar if you have it and the last mock script if one exists. Those five items let us match a specialist and draft a realistic session count the same day, instead of trading messages about availability.

process.title: We check the calendar before we check availability
process.description: We count teaching weeks rather than calendar weeks, subtract the breaks and Eid, and tell you what that number of weeks can and cannot achieve for the subject you have named. If the honest answer is that the hours will not deliver what you are hoping for, you hear that before you are asked for anything.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One session with the tutor who would actually teach your child, not a sales call and not a different tutor. The trial is free with no card required and no obligation to continue. You will get a short written note afterwards naming what the tutor found and what the first four sessions would target.

process.title: A written plan against the dates, then a figure
process.description: A session count mapped to the weeks remaining, the topics ranked by marks available, and the point in the plan where new teaching stops and technique starts. The price comes after that plan exists, because a number quoted before anyone has seen the work is guesswork dressed as a quote.

process.title: Weekly notes, and a stop point we tell you about
process.description: A short note after each session recording what was covered, what was set and what the error log now shows. We also name the week at which further hours stop being useful, usually once a subject's last paper is sat. Saying so costs us sessions and keeps the plan honest.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built backwards, not forwards
whyPoints.description: Most tuition starts at lesson one and works forwards through a syllabus, which is how families arrive at April with three topics uncovered. We start at the morning of the first paper and work back in weeks, so what gets taught in October is chosen by what has to be true in May.

whyPoints.title: Matched on a syllabus code, not a postcode
whyPoints.description: Tell us Physics 0625 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher and we match someone who has taught that specification to that tier. Dropping the distance filter is what makes a specialist available to a family in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain on the same terms as a family in Jumeirah.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the Emirates; home visits are offered only in India. You will not find a sentence on this site promising a visit we cannot make.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED range on this page is attributed to the company or rate table that published it, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price. Where a date or a threshold is not confirmed by a primary source, we say so instead of filling the gap.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody supplies sentences for a portfolio or hands over a finished piece, and we do not distribute board papers or mark schemes. That boundary protects your child's entry, which is the thing actually at stake.

whyPoints.title: An independent platform, with nothing borrowed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, we run no UAE centre, and we name schools only as context for the exam calendar.

faqs.question: Searching for IGCSE tuition near me — does where the tutor sits change anything but the clock?
faqs.answer: It changes the time the lesson can start and almost nothing else. Three things in a UAE IGCSE year genuinely have to be local: the examination centre your child walks into, the Ministry attestation route, and the lesson time, which has to fit a UAE evening in Gulf Standard Time. The syllabus, the papers, the mark schemes and the specialist are not local to anything. Keeping a distance filter means choosing from the adults near your community; dropping it means choosing from people who have taught your child's exact syllabus code at the right tier. For a Year 11 student with a fixed paper date, that is the trade worth making.

faqs.question: What are the four separate calendars an IGCSE family in the UAE has to track at once?
faqs.answer: The board's calendar sets final entries, the tier, the exam window and results. The school's calendar sets mocks, internal coursework deadlines, forecast grades and reports. The Ministry's calendar covers the mandatory UAE subjects and the equivalency documents a university file eventually needs. Your own calendar holds Ramadan, Eid, the winter and spring breaks and any travel. Most families follow only the school's, which is why they discover in January that the entry deadline and the tier decision passed in the autumn. Put all four in one sheet in September, with board dates taken from the board's own site, and every later decision reads off it.

faqs.question: Which month should we start if the papers are in June?
faqs.answer: September, if the aim is a grade change rather than damage limitation. Counting teaching weeks rather than calendar weeks, a September start gives about thirty-four usable weeks once the winter break, spring break and Eid are removed. November gives about twenty-six, January about nineteen, March about eleven. The hourly rate does not change, so the total hours bought and the kind of work possible are what differ. September hours can rebuild a topic from the beginning and can still influence the tier entry. March hours can fix technique and drill one weak area. Both are worth buying; they are not the same purchase.

faqs.question: How many teaching weeks are actually left between January and a June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. From early January to the start of a June series there are roughly twenty-two calendar weeks, but the spring break removes two, Eid usually removes one, mock season absorbs one or two in which no new work lands, and study leave removes the final stretch of normal routine. The honest figure most UAE families should plan against is about nineteen usable weeks, which is nineteen sessions at one a week. Working from the real number changes the plan: it forces topics to be ranked by marks available rather than covered in syllabus order.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge Checkpoint test, and does it have anything to do with IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Checkpoint tests sit at the end of Cambridge Lower Secondary in English, Mathematics and Science, and Cambridge runs them in March, May and October. They are not a public qualification and no university will ever see the result. Their value is timing: they produce an external, comparable mark at the exact point Year 9 option forms and tier expectations are being formed. A weak Checkpoint Mathematics result and a Core tier entry in Mathematics 0580 fourteen months later are very often the same problem, spotted once and then left. Ask your school which window it uses, because October and May imply different windows for acting.

faqs.question: Our school runs mocks in January. Should the hours aim at the mocks or at the real papers?
faqs.answer: At the real papers, using the mocks as the best free diagnostic you will get. Treat mock season as data collection rather than as the target. The mark matters less than the script: which questions were skipped, where method marks were lost, which command terms were misread, whether the paper was mistimed. Sitting with the student and reading the script question by question separates knowledge gaps from technique gaps, and those need different work. Families who chase the mock grade often peak in January. Families who mine the mock script make February and March count instead.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results actually reach a student in the UAE?
faqs.answer: For the June 2026 series, Pearson sent results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. For the November 2025 series, results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read against a UAE school year that restarts in late August, a June-series family gets roughly one week between the grade and the first day of sixth form, which is why remark and retake decision rules should be written down in July rather than argued about in that week. Confirm your own series with your centre, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them.

faqs.question: If we begin in April for a June series, how many hours is that in practice?
faqs.answer: About six usable weeks, so six sessions at one a week or twelve at two a week, before study leave changes the routine. That is enough to fix a pattern of mechanical errors, drill one genuinely weak topic, and rehearse the paper under timed conditions four or five times. It is not enough to learn a year of organic chemistry or to repair algebraic fluency. The useful conversation at this point is triage: which topics carry the most available marks, and which question types reliably cost marks. A provider who promises a transformation from six weeks is selling you the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Where will my child physically sit the IGCSE papers if we have just moved here?
faqs.answer: At a registered examination centre, which is normally the school once your child is enrolled and entered. If you arrive mid-year, if the school will not enter a particular subject, or if your child is home-educated, you need to find a centre that accepts private candidates and you need to do it before the entry deadline rather than before the exam. Ask the centre which of the six Cambridge administrative zones it belongs to, because Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one.

faqs.question: Does booking two subjects in the same week halve the attention each one gets?
faqs.answer: Not if there are enough weeks left, and yes if there are not. With twenty or more teaching weeks remaining, two subjects at one session each works well, because the gaps between sessions are where consolidation happens anyway. Inside ten weeks, two subjects in parallel tends to produce two half-finished plans. The better move late on is to sequence: give one subject two sessions a week for four weeks, then switch. Which subject goes first should be decided by marks available and by which paper falls earlier in the timetable, not by which one feels worse.

faqs.question: Eid falls inside our revision block. How many sessions does that actually cost us?
faqs.answer: Usually one full week, occasionally two around the longer holiday, and families should plan for it rather than pay for it. Ramadan is a different question: it changes the shape of a day instead of cancelling it. School hours shorten, afternoons are unusable for serious work, and the real study window moves to the hours after Iftar. The workable approach is to keep the same number of weekly sessions and move them later in the evening, write off the week of Eid entirely, and count the remaining teaching weeks honestly before agreeing a session total with anyone.

faqs.question: Our daughter has a school coursework deadline before any board date. Which one should the plan follow?
faqs.answer: The school's, because the school's deadline is the one that actually binds her. Internal deadlines for coursework, portfolios and controlled assessments are set by the school, usually weeks or months before the board needs anything, and missing one has immediate consequences for her grade. A plan should carry both clocks: the school's internal dates and the board's entry and exam dates. On the coursework itself, a tutor's role is to teach the skills, question the approach and give feedback on what she has produced. The piece submitted has to be her own work.

faqs.question: Is there any point paying for sessions during the winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: The breaks are the most underused weeks in a UAE school year. They give a Year 9 or Year 10 student daytime hours with no competing homework, which is the only realistic window for rebuilding a foundation topic from the beginning rather than patching it. Three sessions a week for two weeks in December, all spent on one topic, tends to outperform twelve scattered sessions in April. For a Year 11 student in the spring break, the same hours are better used on timed papers than on new content. The break before a Checkpoint window is similarly well spent.

faqs.question: What should already be finished by the time the school asks for forecast grades?
faqs.answer: Enough timed work for the forecast to be based on evidence rather than on impression. Cambridge's key dates for the March 2027 series put forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, and other series have their own equivalent. By that point a student should have sat at least two full papers under timed conditions, have a visible error log, and have covered the high-mark topics even if the last few remain thin. Forecast grades can matter for sixth form conversations and for university applications made before results, so the work that informs them should be done rather than promised.

faqs.question: After results arrive, how long do we have to decide on a retake?
faqs.answer: Days rather than weeks, which is why the decision rules should be written down beforehand. A June-series family receives grades in the second half of August, with a school year restarting in late August, and has to weigh a review of marking, a November entry and the sixth form place almost simultaneously. Write down in July what grade in which subject would trigger a remark request, what would trigger a November retake, and what would need a conversation about changed subjects. A November retake is also a clean teaching job: the content is known and the gap is diagnosable from the original paper.

faqs.question: Do we need someone in our own emirate for the Ministry of Education equivalency appointment?
faqs.answer: Equivalency and attestation run through the Ministry and the authority holding your school's file, so that part of the process is genuinely local and genuinely yours. No tutoring company performs it for you, and none should imply it can. What a family can do is start early: certificates, transcripts and translations take time that does not exist in the week after results. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: How late is too late to book IGCSE tuition before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Three weeks before a paper, almost nothing new should be taught, and inside the final week the useful intervention is sleep, a paper rotation and somebody calm to ask questions to. That does not make the hours worthless; it changes what they are for. Late sessions should work on timing, question selection and the mechanical errors that lose marks already earned. What late hours cannot do is cover absent content, and any provider who says otherwise is taking your money for a result the calendar will not allow. We will tell you when the honest answer is to stop buying hours.

faqs.question: Our son is in Year 9. Is it absurd to start IGCSE tuition this early?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest year to buy. Year 9 is when option forms are completed, when Checkpoint results arrive in the March, May or October windows, and when the foundation topics that later cap a tier entry are still fixable without exam pressure. Work done now is unhurried, costs the same per hour, and can change the tier a child is eventually entered for, which reaches forward to A Level and IB Diploma choices and to the Ministry equivalency count. An IGCSE tutor for Year 11 is usually buying time back. A tutor in Year 9 is buying options.

igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the date, then the subject, then the tutor

intro.heading: The system an IGCSE family in the UAE is actually working inside
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in the UAE is being hired into a school system that no single authority runs. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah has its own Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has a Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education. Which body inspects the school writing your child's reports changes what you should be asking a tutor for.

Underneath the regulator sits a second split most parents only meet in Year 10. Two boards dominate British-curriculum schools here. Cambridge International gives its syllabuses four-digit codes — Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes that look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. They are not interchangeable. The papers are numbered differently, the tiering works differently, and practical science is handled differently. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor who has never opened a 4MA1 paper will teach the right mathematics and prepare a child for the wrong examination.

Then there is tiering. IGCSE Core and Extended are two routes through one subject, and the route a school enters a child for sets the highest grade that child can be awarded. A Core entry in mathematics caps the outcome; an Extended entry opens the top grades and carries content a Core set was never taught. Entries are submitted by the school's examinations officer months before the papers are sat, so a tutor who starts in February can change how a paper is answered but not which paper arrives on the desk.

At the end of Year 11 the federal rules take over. For the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That is the published rule as reported in Gulf Today's July 2026 summary of the ministry's clarification. One page currently ranking for this search tells UAE parents they need six subjects; the sourced figure is five.

This page covers that ground in order: the regulator map, the two boards, the tier decision, where marks actually go missing, what the market charges in AED, how a school year runs backwards from an examination series, equivalency, the mandatory UAE subjects, the permit question and the honesty line around coursework. Tuition from IB Gram is delivered as online IGCSE tuition — one-to-one, over live video, booked in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits belong to our India service only; no lesson arranged here involves a journey to a UAE address.

igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE tutor here is usually asked for at one of three moments: when Year 9 Checkpoint results suggest a set is wrong, when Year 10 tiering is being decided, or when Year 11 mock papers come back lower than the predicted grade. The three programmes below are the ones those moments sit inside, with what each means in a UAE school.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE as a two-year course examined in a June series and a November series, with each subject carrying a four-digit syllabus code. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500. Most subjects offer a Core and an Extended route, assessed through different papers rather than different questions on the same paper. Grades are reported on the A* to G scale in some subjects and 9 to 1 in others, depending on the syllabus a school enters.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance for exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. UAE centres are not all in the same zone as the UK, so a timetable copied from a British school website is the wrong document.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE covers the same ground with a different architecture. Codes run 4MA1 for mathematics, 4PH1 for physics, 4CH1 for chemistry, 4BI1 for biology, 4EA1 for English language. Mathematics is tiered as Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and several science subjects assess practical skills entirely through written papers. Examinations are available in a May or June series and in a November series each year, so a resit does not always mean waiting a full year.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 Pearson International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, so a UAE family planning around a date should read the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site rather than a figure restated on a tuition page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint
programmes.description: Checkpoint tests sit before IGCSE and are available in March, May and October. They are not a qualification and they do not appear on a certificate, but in many UAE schools they are the evidence used to allocate Year 10 sets, and set allocation is what decides tiering. A Checkpoint report that shows weak algebraic manipulation or weak extended writing is the earliest honest warning a parent gets about the grade ceiling two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Because Year 9 Checkpoint outcomes often feed the Core or Extended decision in UAE schools, the cheapest tuition a family ever buys is the term before that decision rather than the term before the examination. A child moved into an Extended set in Year 10 has two years of teaching ahead; a child moved up in Year 11 is trying to cover unseen content while revising everything else.

igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families most often ask about, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes side by side so you can match a request to what the school has actually entered. Where a subject is tiered, the tier matters more than the number of hours booked.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most requested IGCSE subject here. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended papers; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Marks are lost in the same two places either way: algebraic manipulation that was never secured in Year 9, and multi-step problems where the method mark is available but the working is not shown clearly enough to earn it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the equations of motion carry most of the lost marks. Extended papers add quantitative work that Core sets simply do not meet. Practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper at most centres rather than a laboratory examination, which rewards precision about apparatus diagrams, tables and anomalous readings.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are where Extended candidates separate from Core, and where a tutor earns their hour. Organic chemistry and the qualitative-analysis tables are memorisation with structure, and the most common avoidable loss is stating an observation without naming the substance responsible for it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology reads as the accessible science and marks like the most exacting. Command terms decide the grade: describe, explain and suggest want different answers from the same recall. Transport in plants, genetics and homeostasis generate the most queries from UAE schools, usually because the topic was taught before the examination technique was.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 · 0653)
subjects.description: Many UAE schools route non-specialists through Co-ordinated Sciences for a double award or Combined Science for a single one. Content is reduced rather than easier, and the squeeze falls on physics. Families often discover in Year 11 that a double award closes the door on a science A Level, which is a conversation worth having in Year 10.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with and without oral endorsement
subjects.description: A very large share of UAE candidates sit ESL rather than First Language English. The reading paper rewards exact lifting and reshaping of information; the writing paper rewards register. The oral component is endorsed separately in 0510 and counted in 0511, and knowing which the school entered changes what practice is useful.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition paper reward control of structure over vocabulary display. The reading passages carry a summary task where most marks are lost to copying rather than to comprehension. Children who moved from an American or Indian curriculum mid-school usually need the examination's conventions taught, not the language.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
subjects.description: Both subjects reward data response and evaluation in a form students rarely practise on their own. Diagram accuracy in economics and the application of a case study in business studies are the two repeat failures. A tutor's job here is largely to teach the mark scheme's hierarchy: knowledge, application, analysis, evaluation.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 · 0417)
subjects.description: Computer Science theory papers ask for precise definitions and trace tables; the pseudocode questions are where marks disappear. ICT is practical-heavy and depends on software versions the school uses, so useful tuition here follows the school's own task brief rather than a generic course.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 first language · 0544 foreign language)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Arabic runs on two separate routes in UAE schools, and children are placed by first language rather than by ability. The grammar and composition demands of the first-language route are considerably heavier. This is also the subject where school-provided teaching and private tuition overlap most, so it is worth checking what the timetable already gives you.

igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The board a school enters and the body that inspects it both vary by emirate, and so does the number of British-curriculum schools within reach. These notes are about what changes for a family in each place, not about who happens to live there.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The largest British-curriculum market in the country: 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with 37% of enrolment on a UK curriculum. KHDA licenses and inspects them, publishes a KHDA inspection rating for each, and confirmed in May 2026 that fees would not rise for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK school licensing and accreditation covers the capital's private schools, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. For a parent, that rules out the convenient arrangement and makes an outside specialist the correct route rather than a second-best one.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator means a school cannot quietly swap an IGCSE syllabus mid-course, which is useful to know before assuming a change is possible.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain's private schools fall under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi island. The British-curriculum cohort is smaller, which in practice means fewer local Extended physics and Extended chemistry specialists competing for the same evening slots. Live video closes that gap without adding a commute to either side of the lesson.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Schools here are supervised directly by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so inspection reporting and fee approval follow the federal route. IGCSE provision exists but is thinner, and families frequently commute into Sharjah or Dubai for a school, which compresses what is left of a weekday evening.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in that emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods; Fujairah sits under the Ministry of Education. Both returned almost no coverage in the UAE tutoring search results we examined, which is a gap in the market rather than an absence of IGCSE candidates.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's British-curriculum schools run both boards, sometimes within one school: Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics is a common combination. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places, four of them UK curriculum, so set sizes and specialist availability are both moving.

The capital's British-curriculum cohort is concentrated in a smaller number of larger schools, and ADEK's ethics rules mean the school's own teachers cannot take on enrolled students privately. Families here ask most often for Extended sciences and for First Language English support after an international move.

Fewer British-curriculum schools means fewer parallel sets, so a child who is wrongly tiered has less room to be moved internally. That makes the Year 10 tier conversation more consequential here than it is in Dubai, and it is the conversation we have first with northern-emirates families.

igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families use an IGCSE tutor here, all delivered as live one-to-one video. The right one depends on how much of the two-year course is still ahead and whether the entry has already been submitted.

modes.description: One subject, one hour a week, taught in syllabus order alongside the school's scheme of work. This is the format that can still change a tier, because it starts while the entry decision is open. The tutor works from the official syllabus published on the board's own site and from the papers the school has already marked and returned.

Tuition here supports what the school teaches rather than replacing it, because the content for these subjects cannot be varied without prior permission from the Ministry of Education.

sections.heading: Who licenses your child's IGCSE school, and why that comes before choosing a tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are licensed and inspected by five different bodies, not one. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education plays a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The difference is not administrative trivia. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator has a say in what a school may teach and how it may assess. In Dubai and Abu Dhabi the emphasis falls more heavily on licensing and inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why the mandatory UAE subjects appear on an IGCSE timetable at all.

None of these bodies chooses your child's examination board, and none of them approves individual tutors. A school decides whether to enter Cambridge or Pearson papers. A tutor's right to teach privately comes from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, not from an education regulator. Any provider telling you its tutors carry regulator approval is describing something that does not exist in that form, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit — the thing a training institute with premises in Dubai actually holds — is not a credential attached to a person.

What the regulator does give you is evidence. A KHDA inspection rating, or its ADEK equivalent, is published and readable, and the subject-level attainment and progress judgements inside a report are far more useful than the headline band when you are deciding whether to buy hours.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the question to settle before the first lesson
paragraphs: Ask a UAE school's examinations officer for the syllabus codes your child is entered for, and the whole tuition plan sharpens. Cambridge International codes are four digits: 0580 mathematics, 0625 physics, 0620 chemistry, 0610 biology, 0500 First Language English, 0510 or 0511 English as a Second Language. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes are alphanumeric: 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1. The textbook cover usually shows one or the other, and report cards often carry the code in small print.

The two boards cover similar content and assess it differently. Cambridge tiers most subjects as Core and Extended with separate papers for each route. Pearson tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher and leaves several other subjects untiered. Cambridge offers a June and a November series; Pearson offers May or June and November. Practical science is assessed in both through written papers at most centres, but the paper structure, the mark allocation and the phrasing of the questions differ enough that practising the wrong board's paper wastes the hour.

This matters most in mixed schools. Plenty of UAE schools run Cambridge sciences and Pearson mathematics, or move a cohort from one board to another between year groups for timetable reasons. A tutor matched on subject alone can be four weeks into a plan before anybody notices the paper numbers do not match. We ask for the codes at the enquiry stage for that reason, and a Cambridge IGCSE tutor is matched to Cambridge entries rather than to the subject label.

Neither board publishes its papers for free redistribution, and no tuition provider should be sending you mark schemes or past papers as a download. Both publish their syllabuses openly on their own sites. That is the document a tutor should be working from, alongside the work the school has already marked.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: a Year 10 decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: IGCSE Core and Extended is the most consequential thing on this page and the least discussed by the pages competing for this search. A Core entry restricts the grades available. An Extended entry opens the top of the scale and brings content that Core sets are not taught. The school decides, usually on set placement, and the entry is submitted by the examinations officer long before the papers are sat.

In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 the practical consequence is clear. A Core candidate sits papers built for the Core content list; an Extended candidate sits papers that assume the additional topics. Moving a child up in Year 11 means covering unseen material while revising everything else, which is why the honest answer to a December request is sometimes that the tier should have been argued in March. Moving a child down is easier administratively and much harder to reverse later, because an A Level or an IB higher level will ask what the IGCSE actually covered.

A tutor's leverage over this is real but bounded. Before the final entry deadline, a tutor can produce evidence a head of department will take seriously: marked work on Extended questions, a mock paper sat under timed conditions, a written note on what content remains. After the deadline, amendments sit with the centre and the board, may carry a charge and may be refused. What a tutor can still do is make sure every mark available on the entered paper is actually earned, which on a Core paper often means the difference between the middle and the top of the available range.

The question to ask the school, in writing, is simple: which tier is my child currently expected to be entered for, and what would change that? Everything else in a tuition plan follows from the answer.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost in UAE classrooms
paragraphs: Across the subjects UAE families ask about most, the losses cluster in a small number of places, and almost none of them are about intelligence. The commonest is command-term blindness: a student who can describe a process writes a description when the paper asked them to explain it, and earns nothing. The second is working that exists in the student's head rather than on the page, which forfeits method marks that were available regardless of the final answer. The third is time, spent generously on question one and not at all on question eleven.

Subject patterns repeat too. In physics, electricity and moments; in chemistry, moles and the gap between an observation and the substance that caused it; in biology, the three-way distinction between describe, explain and suggest; in mathematics, algebraic manipulation that was never secured in Year 9 and quietly undermines everything after it. In English, the summary task, where copying from the passage caps the mark no matter how accurate the copying is.

There is a UAE-specific pattern as well. Many children here arrive mid-school from an Indian, American or national curriculum, and they are frequently strong in content and unfamiliar with the examination's conventions. A child who can do the chemistry but has never seen how a Cambridge paper allocates marks is not a weak chemist; they are an unpractised candidate. That is a fixable problem and it usually takes fewer hours than parents expect.

A first session that diagnoses which of these is actually happening is worth more than six sessions of general revision, and it is the reason a tutor should be asking to see marked work before quoting a plan.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in the UAE, and what sets the number
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. The IGCSE tuition rates in AED below come from a survey of published UAE provider rates and a Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026. They are market figures and they are presented as the market: they are not an IB Gram price list, and we do not quote a rate before a tutor has been matched to a named subject and tier.

What moves the number is specialism rather than seniority. An hour of general maths help and an hour from someone who teaches Extended 0580 every week are different products, and the second costs roughly twice the first across every provider surveyed. An in-home visit adds the travel to the bill whether the provider itemises it or not, which is most of the gap between the online and in-home bands. Group sessions reduce the hourly figure per student and remove the thing most families are buying, which is a tutor who stops on the exact step a child cannot do.

Worth setting against this: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For families who had budgeted for a fee rise, that is the year to spend on the subject that is actually failing rather than on a broad package. Monthly figures seen in the market run from roughly AED 240 to AED 600 for a weekly budget session and AED 1,000 to above AED 2,000 for specialist examination-year support, with online packages advertised from around AED 799 a month.
Our own position is deliberately boring: a trial lesson at no charge, one per family, booked once a tutor has been matched, and a rate confirmed in writing before any paid lesson is scheduled.

sections.heading: An in-home IGCSE tutor compared with one-to-one online
paragraphs: Searching for a home tutor is a reasonable thing for a UAE parent to do, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home tuition in this market means a tutor who lives within a sensible drive of your community, arrives at a fixed hour, works at the kitchen table and bills the travel into the rate. That has real advantages: a younger child sits still better with someone in the room, and a parent can hear what is happening.

It has two structural costs. The first is the tutor pool, which shrinks to whoever is both free and nearby — and for Extended chemistry, Pearson 4PH1 or First Language English, nearby may be nobody. The second is the clock. A 16:00 finish, a school run and Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:30 means a 17:00 session starts at 17:20 and ends when the tutor has to leave for the next family, and the first casualty is the ten minutes at the end where the student explains the method back.

IB Gram resolves this one way: lessons are one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our India service and are not offered anywhere in the Emirates, which we would rather state here than have you discover at the booking stage. What that buys is a specialist matched on board and tier rather than on postcode, a recording or written notes after each session, and a slot that does not move because of traffic.

For a Year 11 eight weeks out from a series, that last point is usually decisive. Twelve sessions that all happen beat sixteen booked of which four were lost to a school event, a cancelled drive and Ramadan timings.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from an examination series
paragraphs: Nobody in this search result counts the year backwards, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can be shown. An examination series is not one date; it is a sequence of deadlines set by the board and administered by the school, and the ones that constrain a family fall months before the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series make the point cleanly: examinations run 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries are due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Read that sequence in reverse and the tuition plan writes itself. If an entry closes in late November, any argument about tier has to be made with evidence by October. If forecast grades are submitted in February, the mock results that produce them matter more than most students realise, because those grades travel to universities. If the papers begin in early February, the intensive block belongs in November and December, not in January.

The IGCSE November series works the same way at a different offset. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results having reached students on 22 January 2026 — so a child resitting in November has a result in hand in January rather than waiting for an August series. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

One caution that is not in anybody else's calendar. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone the centre is in, and read that timetable rather than a British school's.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the five-subject rule behind a UAE university file
paragraphs: For a child who will apply to a UAE university, the IGCSE certificate has a second audience: the federal Ministry of Education, through the equivalency and attestation process. The British-track requirement, as set out in Gulf Today's July 2026 report on the ministry's clarification, is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details catch families out. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a child counting them towards the total can be a subject short without knowing it. And the figure is five, not six. A page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE searches states that candidates here must take six subjects; the sourced clarification says five. The American track is specified differently again, asking for a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, plus at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB Diploma there is no figure on this page, deliberately. We have not read a points threshold for IB equivalency on the ministry's own site, and publishing an unverified number that a family plans around would be worse than publishing nothing. Check it against moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly.

Ministry of Education equivalency is a process a family completes with the authority, not something a tutoring provider performs, charges for or guarantees. Nor is tuition a requirement for it. What tuition can do is make sure the five subjects clear the grade floor comfortably, and that is a planning conversation for Year 10, not for results week.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Almost no page competing for this search mentions the mandatory UAE subjects, and every IGCSE family here lives with them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidelines state that its requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies.

How they are taught is prescribed in more detail than parents usually realise. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught primarily in Arabic for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

There are two further constraints a tutor has to respect. Schools are required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. In practice that means useful tuition here follows the school's own material and the ministry's content rather than importing a parallel course, and a tutor who offers you a bespoke Arabic syllabus has misunderstood the rules.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. That is the timetable your IGCSE revision has to fit around.

sections.heading: Is the IGCSE tutor you are about to hire permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and exactly one competitor in the pages we examined mentions it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published: Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating online as a fixed amount should not be relied on. The honest position is that the permit is required, it costs nothing, and anyone treating it as optional is telling you something about how they operate.

Two distinctions matter. A permit belongs to an individual; a KHDA Educational Services Permit belongs to a training institute with premises in Dubai and involves initial approval, a window of up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. They are different documents and neither makes anybody's tutors regulator-approved. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction, so the convenient arrangement with your child's own teacher is the one to decline.

IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge accreditation, and claims none. We are an independent matching service, we ask tutors for their permit, and you are entitled to ask to see it before a first paid lesson.

sections.heading: Coursework, papers and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: One page ranking in this space sells completed Internal Assessments. That is worth naming as the thing to walk away from, because the student carries the consequence. Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework or a controlled assessment, the school has to authenticate it as the candidate's own work, and a piece that arrives polished beyond anything the student produces in class is a problem for the student long before it is a problem for anyone else.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, model a technique on a different example, ask questions about a draft the student has written, and point at a paragraph that does not answer the question. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft into their own prose, or hand back a finished piece. If a provider offers to take a project from draft to submission, the correct response is to end the conversation.

The same discipline applies to materials. Board syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and a tuition provider has no business redistributing them as downloads. We reference them and link to the official pages; the papers a tutor works from in a session are the ones your child's school has already set, marked and returned, which are also the most useful papers in existence because they carry a teacher's comments.

None of this makes tuition less effective. Teaching a student to read a mark scheme and audit their own answer against it is more durable than any text a tutor could have supplied, and it is the skill that transfers into the IB Diploma or A Levels the following year.

whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0620 chemistry entry and a Pearson 4CH1 entry need different paper practice. We ask for syllabus codes at the enquiry stage and match on them, because a tutor who knows the content but not the papers will teach well and prepare a child for the wrong examination.
