faqs.question: Which authority licenses my child's IGCSE school, and does that change what they sit?
faqs.answer: Five bodies license private schools across the UAE: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. None of them picks your child's examination board — the school does that. What they change is the evidence available to you, since inspection reporting and curriculum approval sit at different levels depending on the emirate.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my school enters Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the syllabus codes, subject by subject, and get them in writing. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for mathematics or 0625 for physics. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes are alphanumeric, such as 4MA1 or 4PH1. The textbook cover and the small print on a report card usually show one or the other. Mixed schools are common here, so a single answer for the whole timetable is not safe: a child can sit Cambridge sciences and Pearson mathematics in the same year.

faqs.question: What does a Core entry do to the grade my child can be awarded?
faqs.answer: It caps it. Core and Extended are separate routes with separate papers, and a Core candidate sits papers written for the Core content list, which does not reach the top of the grade scale. An Extended entry opens the full range and assumes additional content a Core set was never taught. The decision is made by the school on set placement and submitted by the examinations officer well before the papers. Before you buy any hours, ask in writing which tier your child is currently expected to be entered for.

faqs.question: Can a school still move a Year 11 student from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the final entry deadline has not passed. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows how early that falls: final entries were due 27 November 2026 for examinations beginning 3 February 2027. Before the deadline, a head of department will consider marked work on extended questions and a timed paper sat under proper conditions. After it, amendments sit with the centre and the board, may carry a charge and may be declined. Gather the evidence roughly two months before entries close rather than arguing the case in January.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grade is the floor the Ministry of Education will accept?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That is from Gulf Today's July 2026 report of the ministry's clarification. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, because equivalency rules are revised and a tuition page is not the authority.

faqs.question: Does my child's Arabic grade help the equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Not towards the five-subject count. The ministry's clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE total, so a family counting them can be a subject short without realising. The grades still matter elsewhere: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, they appear on school reports, and they affect progression within the school. Plan the five counting subjects deliberately in Year 10 rather than hoping the total works out.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell me before I book IGCSE hours?
faqs.answer: Less than the headline suggests and more than parents use. The band describes the school, not your child's set, and a school rated well overall can still be short of an Extended chemistry specialist in a particular year. The useful part is inside the report: the subject-level attainment and progress judgements, which tell you whether weak results in a set are a school-wide pattern or specific to your child. Read those sections, then decide whether you are buying teaching the school is not providing or practice the school cannot individualise.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge final entry deadline fall months before the papers?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive everything the board then has to produce: question paper allocation per zone, materials despatch to centres, and the administration around forecast grades. Cambridge's March 2027 key dates put final entries on 27 November 2026, examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades on 27 February 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May. For a family, the practical effect is that subject and tier decisions are effectively locked in autumn, so any case for a change has to be built with evidence in October.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge administrative zone change which timetable we should read?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is worth checking rather than assuming. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its guidance for exams officers that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in, then read that timetable. A date copied from a British school's website is the wrong document for a UAE centre.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE as a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private candidacy runs through an examination centre that accepts external entries, and the centre handles registration, deadlines and the fee. Not every subject is available this way: components requiring coursework, a practical or a moderated oral may be restricted or unavailable to externals, which in science usually pushes a candidate towards the written alternative-to-practical route. Confirm subject availability and the entry deadline with the centre before planning any teaching. A tutor can prepare a private candidate thoroughly but cannot enter them for an examination or act as their centre.

faqs.question: My son studies IGCSE Physics with an online tutor — what happens about the practical paper?
faqs.answer: At most centres, practical skills in IGCSE sciences are assessed through a written paper rather than a laboratory examination, which is why online teaching works for this component. That paper tests apparatus diagrams, tables with correct units and significant figures, graph plotting, identifying anomalous readings and suggesting improvements to a method — all of which can be taught and practised over video. Laboratory time itself remains the school's to provide. Ask the examinations officer which practical component the school has entered, because the answer changes what practice is useful.

faqs.question: What does the IGCSE November series change for a retake?
faqs.answer: It removes most of the waiting. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series each year, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November. Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 — so a resit decision taken in August can produce a result the following January rather than the following August. Entry deadlines still apply months ahead, and the entry is made by a centre, so plan it with the school in September.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IGCSE tuition cost in the UAE in 2026?
faqs.answer: Across providers surveyed in October 2026, rates run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IGCSE or A Level subject specialist. Premium named tutors are advertised above AED 650. These are market figures, not our price list: we confirm a rate in writing after a tutor has been matched to the named subject and tier.

faqs.question: Does an online IGCSE tutor need the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. Ask any tutor to show the permit before a first paid lesson, and treat reluctance as the answer.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go with IGCSE coursework before it stops being my child's work?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, model a technique on a different example, question a draft the student has written and point out where a paragraph fails to answer the task. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft into their own prose or hand back a finished piece. Schools authenticate coursework as the candidate's own, so a sudden leap in quality is a risk the student carries. If a provider offers to take a project from draft to submission, that is the signal to stop.

faqs.question: We are moving from Dubai to Sharjah mid-Year 10 — does the IGCSE course carry over?
faqs.answer: The qualification does, but the detail may not. Both schools may teach IGCSE while entering different boards or tiers, so the first thing to establish is whether the new school uses the same syllabus codes and the same Core or Extended route. The regulator also changes: Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Sharjah's to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves curricula and assessment methods in that emirate. Ask the receiving school for codes, tier and the examination centre, and expect a short block of tuition to close whatever content was sequenced differently.

igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and the date
igcse-tutor.closingBody: An IGCSE tutor in the UAE is worth hiring once you know three things: which syllabus code your child is entered for, which tier that entry sits on, and when the series and its deadlines fall. Those three facts turn a vague worry into a plan with a shape. Send them to us, or send what you have and we will tell you what to ask the examinations officer. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, a trial lesson at no charge is available once a tutor is matched, and the rate is confirmed in writing before anything is paid.

intro.heading: Why a straight answer on price needs the school system behind it
paragraphs: An hour of IGCSE support in the UAE is advertised anywhere between AED 33 and AED 650. Both ends of that range are real and both are legal. Budget online providers publish starting rates from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour; qualified subject tutors working online sit in a published band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300; specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; the premium end of the Dubai market reaches AED 650. A visiting in-home hour, where the travel sits inside the fee, is published at AED 180 to AED 500. Those are market figures from provider rate cards and from a 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey, not IB Gram's price list.

A twenty-fold spread is not a mystery once you see what sits under it. The UAE school system hands different decisions to different bodies, and each decision lands somewhere in the hourly rate. Your emirate's authority licenses the school and, in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, approves its curricula and assessment methods. The federal Ministry of Education sets the subjects every private school must timetable whatever curriculum it is licensed to teach. MoHRE issues the permit that makes paid private tutoring lawful, free of charge, to categories of people as different as a registered schoolteacher and a sixteen-year-old pupil. The exam board fixes the entry deadline, the timetable zone and the results date. None of those bodies sets a tutoring fee. Together they decide who may charge you, for what, and in which weeks the money can still change a grade.

That is the useful way to read a quote. A rate of AED 60 an hour and a rate of AED 400 an hour can both be permitted under the same ministerial resolution, because the permit confirms the right to teach privately and says nothing about subject depth, syllabus knowledge or exam-series experience. Dubai held private school fees flat for 2026-27 under an economic incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion, and no equivalent mechanism holds tutoring rates anywhere in the country. Private tuition is a private contract between a family and a permitted individual or a licensed institute.

So this page does the arithmetic in the order the system imposes it. First the published bands, mapped to the permit categories that can legally occupy each one. Then the four separate bills a UAE IGCSE family receives and who decides each. Then Dubai's own enrolment numbers, which are the demand side of your quote. Then the overheads a licensed tuition centre carries before it teaches anybody, the Abu Dhabi ethics rule that closes the cheapest route on purpose, the three ministry subjects you cannot buy a different version of, and the exam calendar that decides whether an hour bought in March is worth what an hour bought in September was.

One thing is settled before you start comparing. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of our service in India and nowhere in the Emirates, so no tutor on the platform travels to a UAE address. That is a cost structure as much as a format: you are paying for a Chemistry 0620 or Computer Science 0478 specialist on Gulf Standard Time rather than for whoever is willing to drive to your community at 5pm on a Tuesday.

igcse-tutor-cost.programmesIntro: An IGCSE quote should name a board, a tier and a series before it names a price, because those three things decide how many hours the course needs and when they are worth buying. These are the routes UAE schools actually enter, with what each does to a tutoring budget.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the shared content of a Cambridge syllabus and is examined on papers that stop at a capped grade. In Maths 0580 and the sciences a Core entry is sat on different papers from an Extended entry, so Core teaching is not the same lesson delivered more slowly. It is a narrower specification with its own past-paper set and its own mark allocations.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools use Core entries where a pupil's Year 9 evidence does not support Extended, and the decision is made inside the school, not by the board or the emirate authority. For a family this is the single largest cost variable in the whole plan: hours spent chasing Extended content for a Core candidate buy nothing, and hours spent securing the top of the Core range are usually the cheaper route to a usable grade.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: The Extended tier carries the supplementary content and the papers that reach the full grade range, which is what a sixth form asking for a grade 7 in Maths or Physics is looking for. Extended papers reward multi-step problems and extended written reasoning rather than recall, which is why they absorb more teaching time per topic than the Core versions of the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Across Dubai, where UK-curriculum pupils are 37 per cent of the private sector, Extended is the default entry in the academic schools and the pressure point is the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 7. Published market rates for Extended-tier subject specialists sit in the AED 200-450 band. The decision to pay those rates is best made in Year 10, when there are still terms rather than weeks to use.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE suite runs to its own syllabus codes, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, and is examined in May/June and in November each year. Some subjects allow a modular pattern, so a candidate can bank units rather than sit everything at the end. The specifications differ enough from Cambridge that past-paper practice is not interchangeable.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE family often discovers the board only when the entry confirmation arrives. It matters for money: a November series exists in the Pearson calendar, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with the previous November's results reaching students on 22 January 2026. A modular route spreads tutoring across more months and more sittings than a single terminal series does.

programmes.name: Post-IGCSE routes: A Level and IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are the entry currency for the sixth form, and a school's own offer for A Level Physics or Higher Level Chemistry is normally expressed in IGCSE grades. The federal equivalency route for the British track also expects accredited subjects at A or AS Level on top of the IGCSE count, which is why the Year 11 result has consequences well past Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: The practical effect in the UAE is that Year 11 money is buying two things at once: a certificate and a sixth-form place. Dubai adds seven private schools for 2026-27, four of them UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, which creates places but does not lower published grade requirements. Families planning an IB Diploma after IGCSE should treat Maths tier as the decision with the longest shadow.

igcse-tutor-cost.subjectsIntro: Price follows scarcity at subject level more than at tier level. These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families ask for most often, with what the teaching actually involves and where the market pool is thin enough to move a rate.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The deepest tutor pool in the country and therefore the most competitive rate. Extended work turns on algebraic fluency, transformations and the longer multi-step questions near the back of the paper. Marks are lost in method lines that are never written down, which is a habit that takes weeks rather than hours to change.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Numerate and unit-heavy, with a practical component examined either as a laboratory paper or as a written alternative. Most UAE candidates sit the written alternative, which rewards being able to describe a method, identify a control variable and read a results table rather than being handy with apparatus.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for a large share of lost marks at Extended level. Specialists in this subject are scarcer in the UAE market than Maths specialists, which is visible in quoted rates for exam-term hours in the AED 250-400 range.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Looks approachable and is marked strictly. Extended answers need precise terminology and command-term discipline: describe, explain and suggest are scored differently, and a correct idea in the wrong register scores nothing. Genetics and transport in plants are the usual repair jobs.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: A large entry across UAE schools and often the subject that decides whether an equivalency file has five usable grades. Reading comprehension and the summary task are trainable within a term; the speaking component is handled by the school and needs rehearsal rather than content.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature (Cambridge 0500, 0475)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative question reward structure above vocabulary. Tutoring here is mostly timed practice with line-by-line feedback on the student's own writing, which is slower work than content subjects and usually booked as a longer weekly block.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory paper on data representation and networks. One of the thinnest tutor pools in the Emirates: schools teach it, specialist private tutors for it are harder to find, and quoted rates sit at the upper end of the market band as a result.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Marks live in application and evaluation, not definitions. A candidate who can define elasticity but cannot apply it to a named case study loses the top band on every long question. Short, frequent essay-plan sessions beat long content lectures in both subjects.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics (Cambridge 0606, 0607)
subjects.description: Taken by the strongest sets as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level Maths, including calculus and trigonometric identities that sit outside the standard syllabus. Very few private tutors in the UAE market offer it, and availability rather than price is usually the binding constraint.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Timetabled in every UAE private school under federal rules, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Outside support has to work to the school's own programme, because different or additional content needs prior ministry permission, so a tutor's job here is practice and feedback rather than a parallel syllabus.

igcse-tutor-cost.regionsTitle: What changes about the cost in each emirate
igcse-tutor-cost.regionsIntro: The published rate bands are national and the rules around them are not. Who licenses your school, who approves its assessment methods and whether a visiting tutor can realistically reach you all vary by emirate, which is why the same subject feels differently priced in Dubai and in Fujairah.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 pupils, with UK curriculum the largest share at 37 per cent. The deepest tutor pool and the most published rate cards in the country, which keeps the mid-band competitive, and the highest premium rates too.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and sets professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff. Those rules, as reported in the press, bar a teacher from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which removes the cheapest informal route many families try first.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment approval sitting with the emirate is a reason to confirm what your school is actually entering before paying for paper practice.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here answer to the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, so the questions a parent asks about curriculum and assessment go to the school and the ministry. Local specialist supply in less common IGCSE subjects is thin, and live video removes that limit.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, programmes, activities and assessment methods. Published in-home rates carry travel that a northern-emirates address makes expensive, which is the main reason families here compare formats rather than tutors.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision. A visiting specialist for Computer Science 0478 or Additional Mathematics 0606 is close to unobtainable at any price on the east coast, so the realistic comparison is between a generalist nearby and a subject specialist over video.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision again, and the smallest private sector of the seven. The market-rate tables published for Dubai are the only public reference point most families have here, which makes it worth knowing that those figures are Dubai figures with Dubai travel inside them.

schoolClusters.note: The largest IGCSE entry in the country sits in these schools and their feeders, which is why specialist Maths and science tutors are easiest to find on a Dubai timetable and hardest to find at 4pm. Inspection reports for each school are published by the regulator and are worth reading before any hours are booked.

A smaller IGCSE cohort than Dubai and a tighter local tutoring market, with ADEK's staff ethics rules shaping what support a school can offer informally. Families here routinely compare a visiting generalist against a subject specialist taught over video, and the subject specialist usually wins on syllabus fit.

Sharjah schools work under SPEA, while Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah schools work under the federal Ministry of Education. Published in-home market rates of AED 180-500 an hour assume short travel; across these emirates the travel assumption breaks, and the format comparison matters more than the brand of provider.

igcse-tutor-cost.modesIntro: Three ways UAE families buy IGCSE hours, each with a different cost profile. The right one depends on how far away the series is and whether the problem is content, technique or confidence under timed conditions.

modes.title: A weekly one-to-one hour across Years 10 and 11
modes.description: The cheapest route per grade moved, because it spreads the work across terms rather than weeks and uses the school's own sequence. A weekly hour in one subject from early Year 10 gives a tutor room to fix method habits, which is the slow work that cannot be compressed into an exam-term block.

modes.title: A paid block before a series
modes.description: Eight to twelve concentrated hours aimed at a specific paper, usually booked after mock results. This is the format most families buy and the most expensive per hour of change, because technique under timed conditions is all that can realistically shift in the final weeks. It works best when the diagnosis is already clear.

modes.description: One paid hour that answers whether paid hours are the right purchase at all. A specialist reads the mock script, names what is actually holding the grade, and says plainly if the fix is school-side, revision-habit-side or genuinely a teaching gap. Families with nine subjects and one budget start here more often than they expect.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE hour costs in the UAE, and which authority has any say over it
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor cost in the UAE lands between AED 33 and AED 650 an hour as published in 2026, and no UAE authority sets, caps or approves any figure in that range. Emirate regulators approve school tuition fees. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah they also approve curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Private tuition between a family and a permitted tutor sits outside all of that.

What the regulators do decide is who is allowed to charge you. Paid private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, and the eligible categories stretch from a teacher registered at a government or private school to an unemployed resident, a university student and a pupil aged fifteen to eighteen. One permit, one legal status, five very different kinds of teaching, and they do not cost the same.

That is why the band table below is organised by who occupies each price point rather than by adjectives like premium or affordable. A quote of AED 60 an hour is usually a permitted student or recent graduate working from the textbook. A quote of AED 300 is usually a subject teacher with a syllabus code in their head and a drawer of past papers they know by paper number. Both are lawful; only one of them can tell you why your daughter lost four marks on an electrolysis question.

Treat every figure on this page as market information with a date attached. The bands come from provider rate cards published in 2026 and from a 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are not IB Gram prices, and any provider quoting you a number should be willing to say what it includes, what it excludes and when it was last reviewed.

sections.heading: Four bills, four different people deciding: how money reaches a UAE IGCSE family
paragraphs: Parents talk about the cost of IGCSEs as one figure. It is four, and only one of them is a tutoring fee. Confusing them is how families end up paying twice for something already inside the school fee, or discovering an entry cost in the same month they committed a revision budget.

The school fee is approved by the emirate authority. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second package of economic incentives valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, fee approval sits with the emirate authority alongside approval of curricula and assessment methods. Inside that fee sit the mandatory ministry subjects and, in most schools, the exam entries.

The exam entry is a separate transaction between the school as a centre and the board. Cambridge and Pearson publish deadlines rather than parent-facing prices: a centre sets what it recharges, and a private candidate pays whatever the centre they register with charges. No board publishes an AED figure, so any provider quoting you one should name the centre it came from.

The tutoring fee is the only line in the four that is genuinely yours to negotiate, and the only one with no approving authority above it. The fourth line is the one nobody budgets: the cost of fixing something late, which is almost always more expensive than the same work done in Year 10, and occasionally not purchasable at all once an entry deadline has closed.

sections.heading: Dubai's enrolment numbers are the demand side of your quote
paragraphs: Tutoring rates in this country are not set by tutors. They are set by how many families want the same hour. Dubai publishes enough data through its regulator to work out why the mid-band has stayed competitive while exam-term hours have not.

In 2024-25 the Dubai private sector taught 387,441 pupils across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest share at 37 per cent, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. More than a third of a very large sector sitting UK-curriculum examinations is why Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE tutors are the most plentiful category in the market, and why Maths 0580 is the cheapest specialist hour you will price all year.

The supply side keeps moving. Six new private schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent; for 2026-27 Dubai adds seven more, four of them UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. New UK-curriculum places mean a larger IGCSE cohort next year, which pushes demand for the same April and May evening slots rather than spreading it.

The practical reading for a parent is seasonal, not annual. The pool of permitted IGCSE tutors in the Emirates is at its deepest in September and its thinnest in the eight weeks before a series, and that is when the 500-650 band fills. Nothing about the published school-fee freeze changes that, because the scarcity being priced is a Tuesday at 5pm in April, not a place in a school.

sections.heading: The permit that lets someone charge you is free, and open to a school pupil
paragraphs: This is the fact that explains the bottom half of the price range, and almost nobody writing about tutoring costs in the UAE mentions it. The private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Because it costs nothing, a permit is not a quality signal and a permitted tutor is not automatically an experienced one. The eligible categories include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school pupils aged fifteen to eighteen. A sixteen-year-old with a permit and an A* in Maths can lawfully charge your Year 10 for help, and some of the AED 33-65 band is exactly that.

What the permit does tell you is that the person charging you is operating inside the law. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The ministry has not published a fine schedule, so no figure should be quoted at you, and a provider who cannot say which permit route its tutors use is telling you something.

Ask for the permit position, then ask the separate question that actually sets the price: which syllabus code, which tier, which series, and which papers have you taught through to results. The permit confirms the right to teach privately. It says nothing about whether the hour is worth AED 60 or AED 400.

sections.heading: What a licensed tuition centre pays for before it teaches anybody
paragraphs: A group class at a Dubai centre and a freelance hour at your kitchen table are priced by different arithmetic, and the difference is regulatory as much as commercial. An individual needs one free permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from the regulator.

That process has shape and cost. Initial approval comes first, there is a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal has to be requested at least thirty days before expiry. On top of the permit sit rent on a teaching space, trade licence fees, staff visas, and the obligation to keep the whole file current every year. None of that teaching happens before any of it is paid.

So a centre's group rate of AED 100-150 per pupil per hour is not simply an undercut of a one-to-one rate. It is premises and compliance divided by the number of children in the room. That can be real value for a Maths revision class where twelve pupils are making the same mistake, and poor value where one child needs their own electrolysis question unpicked.

A platform that teaches one-to-one over live video carries neither the premises nor the institute permit, and the honest version of that is not that it is cheaper by nature. It is that the overhead sits in matching, scheduling and quality checks rather than in rent, and that the tutor pool is the whole roster rather than whoever the centre has hired for that branch. Never accept the shorthand that a licence to run premises is an endorsement of teaching quality; it is a permit to operate a place.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi closed the cheapest route on purpose
paragraphs: The first thing many UAE families try is not the market at all. It is the teacher who already teaches their child, asked quietly about evenings. In Abu Dhabi that route is closed by design, and understanding why saves an awkward conversation and a risky arrangement.

ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, as reported in the Gulf press, prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school. A teacher tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and that permit's code of conduct also bars serving pupils affiliated with their own school. Treat this as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording, but the direction is unambiguous.

The reasoning is a conflict of interest a parent should want removed. A teacher who sets the internal assessment, writes the forecast grade and marks the mock should not also be paid privately by the family of a candidate in that class. Removing that option is what protects the integrity of the grade you are eventually relying on.

What it leaves is a ladder of support worth climbing in order, because the first two rungs are free. Subject clinics and intervention sessions the school already runs cost nothing and are run by the person who knows the entry. A different teacher within the same school may be permitted, subject to the school's own policy. Only after that does a paid external tutor make sense, and at that point the job is to buy a specialist in the right board, tier and code rather than proximity.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: hours you cannot buy a different version of
paragraphs: Three subjects on your child's timetable are not IGCSE options and are not negotiable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and the federal baseline is explicit that private schools are free on curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The rules are specific enough to change what outside support can legitimately sell. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab pupils and for Arabic as a first language. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must have appropriate approval from the regulator to teach those subjects.

Then the line that matters most for a tutoring budget: for these mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. You cannot buy a better Arabic syllabus. Anyone offering a parallel programme for these subjects is either describing school homework support in grander words or proposing something the rules do not allow.

Instructional time is counted in forty-minute lesson units, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run under twenty-five minutes. Useful arithmetic when a provider quotes a session: a school period is not an hour, and a quote per period against a rate per hour is a twenty-five to thirty-three per cent difference in what you are actually buying.

sections.heading: The money is committed months before the papers are sat
paragraphs: Exam boards do not publish prices for parents, but they publish the deadlines that decide whether your money can still change anything. The pattern is consistent and counter-intuitive: the decisions with the largest financial consequence happen long before the exam season a family is saving for.

Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its published key dates for the February-March 2027 series show the shape clearly: final entries due 27 November 2026, the exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry closed more than two months before the first paper.

Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so confirm dates on the board's own page before committing money to a plan.

Read against those dates, the value of an hour changes through the year. Tier decisions and board confirmation are worth money in Year 10 and worth nothing after an entry closes. A visible mark gap found in a January mock can still be worked on for a June series. An eight-week block bought in April is buying technique, not content, and should be priced and judged as such.

sections.heading: Why a Computer Science 0478 hour costs more here than a Maths 0580 hour
paragraphs: Subject is a bigger price variable than tier, board or emirate, and the reason is supply. With 37 per cent of Dubai's private pupils on a UK curriculum, the schools that teach IGCSE are concentrated in a handful of subjects, and so are the teachers who could tutor them.

Maths, the three separate sciences and English have the deepest pools in the country. There are more teachers of them, more recent graduates who sat them, and more published rate cards that compete on them. That competition is what keeps the mid-band around AED 150-300 for a qualified online tutor of those subjects.

The thin end is narrow and rarely discussed. Computer Science 0478, Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure Mathematics, Design and Technology, and first-language Arabic have small cohorts and few specialist private tutors anywhere in the Emirates. When a subject pool is thin, the constraint that bites first is not price; it is whether anybody is free at all in the eight weeks before a series. The premium that appears in those weeks is scarcity, not quality.

The honest position is to say so, and to say what happens when the answer is nobody. If no UAE-based specialist covers a syllabus code at the hour a family needs, we say so rather than substituting a generalist and calling it a match. Where a specialist outside the UAE teaches the same specification, the lesson is still one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the rate is quoted before anything is booked.

sections.heading: What no amount of money may buy
paragraphs: Some things in this market are for sale and should not be. Pages ranking for IGCSE and IB searches in the Emirates openly sell finished assessed work for four-figure sums. Buying it is the most expensive decision available to a family on this page, because the price is not the fee; it is the candidate's qualification.

The line is simple to state. A tutor may teach the specification, model a method, discuss a plan, ask hard questions about an argument, and give written feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor may not write, redraft to completion or supply coursework, a portfolio piece or any assessed component. Where coursework is part of an IGCSE, the school's own internal deadlines and declarations apply, and a tutor who offers to work around them is proposing malpractice rather than tuition.

Published material has a boundary too. Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the boards. We reference them, name them by code and point at the official pages; we do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, and a fee charged for board material a school can obtain through its own centre access is a fee worth refusing.

The same discipline applies to claims. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so. No tutor here is described as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, and examiner experience is never offered as access to marking, boundaries or paper content. A provider willing to blur any of those lines for a sale will blur others later.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor and a live video hour are two different purchases
paragraphs: Families comparing quotes usually assume they are comparing the same product at different prices. They are not. The published in-home band of AED 180-500 an hour and the qualified online band of AED 150-300 buy different things, and the difference is bigger than the money.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. Home visits are part of what we do in India and not in the Emirates, so no tutor on the platform travels to a UAE address. We would rather state that at the top of a page about cost than let a parent discover it after a deposit. The case for the format stands on its own terms: a family in Khalifa City or Fujairah gets a Chemistry 0620 Extended specialist on Gulf Standard Time, rather than the best available teacher within a twenty-five minute drive.

The practical differences show up in the parts of tutoring that are not the hour itself. A visiting arrangement prices travel into the fee, loses sessions to traffic and school-run timing, and limits the pool to one emirate's commuting radius. A video lesson starts at 7pm after prep without anyone driving, shares a screen onto the student's own marked script, and records nothing unless a family asks for it.

There are honest trade-offs. A child who needs a supervised room to focus is better served by a parent in the next room than by any format change. A connection problem costs a lesson. The written alternative to practical is the examined route for most UAE candidates anyway, so the laboratory objection matters less than it sounds. Price both options on the same table, as below, and the comparison answers itself for most families.

process.description: Before any figure is discussed we ask for the syllabus code on the entry confirmation, the tier, the series your child is entered for and the emirate the school sits in. Those four facts decide which specialists can help and what the realistic hours look like. A quote given without them is a guess.

The tutor reads a recent mock or piece of marked work beforehand and uses the lesson to test whether the diagnosis holds. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again.

process.description: You receive the proposed number of hours, what each block is for, the rate per session and the dates, in writing, before anything is paid. If the plan depends on an entry deadline or a results date, those appear in it with the board's own page named so you can check them yourself.

process.description: Each month brings a short written account of what moved, what has not and what the next block should target. Tutors can be changed without penalty, and we will say when more hours are unlikely to help as readily as when they are. Paid weeks are scheduled around Ramadan, Eid and school breaks.

whyPoints.description: The bands on this page come from provider rate cards published in 2026 and a 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey, and they are labelled as market information rather than our price list. Three of the six pages currently ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote a currency UAE families do not transact in.

faqs.question: Does any UAE authority set or cap what an IGCSE tutor may charge?
faqs.answer: No. Emirate authorities approve private school tuition fees, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah they also approve curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. None of them approves, caps or publishes a rate for private tutoring. What the federal system regulates is who may charge you: paid private tutoring runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. So the published spread of roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour is a market outcome, not a regulated scale, and every figure you are quoted is a private contract term you can question.

faqs.question: Dubai approved no private school fee rise for 2026-27. Does anything hold tuition rates down too?
faqs.answer: Nothing does. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. That decision governs fees the school charges, which an authority approves. Private tutoring has no approving authority above it, so rates move with demand. The practical consequence is seasonal: the pool of permitted IGCSE tutors is deepest in September and thinnest in the eight weeks before a series, which is when premium bands of AED 500 to AED 650 an hour fill up.

faqs.question: The private tuition work permit is issued free of charge. Why does a permitted tutor still quote more?
faqs.answer: Because the permit and the teaching are separate things. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. It confirms a legal right to teach privately and says nothing about subject depth. What you pay for above the floor of the market is specification knowledge, exam-series experience and the ability to diagnose why a mark was lost rather than show a correct answer. Ask which board, which tier, which syllabus code and which series the tutor has taken through to results. That answer, not the permit, explains a rate.

faqs.question: A university student offered IGCSE Maths at AED 60 an hour. Is that permitted, and what is missing at that price?
faqs.answer: It is permitted. University students are an eligible category for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is why the AED 33 to AED 65 band exists legally in this market. What is usually missing is specification-level knowledge. A recent candidate remembers their own papers accurately and can explain a method clearly, which genuinely helps a Year 10 who is behind on content. They rarely know where Extended-tier marks are allocated, how the command terms are scored, or what a particular paper does with multi-step questions. For a tier decision or a technique rebuild before a series, that gap matters.

faqs.question: Can a sixteen-year-old legally be paid to tutor my child here?
faqs.answer: Yes. The eligible categories for the private tuition work permit include school pupils aged fifteen to eighteen, alongside registered schoolteachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. One permit covers all of them, which is the clearest evidence that a permit is a legality check rather than a quality signal. Peer tutoring at the bottom of the published range can work for confidence and for keeping up with homework. It is not a route to moving a grade 6 to a grade 7, changing tier, or rebuilding exam technique, and nobody should price it as though it were.

faqs.question: What does a licensed Dubai tuition centre carry that a freelance tutor does not?
faqs.answer: An operation with premises and staff needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from the regulator: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. On top of that sit rent, trade licence costs, staff visas and administration. A freelance tutor needs one free permit. That overhead is why a centre's one-to-one rate sits above a freelancer's, and why its group classes are priced per pupil. A licence to operate premises is not a statement about teaching quality, and should not be sold as one.

faqs.question: Our school is in Sharjah, where the authority approves assessment methods. What should we pay for there?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, and the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge works the same way. For a family that means the school's assessment pattern is settled above the school, so paying for paper practice against the wrong pattern is wasted money. Get the board, the syllabus code and the tier in writing from the school first. Then buy hours against that specification. The emirate authority is the reason to confirm rather than assume; the board is what the hours should target.

faqs.question: Is there cheaper support inside the school itself before we pay anyone privately?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is worth exhausting first. Subject clinics, intervention groups and departmental revision sessions are inside the fee you already pay and are run by staff who know exactly which papers your child is entered for. Ask the head of department what is available and who attends. One caution: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving pupils affiliated with the teacher's school. Free school support is encouraged. A private arrangement with your child's own teacher is not.

faqs.question: Why will a provider not include Cambridge past papers and mark schemes in a paid package?
faqs.answer: Because they are not the provider's to sell. Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are published by Cambridge and Pearson and belong to them. A reputable tutor references them, names them by code and points to the official pages, which schools and registered centres can access directly. Reproducing them as downloads is copyright infringement, and for unreleased material it is an exam-security problem as well. If a quote has a line item for board material, ask which centre supplied it. In most cases your school can obtain the same material at no charge.

faqs.question: Dubai is adding seven schools and 16,846 places. Does extra supply make tutoring cheaper?
faqs.answer: Not in the way families hope. Dubai adds seven private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places, after six opened in 2025-26 with enrolment up 6 per cent. More UK-curriculum places means a larger IGCSE cohort, which increases demand for the same after-school hours rather than reducing it. Extra places do lower the chance of being unable to find a school, and they slowly deepen the teaching pool in the emirate. Neither effect reaches the 5pm slot in April, which is where UAE tutoring prices are actually made.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a stronger Arabic syllabus than the one our school is licensed to teach?
faqs.answer: No, and that is a rule rather than a preference. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are timetabled in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school teaches, and schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, with language-of-instruction rules for each. Outside support for these subjects is practice and feedback on the school's own programme. Anyone selling a parallel Arabic curriculum is either renaming homework help or proposing something the rules do not allow.

faqs.question: Why does an hour of IGCSE Computer Science 0478 cost more here than an hour of Maths 0580?
faqs.answer: Supply. Maths has the deepest tutor pool in the country, with more teachers, more recent candidates and more competing rate cards, which holds the qualified online band near AED 150 to AED 300. Computer Science 0478 has a small cohort and few specialist private tutors anywhere in the Emirates, so quoted rates sit at AED 250 to AED 450 and the real constraint before a series is whether anyone is free at all. The same applies to Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure Mathematics. Where scarcity is doing the pricing, book early rather than paying more later.

faqs.question: If our daughter sits IGCSE papers as a private candidate, which costs fall to us?
faqs.answer: The entry itself has to go through a centre, and the centre sets what it charges a private candidate. Neither Cambridge nor Pearson publishes a parent-facing AED figure, so ask the centre directly and in writing. Deadlines are the harder cost: Cambridge's final entries for the February to March 2027 series were due on 27 November 2026, months before the papers. Teaching, materials and any practical arrangements are also yours rather than a school's. Budget for entry, teaching and the administrative time, and treat the entry deadline as the point after which money can no longer change the subject list.

faqs.question: A provider quotes AED 650 an hour for an examiner. What should we ask before paying it?
faqs.answer: Three questions. First, what evidence of current examiner status exists, because the status is asserted far more often than it is held, and nobody should describe a tutor as an examiner without being able to show it. Second, what the hour actually delivers that a strong subject teacher's hour does not; examiner experience is not access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and should never be sold as if it were. Third, whether the premium reflects scarcity in the subject or only in the diary. The top of the published Dubai market reaches AED 650, and sometimes that is simply a full calendar in April.

faqs.question: Cambridge entries close months before the papers. When should the money actually be spent?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families spend it. Cambridge's published key dates for the February to March 2027 series show final entries due 27 November 2026, exams from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February and results on 13 May. Before the entry closes, money can still change the board decision, the tier and the subject list, which are the highest-value decisions in the whole plan. After it closes, hours buy content and technique only. An hour bought in Year 10 is working on habits; an hour bought eight weeks out is working on timing and precision, and should be judged on that.

faqs.question: We are in Fujairah. Does distance from Dubai change what we are charged?
faqs.answer: It changes in-home rates and not online ones. Published UAE in-home rates of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour have travel inside them, and those figures assume short Dubai or Abu Dhabi journeys. From an east-coast address, a visiting specialist in a thin subject is close to unobtainable at any price. Private schools in Fujairah come under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, which changes who you ask about curriculum, not what you pay. Teaching over live video is priced identically in Fujairah and in Dubai, because there is no journey in it.

faqs.question: We are comparing a visiting tutor with IB Gram. What are we actually buying?
faqs.answer: Two different products. A visiting arrangement buys a teacher in the room, with travel inside the fee, a pool limited to your commuting radius and sessions that traffic can cost you. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, matched by syllabus code and tier, on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our service in India and not in the Emirates, so no tutor here travels to a UAE address. What that buys instead is a Chemistry 0620 Extended or Computer Science 0478 specialist for a family in Khalifa City or Umm Al Quwain on the same terms as a family in Jumeirah.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson include, and is anything payable before it?
faqs.answer: Nothing is payable and no card details are taken. The trial is a full lesson with the specialist who would teach the course, not a sales call. We ask for the syllabus code, the tier, the series and a recent piece of marked work or a mock script beforehand, so the hour is spent testing a diagnosis rather than collecting information. You finish with a written view of what is holding the grade and what the hours would target. If the match is wrong, say so and we propose a different tutor at no cost.

igcse-tutor-cost.closingHeading: Start with the four facts, then look at the number
igcse-tutor-cost.closingBody: An IGCSE tutor cost in the UAE only means something once the board, the tier, the syllabus code and the series are on the table, because those four facts decide which specialists exist and which weeks are still useful. Send them to us with the emirate your child's school sits in and we will say what the realistic hours are, where the published market bands sit for that subject, and whether paid hours are the right purchase at all. The trial lesson is with the tutor who would teach the course, nothing is payable to book it, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The search says near me; the thing that is actually close is a deadline
paragraphs: An IGCSE year has very few moments that cannot be recovered, and almost all of them are dates rather than places. The final entry deadline for the published Cambridge March 2027 series falls on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the exam period opens on 3 February 2027. Forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. None of those dates move because a family lives in Jumeirah rather than Khalifa City, and none of them care how long the drive is. That is the honest reading of a proximity search: the clock is the local thing, and the tutor does not have to be.

Parents search for an IGCSE tutor near me in the UAE for a sensible reason. A tutor who lives nearby can be there on Tuesday, can see the exercise book, and can be judged on a handshake. The trouble is what a twenty-minute radius does to the shortlist. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE together run dozens of syllabuses, each with its own paper structure, option codes and practical or coursework component. A radius filter selects for who is free and close. It does not select for someone who has marked Extended-tier Chemistry answers, knows where Paper 4 candidates lose method marks, or can tell you in one sitting whether a grade 5 mock was a knowledge problem or an exam-technique problem.

So this page answers the proximity question properly and then answers the one underneath it. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition in the UAE as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. What a family gets instead is a subject-and-tier specialist available in the evening slot that suits a UAE school day, with no travel charge folded into the rate and no session lost to Sheikh Zayed Road at six o'clock.

Everything that follows is organised by time, because that is how an IGCSE year actually fails. Section by section: what near me really measures, the four calendars running at once, the forecast grade that lands in February, the statement of entry and what to check on it, results day arriving in a UAE school holiday, what a mid-year arrival has to close, how Ramadan and the three Ministry subjects sit inside a revision term, and how many weeks are left before the format of a lesson stops mattering.

The figures in AED on this page are market rates published by other providers and read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list. They are here because three of the six best-ranking pages for these queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. A parent deciding in week three of a two-year course deserves to see the band before anyone asks for a phone number.

If you take one thing from this page, take the entry deadline. Confirm the series, the board, the syllabus code and the tier your child is entered for, in writing, from the school's exams officer. Every other decision, including whether to book a tutor at all, gets easier once those four facts are on the table.

igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four routes cover almost every UAE family who searches for IGCSE help. The tier and the board are decided by an entry form, not by a tutor, which is why the first conversation is always about what the school has already submitted. The notes below say what each route means specifically inside the UAE school calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: Core-tier entry covers the Core subject content and is assessed on the Core papers, with a grade range that stops short of the top grades. In most subjects that means Paper 1 and Paper 3 rather than Paper 2 and Paper 4, and in the sciences a Core theory paper that leaves out the extension topics entirely. Tutoring at Core tier is usually about securing the grade the entry allows, closing arithmetic and command-term gaps, and making sure every mark on the paper that is reachable is actually reached.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools a Core entry is often made in Year 10 on the strength of one internal assessment, and families do not always realise the grade ceiling it carries until a university prospectus asks for a grade 6. If a move to Extended is being considered, it has to be raised with the exams officer before the entry deadline, not after the mocks.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended entry adds the supplement content and the harder papers, and it is the route that keeps the top grades available. In Mathematics 0580 that is Paper 2 and Paper 4; in Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 it is the Extended theory paper plus the practical component the school has chosen. The extra content is rarely the hardest part. The harder part is the longer, multi-step question that expects a candidate to select a method rather than recognise one, which is exactly what weekly one-to-one work can rehearse.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the default at most British-curriculum schools in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and the usual UAE pattern is eight to ten subjects sat in one series, with Arabic and the Ministry subjects running alongside. That volume, not the difficulty of any single syllabus, is what makes a Year 11 term feel unmanageable without a schedule.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE uses its own codes, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics, with Foundation and Higher tier in place of Core and Extended. The paper structure differs from Cambridge: fewer, longer papers in several subjects, and a different approach to practical assessment. A tutor who prepares a Pearson candidate on Cambridge past papers will cover most of the content and still miss the question style, which is why confirming the code matters more than confirming the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Because provisional timetables for later series are published and then revised, a UAE family should always work from the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a date someone has retyped onto a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Retake and private-candidate entry
programmes.description: A retake is a short, specific project: one or two subjects, a known weak component, and a fixed series to aim at. The work is different from first-time teaching because the content is largely in place and the loss is usually concentrated in one paper or one topic block. Sessions are built around that diagnosis, on past material from the right code and tier, with written feedback after each paper attempt so the pattern is visible rather than remembered.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE a retake decision is often made in the two weeks after results, while the family is travelling. It is also the point where private-candidate entry matters: a candidate no longer on a school roll has to be entered through a centre that accepts external candidates, and that is one of the few genuinely geographic constraints in the whole IGCSE year.

igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families ask for most, with the syllabus codes that most often appear on a statement of entry. Treat every code here as a prompt to check, not as a fact about your child: schools change specifications, and a subject can be entered under a different code in the same building.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-demand subject in this market. Marks are lost less on topic knowledge than on method: unrounded working carried through a multi-step question, a bearings or similar-triangles diagram not drawn, and the last two parts of a long Paper 4 question left blank because time ran out in the middle section.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A-Level Maths or IB Higher Level. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early and unforgivingly, and the step up in algebraic fluency is the usual reason a confident 0580 candidate suddenly looks shaky on a 0606 past paper.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where UAE candidates most often stall, followed by the practical paper's requirement to describe a method precisely enough for someone else to repeat it. Equation recall is cheap to fix; translating a described experiment into a graph and a gradient is the part that needs weeks.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the organic chemistry block account for a large share of lost Extended marks. The common pattern is a candidate who can define a term but cannot apply it to an unfamiliar substance, which shows up as full marks on recall questions and half marks on everything else.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Biology rewards precise written answers more than any other science at this level, and that is where it is lost. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance questions need the command term obeyed exactly: describe, explain and suggest earn marks for different things, and mixing them is the most common single error.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Two IGCSE grades or one, from a syllabus that samples all three sciences. The difficulty is coverage rather than depth: a candidate has to hold physics, chemistry and biology content at once, and revision usually collapses into whichever one they like most unless the plan forces a rotation.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition task carry a large share of the marks and are the most coachable components on any IGCSE timetable. Reading questions reward selecting and reshaping evidence rather than quoting at length, and most UAE candidates gain quickly once that distinction lands.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A very common entry across the Emirates, including for students who speak English all day at school. Marks concentrate in the exercises that test precise comprehension and controlled writing, and timing is often the binding constraint rather than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application and evaluation marks are the whole game. A candidate who defines cash flow and then fails to apply it to the named business in the case study loses the majority of the available marks on that question, and the fix is drilling the final evaluation paragraph rather than relearning the content.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than most students expect: axes labelled, curves shifted in the right direction, the new equilibrium marked. The structured questions then ask for a judgement, and answers that list advantages without weighing them stop short of the top band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The theory paper covers data representation, networks and security, and the problem-solving paper expects pseudocode written to the syllabus convention. Students who code fluently in Python often lose marks for writing Python where the mark scheme expects the specified pseudocode form.

subjects.name: Arabic (first language and foreign language routes)
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places at once for most UAE students: as an IGCSE entry and as a Ministry-mandated subject with its own KHDA requirements on language of instruction and class organisation. Support is planned around both, with the school's own scheme of work as the reference point.

igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: A proximity search behaves differently in each emirate, because the number of schools, the number of exam centres and the regulator all change. The notes below are about what near me actually returns where you live, and what it means for scheduling a weekly session.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest market in the country and the one where a radius search returns the most results of the most variable quality. KHDA oversees private education here, and its school inspection reports are published, which makes a Dubai parent better informed about the school than about the tutor they are about to hire.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules for school staff bar paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. For a parent, that reframes the proximity search: the nearest qualified teacher is often the one person who cannot take the work.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller cluster of British-curriculum schools and a correspondingly thin local pool at Extended tier in the sciences. Evening sessions are easier to schedule here than in Dubai because the commute does not eat the 4pm to 6pm window.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families have a parent working in Dubai, which pushes the realistic session start past 7pm on weekdays.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The IGCSE cohort is small enough that a single school can be the main source of candidates for a subject, and a specialist in a niche option is unlikely to be found within driving distance at all.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods. Distances between communities here make a weekly visiting arrangement fragile in a way that a scheduled video lesson is not.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, on the east coast, and the clearest case for online delivery in the country. A Fujairah family looking for an Extended-tier Chemistry specialist is not choosing between tutors; they are choosing between a specialist on screen and nobody.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education, and absent from almost every competitor page in this market. The practical consequence is that search results for a tutor here are mostly Dubai listings with a wide service-area claim attached.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE candidates in the country, sitting Cambridge and Pearson entries side by side, sometimes within the same subject department. Students we support attend schools across the emirate; inspection reports for each are published by KHDA and are worth reading before any tutoring decision.

A smaller, more concentrated British-curriculum cluster under ADEK, where a single school cohort can dominate a subject entry. Session timing here is shaped by the capital's commute and by the later school finish at some campuses.

Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah, by the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and by the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Subject specialists at Extended tier are scarce locally, which is the single most common reason families here move to online sessions.

sections.heading: Near me, for an IGCSE family, is three different distances
paragraphs: A proximity search measures one thing: how far away a person is. An IGCSE year involves at least five distances, and the one a search engine returns is the least consequential of them. Your child's exam centre is a real location with a real drive attached on the morning of a paper. The regulator that holds your school's file is in a specific emirate and publishes specific documents. The Ministry counter that attests a certificate is a physical appointment. The board that sets the paper is in the United Kingdom and will never be near you. The tutor is the only one of the five whose location can be made irrelevant, and that is precisely what live video does.

This matters because of how a radius filter behaves. Narrow the search to twenty minutes and the pool shrinks to whoever happens to live close, which in most UAE communities means a handful of people available at 5pm on a Tuesday. Among them, the probability that someone has taught Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 to the current specification, or has marked Pearson 4MA1 Higher-tier Paper 2 answers, is a matter of luck. Widen the radius to the whole country and the pool grows, but so does the travel, and travel time is paid for either in money or in a session that starts late and finishes rushed.

The honest answer to the near me question is that the constraint worth optimising is time of day, not kilometres. A UAE school day finishing between 2pm and 3:30pm, plus activities, plus a commute home, leaves a narrow evening window. Removing the drive from both sides of that window is what makes a 7:30pm session with a specialist possible on a weeknight. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition in the UAE as one-to-one lessons over live video for exactly this reason, and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are part of our India service only.

So the table below is the page's opening argument. Four of the five distances in an IGCSE year are fixed by someone else. One of them is optional. Spending the search on the optional one is how families end up with a nearby generalist and a specialist-shaped problem.
