sections.heading: Four calendars run across one IGCSE year, and your school sets only one of them
paragraphs: Families plan around the school calendar, because that is the one that arrives by email. It is also the one with the most give in it. A school internal deadline can be negotiated, a mock can be re-sat, a parents' evening can be rescheduled. The board calendar has none of that flexibility, and it closes first. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries at 27 November 2026, forecast grades at 27 February 2027, the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry closes before the teaching finishes. That ordering is the single most useful thing a parent can internalise.

The third calendar is the one the UAE itself imposes: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring that those requirements be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those subjects occupy real timetable minutes in the same term as IGCSE revision, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. A revision plan that pretends those hours do not exist will not survive February.

The fourth is the university cycle, which for most UAE families begins while IGCSEs are still being sat. Predicted and forecast grades, personal statements and equivalency paperwork all draw on IGCSE outcomes, and all have deadlines set by institutions rather than by boards. A family that treats IGCSE as a self-contained two-year project discovers in Year 12 that a Core-tier entry made quietly in Year 10 has already closed a door.

Reading the table below in order is the point of it. The board closes earliest and moves least. The school closes next and moves a little. The Ministry subjects are immovable in volume but flexible in timing. The university cycle starts later and is where the earlier decisions get priced.

sections.heading: The forecast grade due in February, and what a tutor can still change after it
paragraphs: Cambridge requires a forecast grade from the centre for each candidate, and for the published March 2027 series that deadline was 27 February 2027, three days before the exam period closed on 4 March. Most UAE parents have never heard the phrase until it affects something. A forecast grade is the school's professional estimate, submitted to the board, and it is built from whatever evidence the department holds at the time: the mock, classwork, past-paper scores, the last two unit tests. It is not a prediction of what a tutor will achieve in the remaining weeks, because the person submitting it has no way to know about that work.

The practical consequence is a sequencing problem. If a mock is sat in December and a tutor starts in January, the forecast submitted in February may still be anchored to December's evidence. Families who want the forecast to reflect improvement have to generate visible, school-facing evidence before the submission date: a re-sat paper the department will look at, a unit test, a conversation with the subject teacher. Evidence the school never sees cannot move a number the school submits.

The second consequence is diagnostic. A mock result is the most informative document a UAE family will hold during the whole course, and it is routinely wasted. The grade is the least useful part. The component breakdown, the question-level marks and the script itself say whether the loss is content, method, timing or reading the question, and those four problems have completely different remedies and completely different timescales. A timing problem can move in three weeks. A two-year content deficit in algebra cannot.

Every row assumes the component breakdown is available, which is why the first thing we ask a parent for is the marked script rather than the report card.

sections.heading: The statement of entry is the only document that tells you which paper your child sits
paragraphs: Ask a UAE parent which IGCSE papers their child sits and the answer is usually the subject name. Ask for the syllabus code, the tier and the option code and the answer is usually silence. That is not negligence; schools rarely volunteer it. But the statement of entry carries all of it, and until someone has read it, a tutor is working from an assumption. Cambridge and Pearson run different codes for the same subject, and within Cambridge a Core and an Extended candidate in the same classroom sit different papers with different ceilings.

The document also carries the candidate number and centre number, which is how every subsequent piece of administration is tracked, and it is the basis for the one thing about exam timetables that genuinely is geographic. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the guidance to exams officers is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, with Cambridge stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A UAE centre and a UK centre sitting the same paper can be working to different published times.

So the first fifteen minutes of a first session are administrative, and parents are sometimes surprised by that. We ask for the board, the syllabus codes, the tier for each subject, the components listed, and the series. Those five facts determine which past papers are legitimate practice and which are a waste of an hour. A Higher-tier Pearson candidate drilled on Cambridge Extended papers will cover most of the content and still meet an unfamiliar question style on the day.

sections.heading: Results day lands when UAE families are out of the country
paragraphs: Pearson has published that June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and that November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put results on Direct at 13 May with certificates in late June. Line those up against the UAE school year and the problem is obvious. August results arrive in the middle of the summer break, when a large share of UAE families are abroad. January results arrive mid-term, with a Year 12 timetable already running.

Results day is not just an emotional event; it opens windows that close quickly. A decision about an enquiry about results, a remark, or an entry for the next available series has to be made in the weeks after the grade appears, and those processes run through the exam centre rather than through the family. A parent in a different time zone, with the school on holiday and the exams officer unreachable, loses days they did not know were scarce.

The fix is dull and effective. Before the series, find out from the exams officer three things: the date results are released to students, the email address that will be monitored during the break, and the centre's own deadline for requesting a review of marking. Write them down. If the family is travelling, decide in advance who opens the results and who can act on them. None of this requires a tutor, and all of it is the kind of thing a tutoring page in this market never mentions.

Where we do come in is the decision itself. A component breakdown either supports a retake or it does not, and that judgement is better made from the marks than from disappointment. sections.heading: Arriving mid-IGCSE: what a family that landed in October has to close
paragraphs: The UAE is a country people move to in the middle of things. Dubai's private sector alone enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places. A meaningful share of those seats are filled by children arriving mid-year from a different system entirely. A student who joins Year 10 in October has eleven months to the series and a syllabus that started in September, and the gap is rarely where the family expects it.

From CBSE or ICSE, the content overlap in mathematics and the sciences is usually high and the assessment style is the gap: IGCSE questions ask for method, explanation and application in a form that rewards written reasoning more than speed. From an American system, the opposite applies: the discussion and project habits transfer well and the quantity of examinable content is a shock. From British Year 9, the student is on the right track and simply behind by a term. From MYP, the inquiry skills are strong and the formal paper discipline is not.

None of this is a judgement about any curriculum. It is a statement about what a specific transition costs in weeks. The useful question for a parent in month one is not whether the child is clever but which three things have to be true by the mock, and that is a diagnosable list rather than a feeling. It usually includes a tier confirmation, two or three content blocks, and one piece of exam technique.

The table below is the map we use in a first conversation with an arriving family. The week counts are what families here typically book, not a promise about outcomes, and the right number for any child depends on the diagnostic rather than on the row.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the three Ministry subjects inside the same revision term
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those are not optional extras sitting outside the timetable. They are weekly instructional minutes, calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

KHDA's requirements go further than volume. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, which is a real constraint on what any tutor can legitimately put on screen.

Set that against the academic year and the collision is visible. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm, and the sensible response is to move sessions rather than cancel the term: a post-Iftar slot works well for many families and is often calmer than a 5pm weekday lesson. Eid holidays remove a working week, and summer removes the weeks either side of August results. A revision plan drawn as a flat weekly grid will be wrong by February; one drawn on a wall calendar with the holidays blocked out first will survive.

Practically, this is what we ask families to do before booking a block: mark the Ministry-subject commitments, the school exam weeks, Ramadan and the Eid break on one calendar, and only then count the sessions that are actually available. The number is usually smaller than expected, which is a better thing to discover in October than in March.

sections.heading: The format question, decided by how many weeks are left
paragraphs: Arguments about online against in-home tuition are usually conducted in the abstract, which is why they go nowhere. In practice the format question has a clear answer once you know two things: how many weeks remain before the first paper, and how specialised the help needs to be. With a year to run and a general confidence problem, almost any competent arrangement will work. With ten weeks to run and a specific Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 problem, the pool of people who can help is small, and insisting that they also live nearby is how families end up with the wrong help at the right distance.

The AED figures below are what other providers in this market publish about their own services, read in October 2026, and they are here because most pages in this category publish nothing. EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. These are market rates and not IB Gram's price list; ours is discussed at the consultation.

The structural point inside those numbers is that an in-home rate includes travel, and travel is both a cost and a scheduling constraint. A visiting tutor has to fit your slot into a route, which is why in-home availability clusters in a few communities and why rates rise closer to exams, when the few available people are busiest. A lesson over live video has no route, so the binding constraint becomes the specialist's own calendar rather than the map, and a Fujairah family and a Dubai Marina family see the same list.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition in the UAE as one-to-one lessons over live video, with screen-shared past papers, annotated scripts and session notes the family keeps. Home visits are offered only in India. sections.heading: Coursework when the school deadline is Thursday and the session is on Tuesday
paragraphs: This is where a tutoring market in a hurry gets dangerous, and it should be said plainly. One page ranking for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not tutoring. For an IGCSE candidate, work that is internally assessed or submitted as coursework has to be the student's own, and a submission that is not can end a candidacy. No deadline, and no amount of parental pressure, changes that arithmetic.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and families are often relieved to hear how much it is. A tutor can teach the underlying content. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria and what each band actually requires. A tutor can look at the student's own draft and say where it does not yet meet the criteria, in the student's own hearing, so the student does what comes next. A tutor can teach method writing, data presentation, graph conventions and referencing as skills. A tutor can rehearse the planning process on a different, unassessed example, which is usually the single most effective legitimate intervention available.

What a tutor must not do is also short and clear. Not supply text to be submitted. Not rewrite a paragraph into its final form. Not provide a worked model of the actual assessed task for the student to follow line by line. Not sit alongside the student during an assessment the school is supervising. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabuses, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those belong on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we reference and link them rather than copying them.

The practical answer to the Thursday deadline is a conversation with the subject teacher, not a tutor working through the night. If the student is behind because of illness, a move or a genuine content gap, the department has processes for that and the school's exams officer knows what can and cannot be requested from the board. A tutor's role at that point is to make the next unassessed piece of work go better, and to be honest that the current one has already become the school's problem to manage.

Feedback is given on the student's own draft, never as replacement text

sections.heading: The equivalency file is opened before results, not after
paragraphs: For a UAE university file, IGCSE results feed into a Ministry of Education equivalency process, and the British-track requirements have been publicly clarified. As reported in July 2026, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the clarified rule is five.

On the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The report does not mention EmSAT and states no IB points threshold, which is why no IB equivalency figure appears anywhere on this page. If you need the IB number, read it on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate's attestation authority directly rather than trusting a tutoring site.

The timing point is the one that costs families money. Equivalency is an administrative process with documents, appointments and processing time, run by the Ministry of Education rather than by a school or a tutor. Opening the file while the family is already in the country, before the summer break and before results arrive, means the only missing item in August is the certificate. Opening it in September, from abroad, with a university asking for a decision, is how a gap year starts by accident.

To be explicit about our own position: IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and nothing about tutoring is required for it. We describe the process because a UAE parent planning an IGCSE year needs to know it exists and roughly when it bites. The authority to rely on is the Ministry and the emirate's own service channel, and that is where this page sends you.

process.title: Send the four facts from the statement of entry
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and series for each subject, plus the components listed. If the statement of entry has not been issued yet, the school's exams officer can confirm what has been submitted. These four facts decide which past papers are legitimate practice, and gathering them takes one email.

process.title: A diagnostic on one real script
process.description: We work from a marked mock or a recent past paper rather than a conversation about confidence. The output is a written read of where the marks went by component, and whether the problem is content, method, timing or command terms. If tuition is not what the problem needs, we say so at this stage.

process.title: An introductory lesson at no charge
process.description: One 45-minute session per family, with the matched subject specialist, before any payment is discussed. No card details are taken to book it. It exists so a parent can judge the fit on evidence, and so the student can decide whether they will actually talk to this person for an hour a week.

process.title: A block counted back from the first paper
process.description: We write the plan as dates rather than topics, starting from the exam date on the statement of entry and working backwards through the mock, the coursework deadlines, the Ministry-subject commitments and the Eid break. The number of available sessions is usually smaller than a flat weekly grid suggests.

process.title: Written feedback the family keeps
process.description: Session notes after each lesson and a fortnightly summary naming the component worked on, what the marking exposed and what changes next. If a specialist in a niche subject or tier is not available, we say so and give a date rather than substituting a generalist quietly.

whyPoints.title: The entry details come before the teaching
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge Extended candidate and a Pearson Higher-tier candidate in the same subject sit different papers. We confirm board, code, tier, components and series before the first full session, because practice on the wrong specification is an expensive way to feel productive.

whyPoints.title: A specialist instead of the nearest available adult
whyPoints.description: Removing travel from the arrangement changes what you can choose from. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain sees the same list of subject and tier specialists as a family in Jumeirah, and the binding constraint becomes the tutor's calendar rather than the drive.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are figures other providers publish about their own services, read in October 2026, with the source named in each case. Most pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A parent should see the band before giving a phone number.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: We teach content, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own draft. We do not supply text for submission, and we do not reproduce board papers or mark schemes as downloads. In a market where one ranking page sells finished coursework, this is a difference worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, around a UAE school day
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in GST and planned around a school day that often finishes before 3:30pm, activities, and a commute. During Ramadan a post-Iftar slot is usually easier to protect than a weekday evening one, and school exam weeks are blocked out in advance rather than cancelled at short notice.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated plainly, including when it is a no
whyPoints.description: Niche subjects and specific tiers are not always covered on the week you ask. When a specialist is not free we give a date, or we say the match is not available, rather than putting a generalist in the slot. Families can plan around a clear no; they cannot plan around a vague yes.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor near me actually mean in a country with five school regulators?
faqs.answer: It means less than the phrase suggests. Your exam centre, your regulator and the Ministry attestation counter all have real locations: KHDA covers Dubai, ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA covers Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covers Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The exam board is in the United Kingdom. The tutor is the only part of that list whose location can be made irrelevant, and live video does exactly that. Filter on board, syllabus code and tier instead of on distance, and the shortlist improves immediately.

faqs.question: When does the entry deadline for my child's IGCSE series actually close?
faqs.answer: Months before the paper, which surprises most families. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series set final entries at 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027. Pearson publishes its own deadlines per series and issues provisional timetables that can be revised. Your school's exams officer works to an internal deadline earlier than the board's, so in practice the decision point is earlier still. Ask for your series, your deadline and your tier in writing in September. Every other planning decision, including whether to book tuition at all, depends on those three answers.

faqs.question: What is a forecast grade, and can tutoring change it?
faqs.answer: A forecast grade is the centre's professional estimate of a candidate's likely result, submitted to the board. For the published Cambridge March 2027 series, forecast grades were due 27 February 2027. It is built from the evidence the school holds when it submits: the mock, unit tests, classwork. Tutoring cannot change a number the school has already sent, and the person submitting it has no visibility of private sessions. If you want improvement reflected, it has to become evidence the department sees before the submission date, through a re-sat paper or an assessment the subject teacher marks.

faqs.question: My child's mock came back at a grade 5. Can that still move before the papers?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on why, and the grade alone does not say. Ask for the marked script and the component breakdown. A strong first half with blank final pages is a timing problem, which can shift in a few weeks of sectioned timed practice. Consistent half marks across every topic is usually a command-term problem, which responds to mark-scheme work. Two or three topics at zero is a genuine content gap that needs direct teaching first. A long-standing algebra deficit is the slowest of the four. The honest answer comes after reading the script, not before.

faqs.question: Which exam timetable applies to a UAE exam centre?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance to exams officers states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong zone timetable has been used. In practice that means a UAE centre and a UK centre can sit the same paper to different published times. Get the zone-correct timetable from your school rather than from a general listing, and check it against the statement of entry for clashes before the series starts.

faqs.question: We will be travelling in August when results come out. What should we arrange first?
faqs.answer: Three things, before the summer break begins. The exact date results are released to students, which for Pearson June 2026 was 20 August 2026 to students and 19 August to centres. An email address at the school that will be monitored during the holiday. And the centre's own internal deadline for requesting a review of marking, because those requests go through the centre rather than direct from a parent. Decide in advance who opens the results and who is authorised to act. The windows after results day are short, and a holiday is how families miss them.

faqs.question: How quickly do we have to decide about querying a mark?
faqs.answer: Faster than most families expect, and the process runs through the exam centre, not through you. Both boards operate post-results services with published deadlines that fall within weeks of release, and the centre has to submit on the candidate's behalf. The useful preparation is to know, before results day, who at the school handles it and what their cut-off is. The decision itself should be made from the component breakdown: a near-miss concentrated in one paper is a different case from marks spread thinly below the boundary across all components.

faqs.question: We moved to the UAE in October and my child joined Year 10 late. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a tier confirmation and a gap list, in that order. Find out from the school whether the entry is Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher, because that sets the grade ceiling and is decided by an entry form rather than by ability. Then identify the units already taught. From CBSE or ICSE the content usually transfers and the question style does not. From an American system the opposite is true. From British Year 9 the student is simply a term behind. Families in this position typically book six to twelve weeks of focused catch-up alongside school.

faqs.question: Do lessons stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. School days shorten and the household rhythm changes, so a post-Iftar slot often works better than the usual weekday evening and tends to be calmer and better attended. The Eid break then removes a working week, which matters if the exam series is close. Our practical advice is to mark Ramadan, the Eid holiday, school exam weeks and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies commitments on one calendar before counting how many sessions a term actually contains. The number is usually smaller than a weekly grid implies.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the practical paper over video?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it is worth being precise about which parts. The practical components reward describing a method precisely, identifying variables, tabulating data correctly, plotting accurately and reading a gradient. All of that is written work and transfers well to a screen-shared past paper. What a video lesson cannot do is give a student time with the apparatus, and that has to come from school. The common pattern we see is a candidate who has handled equipment all year and still loses marks on method writing and graph conventions, which is the part sessions can address directly.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost across the UAE market in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published figures, read in October 2026, run from the budget end upwards: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase quoting AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages appear from around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are each provider's own published rates, not IB Gram's; ours is discussed at the consultation.

faqs.question: Is a group revision class worth it eight weeks before a paper?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is whether the whole group shares your child's problem. A group class teaches to an average. Eight weeks out, most candidates do not need more teaching of the syllabus; they need the specific thing their own script keeps costing them, which differs from the student next to them. A group works well for content that is genuinely missing across a cohort and poorly for timing, command terms or one weak component. If you have a marked script, read it first and let the diagnosis choose the format.

faqs.question: Does my child need Arabic and Islamic Education for the Ministry's five-subject count?
faqs.answer: No, and this is a point one ranking page gets wrong. As reported in the July 2026 clarification, the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A competitor page states six subjects. Separately, those subjects remain mandatory at school under KHDA and federal requirements. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae before relying on any website, including this one.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: Treat that as a no, and check. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor to show their permit.

faqs.question: Six weeks are left before the first paper. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes for some problems and no for others, and you deserve the honest split. Six weeks is enough to fix timing, command terms, graph and method conventions, and one or two missing topics, because all of those respond to concentrated paper work with marking in between. It is not enough to rebuild two years of absent algebra or to learn a full science syllabus from a standing start. The first session should be a diagnostic on a real script so the plan targets the two components with the weakest margin, and so nobody spends the last fortnight on the wrong thing.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for my child's subject and tier?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date. Niche subjects, specific tiers and particular boards are not always covered in the week you ask, and the alternative to saying so is putting a generalist into a specialist slot, which wastes the one resource an exam year does not have. If the match is not available we say whether it is a wait of days or weeks, or whether we cannot cover it at all. A clear no is something a family can plan around, which a vague yes is not.

igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the date on the statement of entry
igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Before anything else, get four facts from your child's school in writing: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series for each subject. Those four decide which papers are real practice and when every deadline falls. Send them to us with a marked mock or a recent past paper and we will come back with a written read of where the marks went by component, and whether a block of sessions is the right answer at all. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with an introductory 45-minute session at no charge, one per family, and no card details taken to book it. Home visits are part of our India service only.

intro.heading: The system your child's IGCSE sits inside, before anything about tutoring
paragraphs: An IGCSE in the Emirates is never a free-standing qualification. It sits inside a private school licensed by an emirate authority, teaching a Cambridge or Pearson specification that the school chose, while also delivering Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies that the school must provide whatever curriculum is on the sign outside. The exam entry is made by the school's exams officer to a deadline set months before the paper. The certificate then goes to a federal equivalency process that counts five subjects and deliberately excludes two of the ones your child works hardest at. Tutoring that ignores any of this is just paid homework supervision.

So when a parent searches for IGCSE tutors in the UAE, the useful answer is not a list of names. It is a match made on four facts: the syllabus code the school entered for, the tier your child is sitting, the series the entry is in, and the hours a Gulf school day actually leaves free. A tutor who knows Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Paper 4 is a different tutor from one who knows Pearson 4CH1. A Core-tier Maths student and an Extended-tier Maths student share a subject name and almost nothing else. Get those four facts wrong and the hours are wasted politely.

IB Gram delivers this as online IGCSE tuition. Lessons are one-to-one, over live video, with screen-sharing and a shared whiteboard, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and the mandatory-subject periods. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the Emirates. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation: a family in Al Ain or Fujairah gets the Extended-tier Physics specialist who is genuinely free at seven in the evening, instead of whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of the villa.

The regulatory picture matters more here than in most markets, because it decides things a parent would otherwise assume. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection reports you can read before you enrol. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school. SPEA in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

What follows is the page we wished existed when we started matching UAE families. It names the two boards and what separates them, explains the Core and Extended decision in terms of the grade ceiling it sets, counts an exam series backwards from the entry deadline, publishes what this market actually charges in AED with the provider who published each figure, sets out the MoE equivalency rule that most tutoring sites get wrong, and states in plain words where the line sits on coursework. Read the part you need and ignore the rest.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the wrong zone timetable is the centre's problem, not Cambridge's
Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour; in-home visits run higher because travel sits inside the rate
A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback; nobody here finishes a piece of coursework on a student's behalf

igcse-tutors.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a UAE family on the British track. The two middle ones are the IGCSE itself, and they are not the same qualification under two names: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel publish separate specifications, separate papers and separate timetables for subjects that share a title.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, the run-up
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins decide which tier a child is offered. Schools use Checkpoint tests, internal assessments and setting decisions in Year 9 to stream Maths and the sciences into Core and Extended groups. The content is not examined externally for a grade that follows the child, so families treat it as low stakes. The tier offer that comes out of it is anything but low stakes.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai and Abu Dhabi the Year 9 setting decision often lands in the same term as a school move, because a family's visa, housing or employer changes mid-year far more often here than in the UK. A child who arrives in January from a CBSE or American school is set on evidence from a different system. That is the single most common reason a UAE family calls us about a tier that does not match the child.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Syllabuses are identified by a four-digit code: 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0455 Economics. Maths and the single sciences are tiered into Core and Extended paper sets. Science candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre offers. Grading is A* to G on most syllabuses, with a 9 to 1 version used where the centre enters for it.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools in the Emirates enter for Cambridge, which is why so many UAE parents assume IGCSE and Cambridge are the same word. They are not. Ask the exams officer for the four-digit code on this year's entry, in writing, before you buy a single hour of tutoring. Codes change between specification versions, and a tutor drilling the previous version's Paper 4 is drilling the wrong paper with complete confidence.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Specifications are identified differently: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A, 4EC1 Economics. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and the single sciences are untiered, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers instead of in a separate practical test. Grading across International GCSE is 9 to 1. Exams run in a May or June series and a November series.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of UAE schools enter for Pearson, and some enter for Pearson in one subject and Cambridge in another, which is how a family ends up with two timetables and two sets of past papers for one child. This is worth ten minutes with the exams officer. The November 2026 final International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, which is a different revision run-in from a June entry.

programmes.name: What follows the IGCSE
programmes.description: A Level, the IB Diploma Programme and BTEC all take IGCSE grades as their entry evidence, and each has subject prerequisites that a Core-tier or Foundation-tier grade can quietly fail to meet. The British track to UAE Ministry of Education equivalency also needs post-16 study: one Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, so the post-16 options near a family may genuinely be different from the ones that existed when the child started Year 10. Check which sixth form will accept the tier your child is entered for before the final entry deadline, not after results day.

igcse-tutors.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones UAE families ask for most, with the syllabus codes attached and a plain note on where marks go missing. Both boards appear, because the paper your child sits depends on the code the school entered, not on the subject's name.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The long structured questions carry method marks that disappear when working is not shown. Bearings, vectors, transformations, compound interest and histograms with unequal class widths account for a disproportionate share of lost marks. Extended and Higher candidates also lose marks to time, not to content, on the final two questions of the long paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606 / Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main Maths course by students heading for A Level Maths or IB HL Analysis and Approaches. Calculus arrives earlier than families expect, and the gap between a strong Extended grade and the opening weeks of this course is where most of the early panic comes from. Worth starting in the summer rather than in October.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: Unit conversion and prefix errors cost marks on every paper. Gradient and area-under-graph questions are reliably under-practised. The command terms matter: describe, explain, state and calculate each expect a different shape of answer, and a correct physics idea written as the wrong command term scores nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: Mole calculations, limiting reagents and percentage yield are where Extended candidates separate from Core. Ionic equations with state symbols, and the organic naming and mechanism questions, are the other two reliable losses. Electrolysis questions reward a drilled method rather than intuition.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · untiered at Pearson
subjects.description: The content feels learnable and then the data-response questions arrive. Marks go on describing a trend without quoting figures from the graph, on confusing osmosis and diffusion in the practical write-up, and on genetics crosses where the notation is right but the conclusion is not stated.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: A double or single award covering all three sciences, chosen by schools to free timetable space for the mandatory UAE subjects. Content per science is reduced, which parents read as easier. The papers still ask Extended-level reasoning, and the reduced teaching time means less practice, not less difficulty.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: The directed-writing task is marked on reading as much as on writing, and candidates who answer in their own voice rather than the required register lose half the available marks. The summary question has a fixed set of content points: finding fourteen of them beats writing beautifully about six.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The note-taking and summary exercises are technique, not vocabulary, and they respond faster to tutoring than any other paper on this list. The speaking component is separately assessed and is the part families forget exists until the week it is scheduled.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 / Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: The long evaluation question is where the grade is decided, and it needs a judgement with a reason, not a list of advantages and disadvantages. Diagram marks are given for correct axis labels and a labelled shift, which is the cheapest mark on the paper and the most often dropped.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Application marks require the answer to use the case study's business, not a generic firm. Students who revise definitions score the knowledge marks and stall in the low grades. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are a reliable source of recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory is learnable; the algorithm and pseudocode questions are not learnable by reading. Trace tables, logic gates and binary arithmetic reward weekly short practice. Students arriving from a different system often have programming fluency and no exam-pseudocode discipline at all.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 first language / 0544 foreign language)
subjects.description: An IGCSE Arabic entry is a different thing from the Arabic lesson the school must provide under the mandatory-subject rules, and families routinely confuse the two. The first-language and foreign-language syllabuses are separate courses with separate papers. KHDA requires schools to teach Arabic as a first language in separate classes from non-Arab groups.

igcse-tutors.regionsTitle: Where your child studies, and who signs off the school
igcse-tutors.regionsIntro: The emirate your family lives in decides which authority inspects the school, approves its fees and curriculum, and publishes anything you can read about it. For an IGCSE plan that changes what you can verify and who you ask. Every lesson we run is online, so the emirate changes the context, not the availability.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. In 2024-25 Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single group at 37% of the roll. KHDA publishes inspection reports you can read before enrolling.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by essentially none of the tutoring sites competing for this search. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort than Abu Dhabi island. Extended-tier science and Additional Mathematics cover is genuinely thinner in the local market, which is the practical argument for an online match rather than a drive-time one.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is approval of the course itself, not inspection alone, which is why a cross-emirate school move can change what is taught.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here, rather than an emirate-level authority. The British-curriculum cohort is small, so a Year 11 student needing a specific Pearson specification is unlikely to find a local specialist in that exact paper set.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision. Many families commute to schools in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, which pushes the realistic start time for a weekday session later than a Dubai family would plan for.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Returns zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this market, which tells you how little of this gets written down.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Federal Ministry of Education supervision, and the longest drive in the country to any tuition centre with a British-curriculum specialist on staff. East-coast families are the clearest case for one-to-one online delivery, because the alternative is ninety minutes of car for sixty minutes of teaching.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE entries in the country, and the widest spread of tier policy. Two schools a few kilometres apart can have very different thresholds for offering the Extended tier in Maths, so a transfer between them can change a child's grade ceiling without changing a single lesson.

Schools here answer to ADEK rather than KHDA, which changes where a parent looks for licensing and inspection information. It also means the staff-ethics position is explicit: an Abu Dhabi school's own teachers are barred from taking paid private lessons with their own enrolled students.

Fewer British-curriculum schools, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the regulator approves the curriculum and assessment methods as well as the fees. Families in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are under federal Ministry of Education supervision instead.

igcse-tutors.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named to describe the school system a UAE family works inside; IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation with, and no endorsement from, any school, group or authority named on this page.
igcse-tutors.modesIntro: Four ways UAE families use us, all of them one-to-one and all of them online over live video. The format does not change; what changes is how the hours are shaped and what the plan counts down to.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one against one specification
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with one tutor, working through the syllabus your child is actually entered for, in paper order. The tutor keeps a running list of topics not yet secure and the paper each one appears on. This is the format that suits Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, when there is still time to teach rather than only to revise.
bullets: One syllabus code, one tier, one tutor
Sixty or ninety minutes, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time
Topic tracker shared with the parent, not just the student
Past-paper questions chosen by paper number, not by textbook chapter

modes.title: Exam-series intensive, counted back from entry
modes.description: A compressed block of hours in the eight to twelve weeks before the papers, built backwards from the series your child is entered in. Full papers under timed conditions, marked against the published assessment structure, with the weakest paper getting the most hours. Suits a Year 11 student whose content is broadly covered but whose marks do not reflect it.
bullets: Planned from the final entry deadline and the exam window, not from a generic calendar
Two or three sessions a week during the run-in
Timed full papers, one per paper number in the entry
Separate technique work for a practical or alternative-to-practical paper

modes.title: Tier-change support, Core to Extended
modes.description: The hardest job on this list. Moving from Core to Extended, or Foundation to Higher, means teaching the extended content from scratch while the class continues at its own pace. It needs more weekly hours than a normal plan, it needs to start before the final entry deadline, and it needs an honest view of whether the move is realistic this year.
bullets: Diagnostic against the extended topics only, not the whole syllabus
A written week-by-week plan with a decision point before final entry
Higher weekly hours for a fixed period rather than indefinitely
A plain recommendation if the move should wait for a later series

modes.title: Mandatory UAE subjects stream
modes.description: Support in Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, which Dubai private schools must deliver whatever international curriculum they are licensed for. These are assessed by the school rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so the work is comprehension, vocabulary and confidence in the school's own set material. KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is prohibited, so a tutor works from what the school teaches.
bullets: Separate streams for first-language and additional-language Arabic, as KHDA requires schools to organise them
Islamic Education taught in the language the school uses for the child's group
Social Studies support aimed at the school's own assessments
No parallel syllabus and no substitute material

sections.heading: What a parent is actually asking for when they search for IGCSE tutors in the UAE
paragraphs: The short answer: a tutor who teaches one named specification, to one tier, for one exam series, at a time a Gulf school day leaves free. IGCSE tutors in the UAE are not interchangeable, because the qualification is not one thing. Two children in neighbouring villas can both be sitting Year 11 Chemistry and be sitting different papers, on different timetables, with different grade ceilings. The match is made on the code, not on the subject name.

That is the whole reason this page leads with the system rather than with the service. A UAE family has four moving parts that a UK family mostly does not: an emirate authority that licenses the school and approves what it teaches, a set of mandatory UAE subjects taking timetable space alongside the IGCSE block, a school that may enter for either board or for both, and a federal equivalency process waiting at the end that counts some subjects and not others. Each of those changes what tutoring should be aimed at.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one online IGCSE tuition. Lessons run over live video with screen-sharing and a shared whiteboard, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that is a service offered only in India. The honest case for the online format is availability rather than convenience. A Year 11 student needing Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics in Fujairah has a local specialist pool of roughly nobody, and a national or international one measured in dozens.

The rest of this page is organised the way the decision actually gets made. Which board, then which tier, then what the ministry will count, then what the school has to teach alongside it, then who regulates the school, then the calendar, then the money, then the format, then the permit question, then the line on coursework. If you only read one section, read the tier one, because it is the only decision on the list with a deadline attached and a grade ceiling behind it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out which one before you book an hour
paragraphs: Ask the school's exams officer, in writing, for the syllabus or specification code on this year's entry for each subject. Not the subject name, not the textbook, the code. Cambridge International uses four digits: 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0500 First Language English. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses a letter-number format: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics, 4EA1 English Language A. One email saves a term of drilling the wrong paper.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge tiers Mathematics and the single sciences into Core and Extended paper sets; Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher and leaves the single sciences untiered. Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on the centre; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Cambridge grades most syllabuses A* to G, with a 9 to 1 version used where a centre enters for it; Pearson International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout.

Mixed entries are common in the Emirates and are the source of most of the confusion we see. A school may enter for Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Maths, or move boards between cohorts, which leaves a family with two timetables, two sets of past papers and two mark-scheme styles for one child. Nothing is wrong when that happens, but a tutor who assumes one board will set the wrong homework with total confidence for weeks.

Verify against the board's own site for the year of entry, never last year's document. Cambridge publishes syllabuses at cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson publishes specifications and timetables at qualifications.pearson.com. We reference those pages and link to them; we do not supply copies of syllabuses, past papers or mark schemes, because those are the boards' copyright material and the boards distribute them through centres.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: On Cambridge Maths and the single sciences, the Core papers do not carry the full grade range. The top grades are only available on the Extended paper set. Pearson does the same thing with different words: Mathematics A Foundation tier does not reach the grades Higher tier does. This is the only decision in a UAE IGCSE plan that permanently limits an outcome, and it is made by the school, often provisionally in Year 10 and confirmed at final entry in Year 11.

Parents are rarely told it in those terms. The conversation usually arrives as reassurance about the right level for the child, which is often correct and sometimes just easier. The question worth asking, in writing, is simple: which grade range does this entry allow, and what would my child need to show to be entered on the other tier? A school that answers that clearly is a school worth trusting on the rest.

Then decide against the post-16 plan rather than against this year's comfort. A Level, IB Higher Level and some BTEC routes have subject prerequisites that a Core-tier grade can fail to meet even when the grade itself looks respectable. The British track to MoE equivalency also requires post-16 study, so the tier decision quietly shapes whether that route stays open. Dubai is adding seven private schools for 2026-27, which widens post-16 choice and makes the prerequisite question more worth checking, not less.

If a tier move is the goal, the work is a specific job with a deadline. The extended topics have to be taught from scratch while the class carries on, the final entry deadline is the hard stop, and the honest answer is sometimes that a later series is the better plan. Tutoring that pretends otherwise sells hours. IGCSE Core and Extended decisions are the one place where we would rather talk a family out of a plan than take the booking.

sections.heading: The five-subject rule: MoE equivalency for an IGCSE student
paragraphs: MoE equivalency is the federal process that recognises a foreign school certificate in the UAE, and it is the step families discover late. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus post-16 study: one subject at Advanced Level with a grade no less than E, or two subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects, even though they are compulsory at school and even though a child may have worked hard for a good grade in them. That means a nine-subject IGCSE programme can leave a thinner margin than it looks like it does once two of those subjects come out of the count. Plan the five before Year 11, not after results.

Get this from the ministry rather than from a tutoring website. One competitor page currently ranking for this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. We are not in a position to perform, guarantee or accelerate equivalency and we do not claim to; what we can do is point you at moe.gov.ae and the emirate attestation channel, and make sure the five subjects your child is relying on are the five being taught properly.

One deliberate gap in the table below: there is no IB points figure in it. No IB equivalency threshold has been read on a ministry source we can cite, so publishing one would be guessing with your child's university application. If a site gives you a number for that, ask where it came from. Equivalency is a regulatory process and tutoring is not a requirement for it; anyone who tells you otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside nine IGCSEs
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The federal position behind that is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. So these subjects are not an optional extra and not a regional nicety.

They cost timetable space, which is the part that touches an IGCSE plan directly. A school fitting mandatory subjects around nine IGCSEs has less contact time per subject than the brochure implies, and that is one reason schools choose Coordinated or Combined Sciences over three separate sciences. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab groups are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA.

That shapes what an IGCSE Arabic tutor can usefully do. For mandatory subjects, KHDA states that using any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited, so the work is comprehension, vocabulary and confidence in the school's own material, not a parallel course. An IGCSE Arabic entry under Cambridge 0508 or 0544 is a separate, externally examined qualification, and families regularly confuse the two. KHDA mandatory subjects and an Arabic IGCSE are different projects.

sections.heading: Which authority signs off your child's school, and what you can look up
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and they do not all do the same job. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The difference that matters to a parent is the depth of the remit. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate, not only inspection. Dubai's position is published in a different way: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Use what the regulator publishes before you use what a school says about itself. Inspection reports, licensing status and fee positions are the checkable facts in this market, and they are free. Abu Dhabi adds one more: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that rule should be in a parent's head the moment a teacher offers evening lessons.

What none of these bodies does is endorse a tutoring provider. IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Any provider describing its individual tutors as approved by KHDA is describing something that does not exist in that form: the KHDA permit in this space is an educational services permit issued to training institutes with premises, which is a different thing entirely.

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam series counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, so here is one. The important date is not the exam. It is the final entry deadline, which fixes the subject list and the tier, and which sits months earlier. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series make the gap plain: final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades 27 February 2027, the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, results reach Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and also publishes key dates for a March series, which is not offered at every centre. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November; the final November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

One more Cambridge detail that costs families real marks. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A parent downloading a timetable from a search result may be downloading another zone's. Get the timetable from your school's exams officer.

Two cautions on dates. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any date can be revised and the live official timetable is the only version to plan from. And no IB exam-session date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; for an actual date, ask the school's IB coordinator. The IGCSE exam series dates below are from the boards' own published documents, read in October 2026.

sections.heading: What IGCSE support actually costs in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency a UAE family transacts in. So here are IGCSE tutor rates in AED, with the provider who published each figure named and the date they were read. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a free trial lesson and then a quote against the plan, because an hourly number without a plan tells a parent nothing useful.

The bands are wide for a reason. At the bottom, providers advertise from AED 45 to AED 65 and from AED 33 to AED 52 an hour, which buys homework supervision rather than paper-by-paper exam technique. In the middle, a qualified subject tutor working online against a named specification sits around AED 150 to AED 300; one agency quotes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one runs higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, because travel time sits inside the rate.

Monthly shapes are worth knowing before you compare hourly numbers. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Divide any package by the number of hours before deciding it is cheaper.

Put the figure in context rather than in isolation. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, so a tutoring decision is not competing with a fee increase this year. Against that, a two-year IGCSE programme with weekly support in two subjects is a four-figure annual commitment, and it deserves the same scrutiny as a school fee: what is the plan, which paper is it aimed at, and what will tell us in six weeks whether it is working.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a group class: how UAE families decide
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market here and the question deserves a real answer. An in-home tutor in Dubai or Abu Dhabi charges roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with travel inside that rate, and the pool a family can choose from is whoever will drive to their community at the hour they want. That pool shrinks fast once the requirement gets specific: Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 at 7pm in Al Ain, or Pearson 4PM1 anywhere north of Sharjah.

Travel also decides the timetable more than families expect. A 5pm start on a weekday in Dubai means a tutor crossing the city in the worst hour of the day, which is paid for either in the rate or in a later start. A ninety-minute round trip for a sixty-minute lesson is a poor trade for everyone in it, and it is the reason in-home sessions cluster into two-hour blocks that suit the logistics rather than the attention span of a fifteen-year-old.

IB Gram delivers online IGCSE tuition, one-to-one over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses in the Emirates; home visits are an India-only service. The argument for that is not cost. It is that the match is made on the specification rather than on the map, so a family in Fujairah and a family in Jumeirah draw from the same pool of subject specialists, and a 7pm slot is genuinely 7pm rather than 7pm plus traffic.

Group classes and tuition centres have their place, with two conditions. A small group only works if everyone in it sits the same board and the same tier, otherwise half the room is being taught the wrong paper. And a centre with premises and staff in Dubai is a regulated business that needs an educational services permit for a training institute, which is worth asking about before paying a term in advance. Trying the school's own intervention sessions first costs nothing.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, which is the single most under-written fact in this market. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is public. MoHRE's own service is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified, including the figure that circulates on forums.

Two conditions matter more than the permit itself. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. So the offer that sounds best to a worried parent, the child's own subject teacher taking paid evening lessons, is the one to decline. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording.

A tutoring business with premises is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram is an independent online tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no permit of that kind, and does not describe itself as approved by any authority named here.
