sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE courses carry less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but they carry some, and UAE families are shown offers that cross the line. A tutor teaches, explains, models a method, reviews a draft and gives feedback the student then acts on. A tutor does not finish a piece of coursework on a student's behalf, does not rewrite a draft into a submission, and does not supply text to be handed in. One provider ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

Feedback that stays on the right side of the line looks specific and unglamorous. Point at the criterion the work is being marked against, name what is missing, give an example from a different context, and send the student away to write it. Mark a timed paper and hand back the mark scheme's logic rather than the answer. Ask the question the examiner would ask. None of that is as satisfying to buy as a finished document, and all of it is the only version that survives a school's academic-honesty check.

The same discipline applies to materials. We reference IGCSE syllabuses, specifications, past papers and mark schemes and link to the boards' own pages at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com; we do not host or distribute copies. Those documents are the boards' copyright and they reach students through centres. A tutor offering a private archive of unreleased material is offering a problem, and in the worst case an exposure that lands on the candidate.

Examiner claims deserve the same scepticism. Nobody should describe a tutor as a current IB or Cambridge examiner without evidence, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content. The useful question for a parent is narrower and more answerable: has this tutor taught this specification, at this tier, through a full exam series, and can they talk about the paper by number?

process.title: Send us the code, the tier and the series
process.description: The first message should carry four things: the syllabus or specification code for each subject, the tier your child is entered on, the exam series the entry is in, and the two or three evening windows that genuinely work on Gulf Standard Time. If you do not have the codes yet, email the exams officer first; it is one email and it changes everything downstream.

process.title: We check who is genuinely free, and say so if nobody is
process.description: We look for a tutor who has taught that exact specification at that tier through a full series, and who is free in your window. If no UAE-based specialist covers a niche paper set, we say that in plain words and offer an India-based specialist in the same online format rather than quietly substituting a generalist. The coverage answer comes before the invoice.

process.title: A free trial lesson, then you decide
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, at no charge, with no card details taken and nothing owed if you stop there. Sit in on it if you want to. The point is to see whether the tutor can talk about the actual papers, diagnose the gaps and hold a fifteen-year-old's attention for an hour over video. If any of those is missing, there is no second lesson.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards from the entry deadline
process.description: After the trial, a short written plan: which topics, in which order, against which paper number, with the final entry deadline and the exam window marked on it. If the aim is a tier move, the plan carries a decision point before final entry and an honest view of whether a later series is the better bet. Plans get revised; unwritten plans get forgotten.

process.title: Review every fortnight, and change the tutor if it is not working
process.description: Every two weeks you get the topic tracker and a straight answer on progress, measured against marked work rather than impressions. If the tutor is not the right fit we change them, and if more hours will not fix the problem we say that too. Scheduling moves around Ramadan, Eid and the exam calendar without penalty.

whyPoints.title: Matched by specification, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Your child is entered for 0620 or for 4CH1, on Core or Extended, in a specific series. We match on those facts, because a Chemistry tutor who has never seen the other board's Paper 4 will teach confidently and aim at the wrong target. Send the code and the tier and the match gets narrower and more useful.

whyPoints.title: Online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Every lesson runs over live video with screen-sharing and a shared whiteboard, scheduled around the school day, the school run and the mandatory-subject periods. There are no home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. Emirate and community change the context on this page, not the availability of a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage, including when the answer is no
whyPoints.description: Specialist cover for Additional Mathematics, Further Pure, Computer Science and first-language Arabic is genuinely thin in some emirates. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. We tell you before you pay whether a UAE-based specialist is available, what the alternative is, and what it costs.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory statement on this page comes from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and names where to check it. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or partnership from any of them and claims none. Where a fact could not be verified, such as an IB session date or a fine amount, this page says so instead of guessing.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line stated in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has written. Nobody finishes a piece of coursework for a candidate, rewrites a draft into a submission or supplies text to hand in. We do not host copies of board syllabuses, past papers or mark schemes, and we link to the boards' own pages instead.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the syllabus or specification code on this year's entry for each subject. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0625 for Physics. Pearson International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. The subject name alone does not tell you, and the textbook on the shelf is not proof, because schools change boards between cohorts and sometimes enter for different boards in different subjects. Get it in writing before you book tutoring, because the two boards have different papers, different tier structures and different timetables for subjects that share a title.

faqs.question: My daughter has been placed on the Core tier in Maths. Does that close off A Level?
faqs.answer: It can, and that is the honest answer. On Cambridge Mathematics 0580 the Core paper set does not carry the full grade range, so the top grades are only available on Extended. Many sixth forms set a prerequisite grade for A Level Maths or IB Higher Level Analysis and Approaches that a Core entry cannot reach. Ask the school two questions in writing: which grade range this entry allows, and what your daughter would need to show to be entered on Extended. Then ask the sixth form you are aiming at what grade it requires. Decide against the post-16 plan rather than against this year's comfort level.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published rule on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates, each at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus post-16 study: one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One tutoring site currently ranking for this market states six subjects, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae and through your emirate's attestation channel before you build a subject plan around it. IB Gram does not perform, accelerate or guarantee equivalency; we can only point you at the official source.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE in Arabic count towards the five subjects the ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. The published equivalency rule states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. They remain compulsory at school under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements, and a good grade in either is worth having, but neither fills one of the five slots. The practical consequence is that a nine-subject programme has a thinner margin than it appears to once those two come out of the count. Work out which five subjects are carrying the requirement before Year 11 rather than after results day, and confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae because requirements are revised.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable my child follows differ from the one I downloaded?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A timetable found through a search result may well belong to another zone. Ask your school's exams officer for the version that applies to your centre, and plan the revision run-in from that document rather than from anything downloaded independently.

faqs.question: When do final IGCSE entries have to be submitted, and who submits them?
faqs.answer: The school submits them, and the deadline sits months before the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. That deadline fixes the subject list and the tier, which is why a tier change requested in January is a school-level problem rather than a simple administrative edit. Ask your exams officer for the entry deadline for your child's series at the start of the academic year, write it on the calendar, and treat it as the real deadline rather than the exam date.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell me about IGCSE teaching at that school?
faqs.answer: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it publishes inspection reports you can read before enrolling. A rating is a whole-school judgement, so it tells you about leadership, teaching quality and outcomes across the school rather than about one department. Read the body of the report instead of the headline band, and look for what it says about the secondary phase and about the subjects your child will take. For Abu Dhabi and Al Ain the equivalent information sits with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there.

faqs.question: Abu Dhabi schools answer to ADEK rather than KHDA. Does that change an IGCSE plan?
faqs.answer: It changes where you look and one rule you should know. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, so licensing and inspection information comes from adek.gov.ae rather than from KHDA. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff also prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The IGCSE itself is unchanged, since the board sets the syllabus and the papers. Treat the ethics rule as press-reported and check the current ADEK document.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do UAE students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Extended-tier Mathematics, Chemistry and Physics come up most, followed by First Language English and Additional Mathematics. The pattern is not random. Those are the subjects where marks depend on a drilled method rather than on recall: mole calculations and ionic equations, unit conversion and graph gradients, shown working on long structured questions, and the directed-writing task that is marked on reading as much as on writing. Arabic also comes up often, usually because a family has confused the mandatory school subject with an IGCSE Arabic entry under Cambridge 0508 or 0544, which are separate courses with separate papers.

faqs.question: My son wants to sit two IGCSEs as a private candidate. How does that work here?
faqs.answer: Private candidate entries are made through a registered exam centre rather than directly with the board, so the first step is finding a centre in your emirate that accepts external candidates for the subjects and series you want. Entry deadlines are the centre's deadlines and they sit months before the papers, so start early. Subjects with a practical component need particular care, because the centre has to be able to offer either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Ask the centre which option it runs before entering, and confirm the current arrangements on the board's own website.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IGCSE grades 9 to 1 and A* to G on one certificate?
faqs.answer: They are two grading scales used by two different arrangements. Cambridge grades most IGCSE syllabuses A* to G, with a 9 to 1 version used where a centre enters for it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 throughout. That is why two siblings in the same family, or two subjects for the same child, can come back on different scales with nothing wrong. When a university or an employer asks for a comparison, use the board's own published equivalence rather than a conversion table from a tutoring site, and keep both certificates for any attestation or equivalency application.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE tutors in the UAE charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates, as published by providers and read in October 2026: budget online tutoring advertised from AED 45 to 65 and from AED 33 to 52 an hour; a qualified subject tutor working online around AED 150 to 300, with one agency quoting IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate; specialist exam-year support AED 200 to 450 and above; premium named tutors advertised at AED 650. Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are the market's numbers, not IB Gram's; our own route is a free trial lesson and then a quote against the written plan.

faqs.question: Who issues the permit a private tutor must hold in the UAE, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: MoHRE issues it. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing and lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold a current permit. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: We move from Dubai to Sharjah in the summer. Will the IGCSE course carry over?
faqs.answer: The qualification carries over; the delivery may not. The board sets the syllabus, so Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 is the same course in both emirates. What changes is the regulator and what it approves: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, while KHDA oversees quality in Dubai. Ask the receiving school three questions: which board and code it enters for in each subject, which tier it will place your child on, and whether the subject options you need are timetabled. Tier is the one that can change a grade ceiling.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE exam series in March, and should we enter for it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge publishes key dates for a March series alongside its June and November series, and it is not offered at every centre. For the March 2027 series the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and results to Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November. Whether a March entry suits your child depends on whether the content will genuinely be finished by early February, and on what your centre actually offers, so ask the exams officer before planning around it.

faqs.question: How should Ramadan change an IGCSE revision plan?
faqs.answer: Shift the hours rather than cutting them. Shortened school days, fasting and a changed sleep pattern make a 4pm session the worst slot of the day for most teenagers during Ramadan, and a post-Iftar slot the best. Eid then removes teaching days from the week either side. Build the plan around that in advance: front-load new content into the weeks before, use Ramadan for consolidation and timed practice at a later hour, and keep the final entry deadline and the exam window in view. Online lessons move hour to hour without anyone's travel plans having to change.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the practical paper or the alternative to practical?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are two different jobs. Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre offers; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards a specific written technique: reading apparatus diagrams, describing a method precisely, identifying sources of error and processing a results table. That is coachable over video with shared diagrams and real past-paper questions. A hands-on practical test needs lab time at school, so tutoring there focuses on method, recording and the examiner's expectations rather than on manipulation.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our address in the UAE, or are lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons are online. Every session is one-to-one over live video with screen-sharing and a shared whiteboard, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not arrange visits to addresses anywhere in the Emirates; that is a service offered only in India. The reason is availability rather than cost. Matching on the specification instead of on the map means a family in Fujairah, Al Ain or Umm Al Quwain draws from the same pool of subject specialists as a family in Dubai, and an evening slot stays at the time it was booked rather than moving with the traffic.

igcse-tutors.closingHeading: Start with the code, the tier and the deadline
igcse-tutors.closingBody: If you take three things from this page, take these. Email the exams officer for the syllabus code and the tier on this year's entry, because everything else follows from those two facts. Write the final entry deadline on the calendar, because it fixes the tier months before the paper. And check the five subjects carrying your child's MoE equivalency, remembering that Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count. When you have those, send them to us. We will tell you honestly who is free in that exact paper set, arrange a free trial lesson with no card details taken, and write a plan counted backwards from the deadline.

intro.heading: Ras Al Khaimah is inspected by the Ministry of Education, and that changes how you choose support
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai choosing a tutor starts from a KHDA band. A parent in Abu Dhabi starts from an ADEK report. In Ras Al Khaimah the regulator is the federal Ministry of Education, which inspects private schools across the northern emirates against the UAE school inspection framework. The practical difference is not the logo on the cover. It is that the report you are handed grades attainment and progress as two separate things, subject by subject and phase by phase, and almost no parent is shown how to read that grid. Once you can read it, you stop buying general tuition and start buying the one thing the report already told you is missing.

The framework rests on six performance standards, and judgements are issued on a six-point scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Standard one, students' achievement, is the one that matters for tuition decisions: it reports attainment against the curriculum standard and progress over time, broken out for Islamic Education, Arabic, English, mathematics and science, and separated by phase. A secondary phase showing Good attainment with only Acceptable progress in mathematics is not a vague worry. It is a specific diagnosis, and it calls for harder questions and command-term precision rather than another pass through content the class has already covered.

The second thing shaping tuition here is supply. Ras Al Khaimah has a compact private-school set concentrated around Al Nakheel, Khuzam, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and the number of teachers in the emirate holding a Chemistry HL or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL specialism is small. Families solve this in one of three ways: they accept a generalist, they drive to Sharjah or Dubai after school, or they go online. The drive is the expensive option. Ninety minutes each way down the E311 turns a one-hour lesson into most of an evening, and it still limits you to whoever has a free slot at the far end.

So the model here is plain. Lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Ras Al Khaimah address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because the phrase families type into Google is a home-tutor phrase and they deserve a straight answer rather than a form. What online matching buys you is the thing distance was costing you: a Chemistry HL tutor in the northern emirates stops being a question of who lives nearby and becomes a question of who has taught the paper.

This page is written for the families who actually live here. Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab households running a southern school route. Al Nakheel, Khuzam and Al Dhait families whose evenings are already full. Al Marjan Island and Al Rams parents with the longest school runs in the emirate. Diploma students in a single-cohort year group, Year 10 and 11 candidates sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers, MYP 5 students stepping into DP, and private candidates entering through a centre elsewhere in the UAE. Below you will find the AED rates the market actually charges, the exam year counted backwards, the internal assessment criteria with their mark allocations, the academic-honesty line a tutor must not cross, and what the Ministry of Education asks for at equivalency.
bullets: Lessons are live online, one to one. No tutor is sent to a Ras Al Khaimah address; home visits run only in India.
Market rates: qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, visiting tutors AED 180-500, on figures published by Unitors, EdFlik and Bestimate.
Inspection reports grade attainment and progress separately, by subject and by phase. That grid is the cheapest diagnostic you own.
Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit issued through MoHRE, and the permit itself is free of charge.

ras-al-khaimah.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah families meet the IB in a narrower band than Dubai families do, so the programme you are in shapes the help that is useful. Here is what each stage assesses, and what it means specifically in a small emirate where one school may be the only provider of a programme.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Six transdisciplinary themes, no external examinations, and assessment built from teacher observation, portfolios and the Year 6 exhibition. Reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method in writing are the three things that carry forward. Tuition at this stage is rarely about a syllabus and usually about one of those three.
programmes.countryNote: PYP provision in the emirate is limited to a small number of campuses, so many Ras Al Khaimah children arrive into MYP from a British or Indian primary instead. The gap that shows up is not content. It is the shift to criterion-referenced marking, where a child who has always been told the answer is right is suddenly marked on the reasoning.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale, plus the personal project in MYP 5. Criterion levels are not percentages and do not convert tidily into them, which is the single most common source of confusion in a parent meeting. The personal project carries criteria A Planning, B Applying skills and C Reflecting, eight marks each.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 in Ras Al Khaimah often sits alongside an IGCSE decision: some students stay with MYP eAssessment, others transfer into a Cambridge or Pearson Year 10 at a city-side campus. Tutoring that treats the two as interchangeable wastes a term. The criteria reward reflection and process; IGCSE papers reward timed accuracy on a published mark scheme.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The total is 45 points, including up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE matrix, and 24 points is the floor for the diploma with conditions on grade spread, CAS completion and no E in TOK or EE. HL subjects carry the weight of the final score.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma cohorts here are small, which means the option blocks are narrow and a student can be timetabled into Applications and Interpretation when their university target expects Analysis and Approaches. A Maths AA tutor in Mina Al Arab is a common request for exactly this reason. Check the route in Year 11, because by the second term of Year 12 switching HL maths is no longer realistic.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses taken alongside a career-related study, with a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development strand. It is assessed partly by the IB and partly by the career-related qualification provider, so the transcript looks different from a diploma transcript.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is rare across the northern emirates, and the recurring problem is paperwork rather than teaching. Families assume equivalency treats a CP transcript like a full diploma. Ask the Ministry of Education what it needs for your child's specific combination before Year 13, not after results, and keep the career-related provider's certification in the same file as the IB transcript.

ras-al-khaimah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Ras Al Khaimah students ask for most, with the assessment structure that decides the grade. Weightings below follow the current guides, including the sciences model first assessed in 2025, where Paper 3 no longer exists and the internal assessment is a single Scientific Investigation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: HL sits Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 30% each and Paper 3 at 20%, with the 20-mark exploration making the final 20%. Paper 3's two long investigations are where prepared students still lose marks, because the question rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. SL drops Paper 3 and weights both papers at 40%.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same paper architecture as AA, different content: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, and at HL graph theory and Markov chains. Marks go in interpretation rather than manipulation, so a student who can run the calculator routine but cannot say what the output means caps out around a 4 or 5.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide Paper 1 is 36%, combining multiple choice with a data-based section, Paper 2 is 44%, and the Scientific Investigation is 20%. The predictable losses are in uncertainty treatment, graph gradients with units, and explanation questions where a correct equation earns nothing without the physical reasoning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics account for most of the difference between a 5 and a 7. The Scientific Investigation is 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, capped at 3,000 words, and a weak research design question cannot be rescued by good data later.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of terminology plus command-term discipline. Students who revise by rereading notes stall; students who answer past-paper questions against the mark scheme move. The current guide's unifying themes mean questions increasingly cross topics, so single-topic revision no longer matches the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: SL weights Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40% and the portfolio at 30%. HL adds Paper 3, the quantitative and policy paper, and reweights the portfolio to 20%. The portfolio is three commentaries of 800 words each, 14 marks apiece, and diagram marks are the easiest marks on the course to drop.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis is 35%, Paper 2 comparative essay 35% at SL, and the individual oral carries 40 marks. HL adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL essay at 20% and reweights the rest. The oral fails most often on the global issue being too broad to evidence in ten minutes.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Relevant to many Ras Al Khaimah students who use English as an additional language. Reading and listening comprehension, a writing task judged on language, message and conceptual understanding, and an individual oral built on a visual stimulus at SL or a literary extract at HL. Register, not vocabulary volume, is what separates the top bands.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a source paper on a prescribed subject, Paper 2 covers world history topics, and HL Paper 3 is a regional depth paper worth 35%. The IA is a 2,200-word investigation marked out of 25, split across source evaluation, the investigation itself and a reflection on method.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic can be taken as a Group 1 or Group 2 subject, and in the UAE it also sits inside a Ministry of Education requirement that runs alongside the IB. Students who switch from MoE Arabic streams into Arabic B often find the vocabulary familiar and the assessment conventions entirely new, which is a tutoring problem, not an ability problem.

ras-al-khaimah.igcseSubjectsIntro: Most Ras Al Khaimah secondary students sit Cambridge or Pearson papers rather than MYP eAssessment, and the first question in any session is which specification the centre entered them for. Codes matter: the same subject name maps to different papers, different tiering and different practical arrangements depending on the board.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge / 4MA1 Pearson)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: From the 2025 series Cambridge splits by calculator use: Extended sits Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 with a calculator, at 50% each. Pearson 4MA1 keeps two calculator papers. An IGCSE maths tutor in Al Nakheel will ask for the paper numbers on the entry sheet before anything else.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: The bridge subject for students heading to Analysis and Approaches or A-Level maths. Calculus, trigonometric identities and series arrive a year early. Taken well it removes the worst of the Year 12 shock; taken badly it produces a weak grade on the transcript for no gain.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Extended candidates sit Paper 2 at 30%, Paper 4 at 50%, and either the Paper 5 practical test or Paper 6 alternative to practical at 20%. Electricity and the practical paper are where the marks actually go, and alternative-to-practical technique is teachable in a handful of sessions.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade, followed by qualitative analysis in the practical paper. Students arrive able to recite the ionic tests and unable to rearrange a mole equation under time pressure, so sessions are built around calculation drills with the mark scheme open.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Extended candidates need definitions precise enough to earn the mark and data-handling practice for the structured questions. The common pattern is strong recall with weak command-term response: describe, explain and suggest each want a different shape of answer.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: One block of three sciences worth two grades. Useful for a crowded timetable in a small school, harder than it looks for revision, because the three papers interleave content and students revise one science at a time. Scheduling the revision is half the work.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English Language A (4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and composition reward structure and control rather than vocabulary display. The reading passages need annotation technique under timing. Most grade movement comes from teaching a planning routine the student can execute in four minutes.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Relevant where English is the school language but not the home language. Grades turn on exercise-specific technique: note-making, summary word limits, and the email and report formats the mark scheme expects. The speaking component differs between 0510 and 0511, so check which the centre entered.

ras-al-khaimah.regionsTitle: Districts we teach across Ras Al Khaimah
ras-al-khaimah.regionsIntro: Distance decides nothing about who teaches your child, but it decides a great deal about what time a lesson can start. These notes are about school runs, evening traffic on the Corniche and the realistic window for a weekday session in each part of the emirate.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The commercial core, close to the Corniche and the main city-side campuses. Short school runs mean a 4pm start is realistic here, which is the best slot of the day for a tired Year 11 student. Evening congestion along the Corniche is the only real constraint.

regions.name: Al Hamra and Al Hamra Village
regions.note: The gated community on the southern coast, with RAK Academy's Al Hamra campuses alongside it. Diploma families here often ask for an IB Diploma tutor in Al Hamra and find the local specialist pool thin at Higher Level. The 25 to 30 minute run into the city is what makes an online slot worth having.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab and Hayat Island
regions.note: Villas and newer apartment stock between the city and Al Hamra, split between a northern and a southern school route. Families here commonly run two different drop-offs, so the useful session time is after 5pm once both children are home.

regions.name: Al Dhait North and South
regions.note: Large inland residential plots behind the Corniche, with a short hop to the city-side campuses. Good 4pm to 6pm availability on weekdays, and the district where sibling bookings in different subjects are most common.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Inland district on the city side, close to several of the emirate's long-established campuses. Students here are usually on a British or Indian curriculum, so IGCSE tuition in Ras Al Khaimah is requested from this district more than Diploma support.

regions.name: Al Mairid and Al Uraibi
regions.note: Older districts between Khuzam and the old town near Julphar. A dense school-run corridor in the afternoon, which argues for a later start rather than an earlier one during the exam term.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed islands with newer apartments and hotel development, and no school on the island itself. Every family here drives, usually south to Al Hamra or north into the city, so evening sessions from 6pm onwards work better than afternoon ones.

regions.name: Al Rams, Sha'am and the northern strip
regions.note: The coastal villages running north towards the Omani border, with the longest school runs in the emirate. An online slot is often the only way to add a second weekly session in exam term without a second round trip.

regions.name: Digdaga, Al Ghail and the inland belt
regions.note: Agricultural and industrial districts inland, 40 minutes or more from the city campuses. Weekend blocks and later weekday slots are the practical pattern here, particularly for Year 13 students working to coursework deadlines.

schoolClusters.city: Al Hamra and the southern coast
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's IB and British provision concentrates on this side, which is why Diploma requests cluster here. Option blocks in a small cohort are narrow, so a student's third HL is often the one with no in-school specialist behind it.

sections.heading: Who inspects a Ras Al Khaimah school, and what the report actually grades
paragraphs: Dubai schools are inspected by KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, and Sharjah by SPEA. Ras Al Khaimah, along with Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain, sits with the federal Ministry of Education. A Ministry of Education school inspection in the northern emirates uses the national framework, and the report that lands with parents is organised around six performance standards with a judgement attached to each.

The reason this matters to a tutoring decision is structural. Standard one, students' achievement, is reported as two distinct things: attainment, meaning how far students are against the curriculum standard, and progress, meaning how far they have moved. Those two judgements are issued separately for each phase and broken out by subject. Two schools both labelled Good can hide completely different problems, and a school with Good attainment and Acceptable progress in secondary mathematics is telling you that capable students are not being stretched.

The other five standards are not decoration either. Standard three covers teaching and assessment, including challenge for higher attainers, which is the usual explanation when a bright student sits at a 5 for two terms. Standard four covers curriculum, including the option blocks available at Diploma level, which in a small emirate is often the reason a student ends up in the wrong maths route. Standard five covers care, guidance and support, including careers guidance, and thin careers guidance is why an equivalency or EmSAT requirement arrives as a surprise in Year 13.

Read your report with a pen before you book anything. Find the subject grid, note where attainment and progress diverge, read the recommendations at the back, and ask the school which of the previous recommendations are still open. That costs nothing and it narrows the brief from help with maths to something a tutor can actually plan a term around.

sections.heading: The six judgements, from Outstanding to Very Weak, and what to ask next
paragraphs: The scale runs Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak, Very Weak. Parents treat it as a league position. Inspectors use it as a description of provision against a defined standard, and the difference matters because the band is awarded at several levels: whole school, phase and subject. A whole-school Good can contain an Outstanding primary phase and an Acceptable secondary mathematics judgement in the same document.

Acceptable is the point most misread. It does not mean failing; it means the minimum expected standard is met, with weaknesses recorded in the body of the report. Those recorded weaknesses are the useful part, because they are specific and they name subjects and phases. Weak and Very Weak trigger improvement planning and closer monitoring, and in that situation the question to ask is not whether to move school but what the action plan says for your child's subject and phase this year.

What you do with the band depends on the direction of travel more than the letter. A school that has moved from Acceptable to Good in three years is managing something; one that has slipped the other way is losing something, often staff. Ask which recommendations from the last report remain open, ask how many teachers in your child's department are new this year, and ask to see the subject-level judgements rather than the headline. Schools that answer those three questions straightforwardly are usually the ones improving. One more test is worth applying: compare the band awarded to your child's phase with the band awarded to the subject they are weakest in. Where the phase judgement is higher than the subject judgement, the school is carrying that department rather than fixing it, and outside support in that one subject is a reasonable response for the exam year in front of you.
bullets: The band is awarded at whole-school, phase and subject level; read all three before drawing a conclusion.
Recommendations at the back of the report are the most actionable text in it.

A new head of department in the exam year is a legitimate reason to add outside support.

sections.heading: Attainment is not progress: the two columns parents misread
paragraphs: Every tutoring brief we receive from the northern emirates says one of two things: the grade is low, or the grade has stopped moving. Those are different problems with different fixes, and the inspection grid already distinguishes them. Attainment answers where the student is. Progress answers whether they are moving. A tutor who treats both the same way wastes the first month.

Take the most common pattern in a well-regarded school: attainment Good, progress Acceptable. The cohort arrived strong and has coasted. The content is largely there, so reteaching it is pointless. What is missing is difficulty: the harder past-paper variants, the command-term discipline that separates describe from explain, and the Paper 3 style question that wants sustained reasoning. The work is not more content, it is harder questions marked honestly.

The reverse pattern, attainment Acceptable with progress Good, means real teaching gains from a low base. Here content gaps from earlier years are the binding constraint, and the fix is unglamorous: indices, rearranging formulae, moles, significant figures, the prerequisites nobody wants to revisit in Year 12. Skip that and every new topic lands on sand.

Then there is the single-subject anomaly, where one subject sits lower than everything around it. That is usually departmental rather than individual, and often a staffing story. In that case the published syllabus becomes the plan: the tutor works through it in sequence and does not assume in-class coverage. If your report carries no subject detail at all, which happens with smaller or newer schools, use a full past paper under timed conditions as the diagnostic instead. One marked paper tells you more than a term of effort grades.

sections.heading: Why postcode matching fails in the northern emirates
paragraphs: In Dubai, hiring by proximity is inefficient. In Ras Al Khaimah it is a real constraint on what your child can be taught. The emirate's private secondary provision is compact, and the pool of teachers holding a Higher Level specialism in Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Economics is correspondingly small. Ask for a Chemistry HL tutor in the northern emirates on a proximity basis and the honest answer is that you are choosing from a handful of people, most of whom are already teaching full timetables.

That pressure produces three familiar outcomes. The first is the generalist: a capable science teacher covering Chemistry HL from a Year 11 knowledge base, which works until the organic mechanisms arrive. The second is the commute: a weekly drive to Sharjah or Dubai, ninety minutes each way on the E311 in term-time traffic, which converts a 60-minute lesson into most of an evening and still restricts you to whoever is free at the far end. The third is the group class, where a student with one specific gap sits through five topics they already know.

Removing distance removes the trade-off rather than softening it. An online IB tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is matched on the paper your child sits, the level they sit it at and the board that set it. A Maths AA HL student gets someone who has taught Paper 3. A 0580 maths tutor in Ras Al Khaimah entered for the Extended non-calculator paper gets someone who knows that paper, not the Core variant. A Year 13 three weeks from an Extended Essay deadline gets a subject reader rather than a general essay coach.

The second thing it buys is timing. Evening slots can be booked at 4pm for a short school run from Al Nakheel or at 8pm for a family coming off the northern strip, and an extra 30-minute review can be added the night before a mock without anyone driving anywhere. In exam term that flexibility is worth more than any single lesson.

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs around Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Most competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and the ones that do quote US dollars. Below are the market bands in the currency families transact in, attributed to whoever published them. These are market rates, not an IB Gram rate card: our quote follows the free trial and the diagnostic, because an exam-term Physics HL brief and a Year 10 maths confidence brief are not the same job.

The spread is wide for a reason. A university student revising alongside your child is a different service from a teacher who has marked the paper, and travel is a real cost that has to sit somewhere. A visiting tutor pricing at AED 300 an hour in the northern emirates is typically absorbing 40 to 60 minutes of driving inside that figure, which is why the same tutor costs less online than at a door.

Monthly packages circulate too, and they are worth comparing on a per-hour basis rather than a headline one. Published examples include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Two practical notes. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, since a 45-minute session quoted hourly is not the same price. And ask what happens after one lesson: a provider who will not take a single trial session before a block booking is managing their risk, not yours.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against hiring a visiting tutor locally
paragraphs: The phrase most Ras Al Khaimah parents type is a home-tutor phrase, so here is the straight comparison rather than a sales line. Hiring someone to teach at a home address is a legitimate market and plenty of families use it. It has two costs that are easy to miss: the travel priced into the hourly figure, and the way proximity quietly decides which subjects you can even ask for.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition in Gulf Standard Time over live video, screen shared, with annotated past papers kept in one place and a written note after each session. No tutor is sent to a Ras Al Khaimah address; home visits are a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful than letting you discover it at the booking stage.

The case for online here is not that it is cheaper, though at market rates it usually is. It is that a small emirate cannot supply every Higher Level specialism locally, and that the second weekly session an exam-term student needs is the one a commute makes impossible. A Diploma student in Al Hamra with Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL and Economics HL needs three different specialists. No postcode in the northern emirates contains all three.

The honest counterpoint: a student who cannot sit still in front of a screen for 45 minutes will struggle online, and a student with very low confidence sometimes needs a physical room first. We say so at the diagnostic rather than after the first invoice.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from May and June 2027
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the calendar is the one part of the exam year a family can control. Work backwards from the paper and most panic disappears.

For the May 2027 IB session, schools register candidates in the autumn before, with the standard deadline in mid-November 2026 and late registration running to mid-January 2027. That deadline, not the exam, is the real decision point for HL and SL choices and for the Extended Essay subject. Results are released on 5 July 2027, with an enquiry-upon-results window after that and a November 2027 session available for a retake. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates the June 2027 series entries are submitted by the centre around late February, with late entries carrying fees, and results arrive in the second half of August.

Two UAE-specific features reshape the middle of that year. Ramadan is expected to begin in the second half of February 2027, and schools shorten the day during Ramadan under Ministry of Education guidance. That lands squarely in the last full revision term before the May papers, so the families who plan for it move sessions to after Iftar and treat the shorter school day as recovered revision time rather than lost teaching. The unified school calendar also places a winter break through late December and a spring break in late March, which are the two blocks where a serious past-paper programme actually fits.

The deadline families forget entirely is the equivalency file. Ministry of Education equivalency is processed after results, and attested transcripts take time. Collecting documents in July rather than September is the difference between a calm university application and a scramble.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, mark allocations and word limits
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the most recoverable marks in the Diploma sit, and it is the part of the course most often discussed without reference to the actual criteria. Every component below is marked against named criteria with published mark allocations, and a student who has read the descriptors for their own component is already ahead of most of the cohort.

The pattern across subjects is consistent. Marks reward design, reasoning and evaluation rather than effort or length. In the sciences the Scientific Investigation carries 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and a weak research design cannot be rescued by neat graphs later. In mathematics the exploration carries 20 marks, and personal engagement and reflection together are worth six of them, which is why a technically competent exploration written in the third person about a borrowed data set still caps out in the middle.

Word limits are hard limits, not guidance. The Extended Essay stops at 4,000 words and examiners stop reading there. The TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title, the exhibition commentary 950. The science investigation is capped at 3,000 words, a History IA at 2,200, an Economics commentary at 800 each. Going long is not ambition; it is a mark penalty with extra steps.

The timing rule that matters: feedback is worth most on a draft that is finished enough to criticise and early enough to change. One structured round on a complete draft, four weeks before the school deadline, moves more marks than three rounds in the final fortnight.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments. One advertises finished IA work at four-figure AED prices. Buying that is academic misconduct under IB rules, it can trigger a malpractice investigation, and the sanction falls on the student rather than the seller. A diploma withdrawn in Year 13 is not recoverable by appeal to anyone's good intentions.

The working rule is simple enough to apply mid-session: a tutor may teach, question, model on different material and point at a criterion descriptor. A tutor may not supply content that will be submitted as the student's own. Choosing the research question, providing the data set, drafting a paragraph, restructuring an argument or line-editing prose are all on the wrong side of that line, however helpful they feel at the time.

The IB expects supervision to be documented, and that works in a family's favour. Our tutors keep written feedback that can be shared with the school, so a coordinator asking what outside support a student received gets an answer with a paper trail instead of a shrug. If a tutor is reluctant to have their comments seen by the school, that reluctance is the warning.

None of this makes coursework support weak. Criterion-referenced questioning is the most effective intervention available on an IA, precisely because the student still has to do the thinking and therefore still owns the argument in the viva or the reflection. It also survives contact with the examiner. A student who has defended their own research question against hard questions in a session can answer the supervisor's check and write a reflection that reads as theirs, which is exactly what criterion E on the Extended Essay and criterion D on the mathematics exploration reward. Bought work cannot do either, and the marks it loses are the ones it was supposed to buy.

sections.heading: Equivalency, EmSAT and the Ras Al Khaimah university route
paragraphs: An IB or IGCSE qualification does not travel through UAE admissions on its own. For study at a UAE institution, for government employment and for professional licensing, the Ministry of Education issues an equivalency decision on the school qualification. Nobody in this market writes about it, and it is the single most common late discovery in a Year 13 household.

The broad shape is stable even though thresholds are revised: the Ministry looks for a recognised school-leaving qualification with a minimum subject count and minimum grades, including English and mathematics, and for students educated in UAE schools it also expects the Arabic and Islamic Education record. A full Diploma with its total out of 45 is the clean case. Certificate-only courses, a Career-related Programme transcript or a thin IGCSE profile with fewer subjects than the Ministry counts are the cases that need checking in advance. Ask the Ministry of Education what applies to your child's cohort rather than relying on a figure from a forum, and keep attested transcripts in one file.

Then there is EmSAT Achieve, the national assessment used by federal institutions. A student heading to Higher Colleges of Technology in Ras Al Khaimah or to UAE University is in EmSAT territory, with accepted equivalents for the English component. Students applying to the American University of Ras Al Khaimah, RAK Medical and Health Sciences University or the international branch campuses in the emirate face a mix of institutional English requirements and the MoE equivalency certificate. Registering for EmSAT in Year 12 rather than after results avoids a lost semester.

The decision that sits upstream of all of this is the maths route. Engineering, computing and most health-science programmes expect Analysis and Approaches or a recognised equivalent, and that choice is made in Year 11. It is the cheapest thing on this page to get right and the most expensive to get wrong.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE, whatever curriculum it teaches, runs Ministry of Education requirements alongside it. Arabic is taught to all students through the compulsory phases, as a first language for Arabic speakers and as an additional language for everyone else. Islamic Education is required for Muslim students. Moral, Social and Cultural Studies covers UAE social studies, national identity and ethics. These sit on the timetable next to the IB or IGCSE course, and they appear in the inspection report as graded subjects in their own right.

Families underestimate them for an understandable reason: they rarely affect the IB score. They do affect the inspection grid, the school report, the equivalency file and, for Arabic as an additional language, a student's confidence in a subject they will study for a decade. A Year 9 student who has quietly disengaged from Arabic as an additional language is usually not struggling with the language. They are struggling with the assessment conventions, which is a teachable problem.

The practical question is where tuition is worth spending. For most Diploma students the answer is the IB subjects first, because that is what the university offer rests on. For a student whose Arabic or Islamic Education grades are dragging the school report, or who is moving between an MoE Arabic stream and IB Arabic B, a short block of targeted support fixes the specific thing rather than the general feeling. Sequencing matters more than volume: one subject at a time, with the exam calendar as the tie-breaker.

Islamic Education is required for Muslim students and is reported separately from the IB or IGCSE subjects.

Attendance and grades in these subjects can matter at Ministry of Education equivalency; keep the records.

process.title: Send the inspection report and the last school report
process.description: Start with documents rather than a phone call. The subject grid in the Ministry of Education inspection report, your child's most recent school report and the exam entry sheet together tell us the board, the tier, the papers and where attainment and progress diverge. That is twenty minutes of your time and it removes the first two weeks of guesswork.

process.title: A short diagnostic in the actual subject
process.description: A specialist in that subject runs a 20 to 30 minute diagnostic built from real past-paper questions at the right tier, not a general assessment. The output names topics and question types, not a vague level. For coursework, the diagnostic reads the current draft against the published criteria instead.

process.title: A plan written against the paper
process.description: You receive a plan mapped to the specification and the exam date: which topics, in which order, against which paper, with the mark allocation beside each. Where the school report and the diagnostic disagree, we tell you which one we are following and why.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: The trial is with the specific tutor who would teach the block, not a sales session with someone else. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than the student. Nobody is asked to commit to a package before a lesson has happened.

process.title: Weekly notes, and a reset each reporting cycle
process.description: A written note after every session names the topic covered, what was set and the next target. At each school reporting cycle we re-read the report against the plan, because a plan that no longer matches the evidence is just a habit.

whyPoints.title: Matched by paper, not by proximity
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the papers on the entry sheet. A 0580 Extended candidate and a 4MA1 Higher candidate need different teaching, and a Paper 3 AA HL student needs someone who has taught Paper 3. Distance from Al Nakheel or Al Hamra plays no part in it.

whyPoints.title: Built around the framework your school is judged by
whyPoints.description: We read the Ministry of Education inspection report with you and plan from the subject grid, separating an attainment problem from a progress problem before buying either. Most families have never been shown how to use that document, and it is the most specific evidence about their own child they already own.

whyPoints.title: The supply problem solved by removing distance
whyPoints.description: A compact emirate cannot staff every Higher Level specialism locally. Online one-to-one turns the question from who lives within a drive of Mina Al Arab into who has taught this paper, which is the only version of the question that helps a Chemistry HL or Economics HL student.

whyPoints.title: Honest about money
whyPoints.description: Market rates are published on this page with the source that published them, in AED rather than dollars. We do not quote a rate card before understanding the brief, and the trial lesson and consultation are free. Anyone who prices an exam-term Physics HL block identically to Year 9 maths support has not read the brief.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coursework
whyPoints.description: Our tutors teach, question and give criterion-referenced feedback on internal assessment. They do not write it, draft it or restructure it, and written feedback is retained so a coordinator can see what support was given. Providers selling completed IA work are selling a malpractice risk that lands on your child.

faqs.question: Who inspects private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, and where do I read the report?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah schools are inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, not by KHDA, which covers Dubai, nor ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, nor SPEA in Sharjah. Inspections use the national framework, with six performance standards and judgements running from Outstanding to Very Weak. Schools are expected to share their report with parents, so ask the school office directly and ask for the subject-level detail rather than only the headline judgement. The useful sections are the achievement grid, where attainment and progress are reported separately by subject and phase, and the recommendations at the back.

faqs.question: Our report says attainment is Good but progress is only Acceptable in maths. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means your child arrived with solid content knowledge and has not moved much since. The usual cause is limited challenge for higher attainers rather than a knowledge gap, so reteaching the syllabus achieves very little. What moves that pattern is harder questions: the awkward past-paper variants, the command terms that separate describe from explain, and extended reasoning questions where method marks live. Bring the marked mock paper rather than the report to the first session, because the paper shows which question types the marks are coming off. Expect the plan to look like difficulty rather than coverage.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors cost for a family in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates across the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor with travel priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, on figures published by EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate. Premium examiner tiers are quoted higher again. We do not publish a rate card before understanding the brief, because an exam-term Chemistry HL block and a Year 9 maths confidence block are different jobs. The trial lesson and the consultation are free.

faqs.question: Is tuition delivered online, or does someone attend a Ras Al Khaimah address?
faqs.answer: Online, one to one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any address in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Sessions use a shared screen with annotated past papers, and a recording is available on request. We target home-tutor search phrases because that is what parents type, but the answer stays the same. In a small emirate the advantage is concrete: your child is matched to whoever has taught their paper, not to whoever happens to live within a reasonable drive of Al Hamra or Al Nakheel.

faqs.question: Our school has no Higher Level chemistry specialist. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: That is the most common brief we take from the northern emirates. A Chemistry HL tutor in the northern emirates found on proximity means choosing from a handful of people, most already teaching full timetables. Matching online removes that constraint: the tutor is selected for the current guide, the Paper 1 and Paper 2 weightings of 36% and 44%, and the 24-mark Scientific Investigation. If no specialist is free at your preferred slot we say so and offer the nearest alternative time rather than substituting a generalist, because organic mechanisms and energetics are where that substitution shows up in May.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE permit, and is yours in order?
faqs.answer: Yes. A private tutor permit from MoHRE is the legal route for private tutoring in the UAE, and it is issued free of charge, which every regulatory source states plainly. Residents sponsored by an employer need their employer's no-objection, and tutoring at a scale that becomes a business needs a commercial licence rather than a personal permit. Ask any provider about permit status before booking, and be sceptical of a provider quoting a fee for the permit itself. The ministry has not published the penalty amounts for unpermitted tutoring, so treat figures circulating online with caution.

faqs.question: How long does the private tutor permit last, and does it cover online lessons?
faqs.answer: MoHRE sets the validity period and the renewal route, and publishes both on its own channels, so check the current term there rather than relying on a figure from a forum. The permit is applied for by the individual, requires employer consent for sponsored residents, and carries no fee. On delivery format, the permit framework concerns the person tutoring rather than the room they tutor in, and our model is online one-to-one in any case. If a provider cannot answer a permit question clearly, that is a reasonable reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematics exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the technique, question whether your data supports your claim, explain what criterion C personal engagement actually rewards, and point out where a reflection is description rather than reflection. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the data set, draft any part of the text or restructure the argument. The exploration carries 20 marks, with personal engagement and reflection worth six of them, so a borrowed topic caps the mark anyway. Our written feedback is retained and can be shared with your coordinator if the school asks what support was given.

faqs.question: Will my child's IB Diploma need a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate?
faqs.answer: For study at a UAE institution, for government employment and for professional licensing, yes: the Ministry of Education issues an equivalency decision on the school qualification, and an MoE equivalency certificate is what institutions ask to see. A full Diploma with its total out of 45 is the straightforward case. Certificate-only courses, a Career-related Programme transcript or an IGCSE profile with fewer subjects than the Ministry counts need checking in advance rather than after results. Thresholds are revised, so confirm what applies to your child's cohort directly with the Ministry, and keep attested transcripts and the Arabic and Islamic Education record in one file.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE or IB leaver in Ras Al Khaimah still have to sit EmSAT?
faqs.answer: It depends on the destination. Federal institutions, including Higher Colleges of Technology in Ras Al Khaimah and UAE University, use EmSAT Achieve, with accepted equivalents for the English component. Private and international institutions in the emirate, such as the American University of Ras Al Khaimah and RAK Medical and Health Sciences University, set their own English requirements alongside the Ministry equivalency. Check each programme page rather than assuming, and register during Year 12 instead of after results. Students who leave EmSAT until results are published routinely lose a semester to the sequencing, not to the score.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or AI for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Engineering, computing and most health-science programmes expect Analysis and Approaches or a recognised equivalent, and admissions pages state their own requirement, so read the specific programme page rather than a general rule. The structural point is the deadline: that decision is made in Year 11, and by the second term of Year 12 switching Higher Level maths is no longer realistic. AI is a serious course with a real Paper 3, not a soft option, and it suits business, social-science and some health routes well. A Maths AA tutor in Mina Al Arab is most often booked because the option block, not the student, made the choice.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and the shortened school day?
faqs.answer: Schools shorten the day during Ramadan under Ministry of Education guidance, which in 2027 falls in the second half of February, immediately before the May and June exam series. Families generally move sessions to after Iftar, and some use the shorter school day for an earlier afternoon slot instead. Either works online, since nothing depends on a drive. The practical advice is to treat the shorter timetable as recovered revision time rather than lost teaching, and to schedule the past-paper programme before the break rather than hoping to catch up in the final weeks. Weekend blocks are also available through the month.

faqs.question: We drive to Sharjah or Dubai for tuition. Is that still necessary?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, no. A weekly round trip on the E311 costs around three hours door to door in term-time traffic, and it still limits you to whoever has a free slot at the far end. The cases where a physical room genuinely helps are a young student who cannot hold attention on a screen, or a student whose confidence has collapsed and who needs a person in the room first. We say so at the diagnostic. For a Diploma student needing three different Higher Level specialists, the commute cannot solve the problem at all, because no single location holds all three.

faqs.question: Does my child still study Arabic and Islamic Education at an IB school here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every private school in the UAE runs Ministry of Education requirements alongside its own curriculum: Arabic for all students through the compulsory phases, as a first or additional language, Islamic Education for Muslim students, and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies covering UAE social studies and national identity. These are graded in the inspection report and appear on the school report, even though they sit outside the IB score. They can also matter at equivalency, so keep the records. Where a grade is dragging the school report, a short targeted block usually fixes the assessment conventions rather than the language itself.

faqs.question: When should a Year 11 student start revising for the June IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the entry sheet. Centre entries for the June series are submitted around late February, mock examinations usually fall between late January and early March, and the written papers run from late April into June. A student starting a structured past-paper programme at the beginning of the spring term has time to cover every paper twice; one starting after the mocks is triaging. If your child is already past that point, the highest-value work is paper technique and the two or three topics carrying the most marks, which the marked mock identifies in an afternoon.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Ras Al Khaimah Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the normal starting point in term time, moving to two a week per subject in the final six weeks before papers. Families running IGCSE tuition in Ras Al Khaimah for a Year 11 candidate often start with a single subject and add a second once the pattern is working, which we encourage over booking three at once. Coursework support is different: it works in feedback cycles tied to draft deadlines rather than a weekly slot. We would rather you start with one session and a free trial than commit to a block before a tutor has met your child.

ras-al-khaimah.closingHeading: Start with the report you already have
ras-al-khaimah.closingBody: Before booking anything, find your school's Ministry of Education inspection report and your child's last school report, and look at the subject grid. Where attainment and progress diverge is the brief. Send us those two documents and the exam entry sheet, and a subject specialist will run a short diagnostic from real past-paper questions at the right tier, then write a plan against the paper and the date. Lessons are live online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time, from Al Hamra to Al Rams, with a free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach the block.

sharjah.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work the IB Diploma and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE specifications your child is actually sitting. Each one teaches a short list of subjects at a named level rather than everything on a timetable, and each works with Sharjah families in the evening slot that survives the school run.

intro.heading: Start with the inspection report, not the tutor search
paragraphs: Most tutor searches in this emirate start in the wrong document. A parent types a phrase, collects five names and five hourly rates, and chooses on price or on who lives nearest. The more useful paper is already in the house. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, SPEA, which is a separate body from Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK, and its judgement on your child's school carries subject-level detail underneath the headline band. That detail tells you which departments catch a slipping student early and which ones will not.

A band describes systems, not children. A school judged Good can hold a Chemistry teacher who has marked Higher Level papers for a decade, and a school judged Very Good can have lost its only Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist in August. Read the report backwards instead: find the subject group your child sits at Higher Level or at Extended tier, read the attainment and progress line for it, and hold that against the predicted grades on the last report card. Where the two disagree, the school is either being generous or carrying your child on momentum, and that gap is the conversation a first tutoring call should be about.

Geography then decides what is possible. Al Nahda sits on the Dubai border at Al Qusais and empties into the heaviest school-run corridor in the country, so a three o'clock pickup in Dubai can put a family back indoors at half past four with a tired student and a full evening still to run. Al Majaz and Al Taawun send children in both directions across the Al Mamzar crossing. Muwaileh and University City feed large Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools within a few minutes of each other. Kalba and Khor Fakkan are under the same regulator but an hour and more of mountain road away from all of it, and IGCSE tuition in Al Nahda and tuition on the east coast are not the same logistical problem at all.

Our answer to both problems is the same. Tuition for families here is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and matched on the specification rather than on the postcode. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature: an online IB tutor in Sharjah can be the person who taught Physics Higher Level for fifteen years and knows how Paper 3 is marked, instead of the one teacher prepared to drive to Al Suyoh at six in the evening. The pool a family chooses from stops being a function of the traffic.

What follows is the reference material competitors in this market leave out. The AED bands the UAE tutoring market charges, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. The exam year counted backwards from results day. The internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations. What Ministry of Education equivalency asks of an IB or IGCSE leaver. The line a tutor must not cross on coursework. None of it is a price list, because our own numbers depend on level and frequency and belong in a conversation, not in a table pretending to be a quote.
