sharjah.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every internationally schooled child in the emirate: the three IB programmes running in continuum schools, and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE in the much larger British-curriculum set. Each one fails students in a different place, so each one needs a different kind of hour.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject textbooks, and it reports on approaches to learning as much as on content. Parents moving in from an Indian or British primary often read a PYP report and cannot find the marks. There are none to find. What matters at this stage is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method out loud, because all three are assumed by the Middle Years Programme and none of them is retaught.
programmes.countryNote: Several continuum schools in the emirate run the PYP and then hand students on to the MYP in the same building, which hides gaps for years. A Year 5 student in Al Zahia or Aljada who cannot yet hold two steps of a method in working memory will look fine in a unit of inquiry and will struggle badly in MYP 3 mathematics. Short, frequent sessions work far better at this age than a weekly hour.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject on a one-to-eight scale, and those criterion scores convert to a grade through published boundaries. The usual shock is the criterion that rewards investigation and reflection rather than correct answers. A student who is strong at the mathematics and weak at explaining the mathematics will sit at a five. MYP 5 also carries the ePortfolio and the personal project, both of which are assessed on process and both of which reward early planning.
programmes.countryNote: Families here often move a child from MYP 5 into a Diploma Programme at a different school, sometimes across the border into Dubai, and the two institutions do not use the same internal standards. An MYP 5 seven in sciences is not a promise of a Diploma six. The reliable check is a past Diploma Paper 1 under timed conditions before the option forms are signed, which in this emirate usually means February of MYP 5.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run one to seven, with up to three further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix, for a maximum of forty-five. Internal assessment is typically a fifth of a science or mathematics grade. The Diploma punishes a student who is behind in two Higher Levels simultaneously, because the coursework deadlines of both land in the same fortnight of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: An IB Diploma tutor in Al Majaz or Al Khan is usually asked for in October of DP2, which is late but survivable, or in February, which is not. The emirate has fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, so a student taking an unusual combination such as Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Physics may be the only one in the year group with that timetable. Live video is the practical way to reach a teacher who has taught exactly that pairing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum students here sit eight to ten IGCSEs across two years, at Core or Extended tier with Cambridge and at Foundation or Higher tier with Edexcel. The syllabus code on the exam entry matters more than the subject name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover similar ground and examine it differently, with different paper structures and different formula support. Grades are reported nine to one, with grade four as the standard pass reference point.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in Muwaileh and along the University City Road corridor enter students with Cambridge in some subjects and Edexcel in others, which is legitimate and frequently missed by a tutor who asks only which school a student attends. An IGCSE tutor in Muwaileh should know the board and the tier before the first lesson, and a parent can get both from the statement of entry rather than from the textbook cover.

sharjah.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Sharjah families ask for most, at the levels they ask for them. A request for an IB Maths AA tutor in Sharjah is really a request for one of four different courses, so the level and the board come first and the teacher comes second.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level sits on proof, calculus and complex numbers, and Paper 3 asks for extended reasoning with no obvious route in. Marks disappear in the middle of long questions where method is implied rather than written. The twenty-mark exploration is where a student can bank security early, and criterion D, reflection, is where most of this emirate's cohorts lose it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and graph theory, with the graphic display calculator treated as part of the method rather than a convenience. Students who switched from Analysis and Approaches in DP1 usually arrive fluent in algebra and unpractised at interpreting output in context, which is exactly what the papers reward. Check which course UAE and overseas engineering admissions expect before switching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level additions in fields, induction and quantum physics are conceptually separate from the Standard Level core, so a student cannot revise their way across the gap. Paper 2 long questions are lost on units, significant figures and unstated assumptions far more often than on the physics itself. The scientific investigation is marked on research design before any data exists.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two topics that separate a five from a seven, and both reward drawing before writing. Data-based questions require fluency with the data booklet, which is a trainable skill and rarely trained. Students here frequently ask for help on the investigation after collecting unusable data, which is six weeks too late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. The command terms do the work: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate carry different mark expectations, and a correct answer written to the wrong command term earns nothing. Higher Level adds depth in plant biology and genetics that Standard Level students never see, so cross-level study groups mislead everyone involved.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries on published news articles carry twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade and thirty per cent at Standard Level. Diagrams must be labelled fully and must be referred to in the prose. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and is where students who treated economics as an essay subject run out of time.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools, techniques and theories list is examinable and finite, and candidates lose marks by answering from general business sense instead of from it. Paper 1 works from a pre-released case study that rewards months of preparation and usually gets days. Higher Level extension topics appear in Paper 2 section C with no warning.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and the guiding question is a gift that most candidates ignore. The Higher Level essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words is twenty per cent of the grade and is written in DP2 alongside everything else. Second-language speakers need the analytical vocabulary taught explicitly rather than absorbed.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended tier reaches to grade nine and Core caps at grade five, so tier choice decides a ceiling before any revision happens. Both papers are calculator and non-calculator split, and the formula support is thinner than most students expect. Working shown earns method marks even when the final answer is wrong, which is the cheapest grade gain available.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is a distinct skill from the theory papers: it tests apparatus, variables, anomalous readings and graph plotting. Students taught online practise it on scanned past papers and often outscore classmates who did the experiments and never analysed them. Electricity and circuit calculations are the single largest source of lost Extended marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, a different formula sheet from Cambridge and a question style that leans more on multi-step problems in context. A student moving school mid-Year 10 between a Cambridge centre and an Edexcel centre is changing specification, not just teacher, and needs the differences mapped rather than assumed away.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A is for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and placing a student in the wrong one wastes two years. The Diploma Arabic B assessments reward prepared text types and consistent register. For many families in the emirate this is the subject with the widest gap between home fluency and written examination performance.

sharjah.regionsTitle: Districts we work with across the emirate
sharjah.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one tutoring market. A district's schools, its commute and the hour at which a student is finally free decide what a weekly session can look like, and those three things differ sharply between the corniche, the University City corridor and the east coast.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks along the lagoon with schools within walking distance, so the school run is short and a session can realistically start at half past four. Families here are split between Sharjah schools and a Dubai commute, which is why two siblings in one flat often need different slots.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Straddles the Dubai border at Al Qusais and carries the heaviest cross-emirate school traffic in the country. A three o'clock pickup in Deira or Al Qusais regularly turns into ninety minutes of road, so evening slots from six work and afternoon slots quietly collapse.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Lagoon-side towers close to the Al Mamzar crossing, with a mixed Indian and Arab expatriate population and a strong British-curriculum pull. IGCSE requests dominate here, usually in mathematics and the separate sciences, and usually in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

regions.name: Al Taawun and Al Qasimia
regions.note: Older high-rise districts feeding both local schools and Dubai campuses across Al Mamzar. Two working parents is the norm, so the viable window is often after seven in the evening, which rules out most tutors who are also full-time classroom teachers in the same time zone.

regions.name: Muwaileh and University City
regions.note: The emirate's largest concentration of school places, with Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum campuses minutes apart along University City Road. Mixed-board entries are common here, so the statement of entry matters more than the school name when matching a tutor.

regions.name: Aljada, Al Zahia and Al Mamsha
regions.note: Newer master communities with younger cohorts moving through the Primary and Middle Years Programmes. Demand is heaviest for MYP mathematics and sciences, and Diploma specialists are genuinely scarce within driving distance, which is where live video stops being a preference.

regions.name: Tilal City, Sharjah Garden City and Al Suyoh
regions.note: Villa communities out along the Emirates Road corridor where the school run is a highway run in both directions. Seven o'clock starts are standard, and a session that has to survive a forty-minute drive at both ends rarely survives the term.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: East-coast exclaves under the same regulator as the city, separated from it by the Hajar mountain road. The local pool of Diploma subject specialists is very thin, so Khor Fakkan online tuition is often the only route to a Higher Level Chemistry or Economics teacher at all.

schoolClusters.city: Al Majaz, Al Khan and Al Qasimia
schoolClusters.note: The older central districts, where school and home are frequently in the same few streets. Families from here most often name the schools below, and the short commute is why this is the one part of the emirate where a late-afternoon session genuinely works.

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh, University City and Al Zahia
schoolClusters.note: The largest cluster of places in the emirate, and the one where mixed Cambridge and Edexcel entries turn up most. Older siblings at the University of Sharjah or the American University of Sharjah often sit in on the first lesson, which is useful and occasionally unhelpful.
schools: International School of Creative Science, Muwaileh

schoolClusters.city: Al Nahda, Al Taawun and the Dubai border strip
schoolClusters.note: Households here are routinely split across two emirates' school systems, with one child inspected by SPEA and the sibling inspected by KHDA. The two report cards are not on the same scale, and comparing them is the commonest source of a wrong decision we see.

sharjah.modesIntro: Three ways of working cover almost every request that reaches us from the emirate. All three run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, and all three produce a written record a parent can take into a meeting with the school.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject at a time
modes.description: A fixed slot in a single subject at a named level, holding pace with the school's scheme of work and pulling ahead of it where the coursework deadlines demand. This is the default for a Year 10 or DP1 student who is not in trouble yet and should not be. Two subjects means two tutors; a single person covering four subjects at Higher Level is a staffing convenience, not a teaching decision.

modes.title: Coursework clinics for the IA, Extended Essay and TOK
modes.description: Short blocks booked around the school's internal deadlines rather than weekly: topic viability, research design, data handling, criteria-by-criteria review of the student's own draft. Extended Essay support in Sharjah is asked for far too late, usually after the first reflection session has already happened. The tutor reads, questions and marks against the published descriptors, and never writes.

modes.title: Exam-season sprint from mocks to study leave
modes.description: A denser block from the mock scripts in December through to study leave in April. The diagnostic is the marked mock paper, not the report card, and the work is timed full papers under exam conditions with the marking returned fast enough to change the next attempt. Session length drops to forty-five minutes during Ramadan and moves to post-Iftar timing.

sections.heading: What SPEA inspects, and how to read the verdict
paragraphs: SPEA licenses, inspects and approves fees for private schools across the emirate, including the east-coast exclaves at Kalba and Khor Fakkan. An inspection looks at students' attainment and progress subject group by subject group, at the quality of teaching and assessment, at the curriculum, at how well the school protects and supports its students, and at leadership and management. The overall judgement is the band parents repeat to each other at the gate. The subject-level lines underneath it are the part that should change what a family does next, and almost nobody reads them.

The national school inspection framework runs on six bands from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The top two describe a school whose systems notice a slipping student before the parent does. Good and Acceptable describe schools where that noticing depends on the individual teacher your child happens to have. Weak and Very Weak describe a school working through an improvement plan, which is a reasonable thing for a school to do and an unaffordable thing for a Year 11 or DP2 cohort to wait for. None of the bands says anything about one child in particular.

So read it as a map of risk. Take the subject your child sits at Higher Level or at Extended tier, read the attainment and progress judgement for that subject group, and compare it with the predicted grade on the most recent report card. Agreement means the school's internal standard is calibrated and you can trust the prediction. Disagreement means one of the two is wrong, and the exam will decide which. Ask the school directly for its most recent SPEA inspection report: the emirate does not maintain a school-by-school public archive in the form Dubai parents have grown used to.

sections.heading: Three authorities and one awarding body: who governs what
paragraphs: A family in this emirate deals with more education bodies than a family in Dubai does, and they are routinely confused with one another. SPEA licenses and inspects the school. If the sibling crosses the border to a Dubai campus, that school answers to KHDA and is inspected by its own framework on its own cycle, which is why two report cards from the same household are not on a shared scale. The federal Ministry of Education does not inspect your private school here, but it is the body that decides whether a foreign leaving certificate counts as equivalent to the UAE secondary certificate.

The private-tutoring permit is a fourth thing again. It is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every government source we could check states that it is granted free of charge. A tutor who is employed elsewhere needs their employer's no-objection as part of the application. We have deliberately not published a figure for penalties: the reporting on this says the ministry did not specify the fine amounts, and a number circulating online that cannot be traced to a ministry statement is not something to plan around.

The IB, Cambridge and Pearson are awarding bodies, not regulators. They set the specification, write and mark the papers, and moderate internal assessment. A query about a mark goes to the awarding body through the school's exams officer, on the awarding body's own deadline, and not to SPEA. Knowing which door to knock on saves a term: the table below is the version of this a parent can keep.

sections.heading: Ministry equivalency: the paperwork an IB or IGCSE leaver needs
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education recognising a foreign school-leaving certificate as equal to the UAE secondary certificate. A family heading straight to a British or North American university often never needs it. A family applying to a UAE federal or public university, applying for a government scholarship, or expecting the student to work in the public sector or a licensed profession here almost certainly does. MoE equivalency for IB students is not difficult, but it is sequential, and every step of it depends on documents that are easier to collect while the family is still in the country.

The failure mode is always timing. Transcripts need attestation, attestation takes a queue, and the queue is slower from abroad than from Sharjah. A transfer certificate from a previous school in another country, unattested at the time of the move, becomes a two-month problem three years later. On the British route the subject count is the trap: a student who quietly dropped a science in Year 12 can find the count no longer satisfies the condition, long after the decision could have been changed.

Treat the published conditions as live rather than settled. They have been revised more than once, the detail differs between the IB route and the Cambridge or Edexcel route, and a school office repeating what was true three years ago is a common source of bad advice. Ask for the current requirement in writing, dated, and keep it. The table is the shape of the process, not a substitute for that document.

sections.heading: What one-to-one tuition costs in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six agency pages ranking for tuition queries in this country publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in. So here are the bands, in AED, with the source of each figure named. They are market rates. They are not our rate card, and no page that gives you a single number for a category this wide is telling you anything useful.

Two things move a rate more than anything else. Format is the first: an hour in which a tutor travels carries the travel inside the price, which is most of the gap between the online bands and the in-home bands. Level is the second: Higher Level Diploma sciences and mathematics cost more than IGCSE in every published list, because the teaching pool is smaller. Monthly packages are common and worth comparing carefully. Published examples include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Ask three questions of any quote. Is the price per hour or per session, because a ninety-minute session quoted as a session price is a different number. Is VAT included or added. And what happens if you stop after one lesson. Our own model is a free trial lesson and a consultation that sets level and frequency first, because a rate quoted before anyone has seen the student's marked work is a guess with a decimal point on it.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room or a tutor on the screen: the arithmetic here
paragraphs: Home tuition is a real service with real advantages, and it deserves an honest answer rather than a dismissal. A tutor sitting beside a twelve-year-old can see a pencil hesitate. A parent can hear the lesson from the next room. For a primary-age child with a short attention span, that physical presence is worth something no camera supplies. What it costs is the gap between roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online and roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, plus the forty to ninety minutes of road that the tutor either charges for or absorbs by teaching fewer students.

The second cost is choice, and in this emirate it is the larger one. Dubai has enough Diploma cohorts that someone who has taught Chemistry Higher Level for a decade probably lives within a reasonable drive of most districts. Here the number of Diploma cohorts is smaller, and on the east coast the mountain road makes the question academic. A family in Kalba choosing from tutors willing to drive to Kalba is not choosing from teachers of their child's subject. They are choosing from drivers who also teach.

Which is why IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video, with a shared screen, an annotated past paper and a file left behind after every session. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to an address in this country. The comparison below is the case on its merits: same hour, wider pool, lower price, better record. Decide it on the rows rather than on the word.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides whether tuition arrives in time to matter. Count backwards. IB papers run through May with results released in early July. Cambridge and Edexcel's June series is the one almost every school here enters, with results in August. The October and November series exists for resits and November-entry candidates, with results in January. Cambridge's February and March series runs for India only and is not available to centres in this country, which catches out families who move here from Mumbai or Delhi mid-cycle.

Registration is owned by the school's exams officer, not by you, and the internal deadline for it sits months before the exam. A resit decision taken in February for a June series is usually a decision taken after the entry closed. The same is true at the other end: the window for an enquiry upon results after August or July is short and runs on the awarding body's clock, so the question to ask the exams officer is not whether a remark is possible but by which date the request must reach them.

Then there is Ramadan, which in these years falls across the stretch between mocks and study leave. School days shorten, energy drops in the afternoon and the evening reorganises itself around Iftar. A Ramadan tutoring schedule in Sharjah that pretends none of this is happening will be abandoned by the second week. Ours moves to post-Iftar slots at forty-five minutes rather than sixty, keeps the frequency, and returns to full length afterwards. Frequency protects a student's momentum far better than length does.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria by letter, and the marks students leave behind
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the one part of a Diploma grade that can be secured calmly, months before any exam, and it is the part most families treat as an afterthought. It is marked by the school's own teacher and then externally moderated by the IB, which means a generous internal mark can be scaled down across a whole cohort. A high mark from a school is therefore not a banked grade. A piece of work that scores well against the published descriptors is.

Those descriptors are public, they are organised by criterion letter, and each letter carries a stated number of marks. That is the whole trick. A student who knows that the mathematics exploration gives six marks for use of mathematics and three for reflection will not spend a fortnight on presentation. A student who knows the scientific investigation gives equal weight to research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation will not collect data for three weeks before deciding what the question was.

The pattern across cohorts here is consistent and it is not a content problem. Marks go in criterion D of the mathematics exploration, where students describe what they did instead of reflecting on what the result meant. They go in criterion D of the scientific investigation, where weaknesses are listed without a realistic improvement attached. They go in the economics commentaries, where a correct diagram is never referred to in the prose. A tutor's job on all of these is to mark the student's own draft against the letters and hand it back, which is also the only thing a tutor is permitted to do.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may touch and what stays the student's
paragraphs: One agency in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. That is not tutoring, and a student who submits one is exposed to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma rather than one subject grade. The supervisor signs a declaration that the work is the student's own, and moderators read thousands of scripts a season and recognise an adult's register in a sixteen-year-old's essay. There is no version of this that is a shortcut. It is a risk transfer from the seller to your child.

The permitted ground is wide and most families underestimate it. A tutor can teach the skill the task requires, model the same technique on a completely different dataset or text, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, mark a draft against the published criteria and explain why a criterion scored what it scored, and teach referencing to the school's required style. What a tutor cannot do is write a sentence that goes into the submission, restructure a draft line by line, supply the data, or choose the research question outright. The test is simple: could the student explain and defend every decision in an oral?

Artificial-intelligence tools now sit inside the same question, and the school's own policy governs them. The IB's position is that use must be acknowledged and that unacknowledged generated text is misconduct. Extended Essay support in Sharjah that leans on a generator to produce a literature review is the same breach as buying one, with a worse writing style. Our coaching assumes the student writes, the tutor questions and marks, and the record of drafts shows exactly that progression if anyone asks.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies around a Diploma timetable
paragraphs: Every internationally schooled child in this country carries subjects that sit outside their examined programme. The Ministry of Education requires private schools to teach Arabic, with Arabic A for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and Islamic Education for Muslim students; Moral, Social and Cultural Studies appears alongside them at defined stages. The precise point at which each requirement ends varies by cohort and has been revised, so confirm the current rule with the school office rather than with another parent.

These subjects rarely appear in a tutoring conversation, and they are frequently the reason a conversation was needed. They occupy real periods in the week, they carry homework and assessment, and they appear on the school report that a parent reads for signs of trouble. A DP1 student with three Higher Levels, an Extended Essay, Arabic B and Islamic Education has a week with no slack in it. The subject that gives way is usually the Higher Level with the latest deadline, which is how a student arrives in October of DP2 two topics behind in mathematics.

They also matter to the equivalency record described earlier, because enrolment and assessment in the mandated subjects form part of what the Ministry examines. A student who joined a school here in Year 10 from overseas can carry gaps that nobody notices until a university application. The practical response is to timetable around them honestly: put the tuition slot where the week actually has room, keep sessions shorter and more frequent rather than long and heroic, and treat Arabic as a subject to be planned for rather than absorbed.

Those three documents tell us more in five minutes than a phone conversation does in thirty, because they show where the school's own judgement and the student's work disagree.

process.title: A thirty-minute diagnostic, not a sales call
process.description: We go through one piece of the student's marked work question by question and name the specific failure: a command term misread, a method mark never written down, a criterion misunderstood. If the honest answer is that the school has this in hand and tuition would be an expensive reassurance, we say so.

process.title: Meet the shortlist on a free trial lesson
process.description: You get a short list of teachers who work that specification at that level, with what each one has taught and for how long. The trial lesson is a real lesson with real content, not an introduction, and the student's view of it counts more than yours. A bad fit here costs an hour instead of a term.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run, not around the tutor
process.description: Al Nahda at four is not Al Majaz at four, and Khor Fakkan is neither. We set the weekly time against the commute the family actually has, with the Ramadan arrangement agreed in advance rather than renegotiated in week two of it.

process.title: Fortnightly written notes against the criteria
process.description: After every session the tutor leaves annotated work and a short note; every fortnight that becomes a summary naming what moved and what has not. It is written so you can take it into a meeting with the school, which is usually where it ends up being most useful.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the specification, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: The first questions are the board, the syllabus code and the tier: Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Core or Extended. Schools in Muwaileh regularly split entries across two boards, and a tutor who assumed the board from the school name teaches the wrong paper structure for a term.

whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are the market's, with every figure attributed to whoever published it. We quote our own numbers after a consultation that establishes level and frequency, because a rate given before anyone has looked at the student's marked work is a guess. The trial lesson costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: Coursework coached inside the honesty rules
whyPoints.description: Tutors mark the student's own draft against the published criteria and explain the marks. They do not write, restructure or supply data, and they do not hand over finished work. That boundary protects the diploma that the coursework is part of, which matters more than a few marks on one component.

whyPoints.title: The east coast gets the same shortlist as the corniche
whyPoints.description: Kalba and Khor Fakkan are under the same regulator as the city and an hour of mountain road from its tutoring pool. Delivery over live video means a student there chooses from teachers of their subject rather than from whoever is willing to make the drive, which is the whole argument for this format in one sentence.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for how the week here actually runs
whyPoints.description: Two working parents, a cross-border school run, Arabic and Islamic Education in the timetable, and Ramadan arriving between mocks and study leave. Sessions are set for the hour the family is genuinely free, shortened to forty-five minutes through Ramadan, and kept frequent rather than long.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and does it change how I pick a tutor?
faqs.answer: Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which is separate from Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK. It inspects schools rather than tutors, so there is no such thing as a regulator-endorsed private tutor here. What it changes is where you start. The subject-level attainment and progress judgements in your school's inspection report tell you which departments are strong and which depend on one teacher, and that is the gap tuition should be aimed at. Ask the school for its most recent report and read the subject lines rather than the overall band.

faqs.question: What do the six inspection bands in a school report actually mean for my child?
faqs.answer: The national framework runs from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. They describe the school's systems, not your child. Outstanding and Very Good mean the school usually spots a slipping student before you do, so predicted grades tend to be reliable. Good and Acceptable mean that depends on the individual teacher. Weak and Very Weak mean an improvement plan is running, which a Year 11 or DP2 student cannot afford to wait for. Use the band to judge how much to trust the prediction, then check the prediction against a timed past paper.

faqs.question: Can I see my own school's SPEA inspection report before I enrol?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and ask for the most recent one with the subject-level detail, not a summary slide. The emirate does not maintain the school-by-school public archive that Dubai parents are used to browsing, so the school office is the practical route. A school confident in its report will share it. If a school will not, that is information too. Read the attainment and progress lines for the subject group your child will sit at Higher Level or Extended tier, because that is the part that affects your decision rather than the headline judgement.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour in this emirate in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates across the country run from about AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a tutor who travels to a home, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 or more at examiner level. EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other providers' numbers. Ours follow a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is a tutor physically in the room worth the extra AED an hour here?
faqs.answer: For a young child with a short attention span, sometimes. For a Diploma or IGCSE student, the money buys travel rather than teaching. The gap between roughly AED 150 to 300 online and AED 180 to 500 with a visit is the car. More importantly, this emirate has fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, and on the east coast the mountain road makes local choice almost theoretical. A family choosing only from tutors willing to drive to their district is choosing from drivers who also teach, rather than from teachers of their child's subject.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private-tutoring permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every government source we could check states that it is granted free of charge. A tutor already employed elsewhere needs their employer's no-objection as part of the application. You can simply ask a tutor whether they hold a current permit and under what name. We have not published penalty figures here, because the reporting on this states the ministry did not specify the fine amounts, and an unverified number is not something to plan around.

faqs.question: We live in Al Nahda and my daughter's school is in Dubai. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Later than you think. A three o'clock pickup in Al Qusais or Deira regularly turns into ninety minutes of road at that hour, which puts a tired student indoors at half past four with homework still to do. Sessions from six in the evening hold through the term; sessions at four quietly collapse by October. If both parents work, a seven o'clock start with a forty-five minute session is more durable than a longer slot earlier. The point of online delivery here is that the tutor's own commute never enters the calculation.

faqs.question: How should a tutoring schedule change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, afternoons are low on energy, and the evening reorganises around Iftar. A schedule that ignores all three is abandoned by the second week. We move sessions to post-Iftar timing, shorten them from sixty minutes to forty-five, and keep the frequency unchanged, because frequency protects momentum far better than length does. This matters most in February and March, which is exactly the stretch between mocks and study leave when past-paper discipline decides outcomes. Agree the arrangement before Ramadan starts rather than renegotiating it mid-month.

faqs.question: Does my child need Ministry equivalency after finishing the IB Diploma here?
faqs.answer: If they are going straight to a university abroad, usually not. If they are applying to a UAE federal or public university, seeking a government scholarship, or expecting to work in the public sector or a licensed profession here, then yes. MoE equivalency for IB students needs the IB transcript, the diploma record and an attested school letter. The common failure is timing: attestation takes a queue, and the queue is far slower once the family has left the country. Start the week July results are confirmed, while the school office is still accessible.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Studies fit around a Diploma or IGCSE timetable?
faqs.answer: They occupy real periods, carry homework, and appear on the school report. The Ministry requires private schools to teach Arabic, with Arabic A for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and Islamic Education for Muslim students, with Moral, Social and Cultural Studies alongside at defined stages. The stage at which each requirement ends has been revised, so confirm the current rule with the school. Practically, a DP1 week with three Higher Levels plus these subjects has no slack, and the subject that gives way is the Higher Level with the latest deadline.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment criteria cost students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion D, twice over. In the mathematics exploration, reflection carries three marks and students describe what they did instead of reflecting on what the result meant. In the scientific investigation, evaluation carries six and students list weaknesses without attaching a realistic improvement. In economics, the commentaries lose marks on unlabelled diagrams that are never referred to in the prose. In the Extended Essay, criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve of thirty-four marks and typically receives a quarter of the student's time. All four are fixable in a fortnight if caught before the final draft.

faqs.question: What exactly is a tutor allowed to do with an IA or an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skill the task needs, model the method on entirely different material, ask the questions a good supervisor asks, mark the student's own draft against the published criteria and explain each mark, and teach referencing in the school's style. A tutor may not write a sentence for the submission, restructure a draft line by line, supply data, or choose the research question. One agency in this market sells completed assessments at around AED 3,750; a student who submits one risks a malpractice finding against the whole diploma, not one grade.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry rather than the textbook cover. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier, which is what a tutor actually needs: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier is a different paper structure and a different formula provision from Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 at Higher tier. Several schools along the University City Road corridor enter students with Cambridge in some subjects and Edexcel in others, legitimately, so one answer for the whole timetable is often wrong. Check subject by subject before booking anything.

faqs.question: Mocks are six weeks away and the marks are poor. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the scope narrowed hard. Six weeks is enough to fix command-term errors, method marks that were never written down, and two or three topics that carry disproportionate paper weight. It is not enough to reteach a two-year syllabus, and anyone saying otherwise is selling. We start from the last marked script, not the report card, and work backwards from the paper that carries most marks. The honest ceiling is a grade, sometimes two in a subject where the gap is technique rather than content.

faqs.question: Does live video work for a student in Khor Fakkan or Kalba?
faqs.answer: It works better there than almost anywhere else in the emirate. Both towns sit under the same regulator as the city and an hour or more of mountain road away from its tutoring pool, so the realistic local choice of a Higher Level Chemistry or Economics teacher is close to none. Khor Fakkan online tuition removes the drive from the equation entirely: the student sees the same shortlist an Al Majaz family sees, at the same hours, with a shared screen, annotated past papers and a file left behind after each session.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's subject combination?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone who nearly fits. A student taking Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Physics may be the only one in their year group with that pairing, and the right teacher for each is two different people with two different slots. If one of them has no availability for a few weeks, we tell you the date, and you can decide whether to wait or to start with the other subject. A generalist booked into a Higher Level slot wastes a term that an exam year does not have.

sharjah.closingHeading: Start with the report, then book one trial lesson
sharjah.closingBody: Two documents decide most of this. The subject-level lines in your school's inspection report, which tell you where the school is strong and where it depends on one teacher, and your child's most recent marked script, which tells you whether the gap is content or technique. Send us both and we will go through the script question by question on a thirty-minute call, and tell you honestly if the school has it in hand. If tuition is the right answer, you get a short list of teachers who work that specification at that level, a free trial lesson, and a weekly slot set around the commute you actually have.

intro.heading: The regulator behind your child's school decides what you can check
paragraphs: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are licensed and inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, not by KHDA and not by ADEK. A parent in Dubai can open a KHDA report for a named school, read a six-band judgement, see the evidence behind it and compare it with last year's. A parent in Al Salamah or Al Raas is working with less published paper, and the school's own prospectus fills the gap. That changes how you choose tutoring support, because the first question — is my child behind the school, or behind the syllabus? — is harder to answer from documents.

The second fact that shapes this page is distance. Most internationally-schooled students here commute out of the emirate: to Muwaileh and University City in Sharjah, to Ajman, or north to Al Hamra in Ras Al Khaimah. A child who leaves Al Riqqa at 6:40am and is home at 4pm has a narrow evening left. An in-home arrangement in that window means a tutor driving the same roads in the same traffic your child just sat in, and the session time moves whenever the road does.

So IB Gram teaches Umm Al Quwain students one-to-one over live video. Nobody is sent to an address in this emirate — home visits are a service we run only in India, and that is stated on every country page on this site. What a UAQ family gets instead is the whole specialist pool rather than the fraction of it inside a 30-minute drive: a Chemistry HL teacher who marks scientific investigations against the current guide, or an Edexcel 4MA1 Higher specialist, holding a 7pm slot that does not shift because the E311 is slow.

This page is written around that regulatory gap. It sets out which authority inspects what across the seven emirates, what each of the six inspection bands actually describes, and the three questions a report will not answer about your own child. Then the practical layer: market tutoring rates in AED with the providers who charge them named, the evening window after each commute, the exam calendar counted backwards from a May session, MoE equivalency before a UAE university application, and the criterion letters an Internal Assessment is marked against.

Two things are off the table here. A tutor does not write, draft or edit an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay; the IB treats that as malpractice, and the provider selling finished coursework is selling your child a withdrawn diploma. And nobody on this platform predicts a grade. What a specialist does is read the mark scheme with your child, work out which criterion or which paper is losing the marks, and make them practise the thing that moves it.

umm-al-quwain.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every Umm Al Quwain student who needs subject support. Which one your child sits depends on the school they commute to rather than on the emirate you live in, and the two IGCSE boards behind the same subject name are chosen by that school. Each note below says what the programme looks like from a UAQ address specifically.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP runs on criterion-based assessment: four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted into a 1-7 grade using boundaries the school applies. There are no external papers until the optional Year 11 eAssessment. For a parent that means a report-card grade is a professional judgement against published descriptors, and the useful question is which criterion the marks are coming off — knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, or reflecting.
programmes.countryNote: UAQ students in MYP are usually in a Sharjah or Ajman school where the cohort is small and sets are mixed. The real risk is the step into the Diploma: a student scoring 6s on criterion A can still meet Maths AA HL algebra cold. A MYP tutor in Umm Al Quwain earns their keep in Years 9 and 10, before subject and level choices are locked.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. It is marked out of 45: seven points per subject, up to three bonus points from the EE and TOK matrix, and 24 points to pass with no failing conditions. Internal Assessment carries 20% in most subjects, so a fifth of the grade is settled months before the exam hall opens.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of schools within reach of Umm Al Quwain run the full Diploma, so subject choice is constrained by which timetable blocks collide rather than by preference. An IB Diploma tutor in Umm Al Quwain is often covering a Higher Level the school teaches in a combined class, HL and SL in one room, which is where the HL-only content quietly goes missing.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined subject by subject against a syllabus code you can look up: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0455 Economics. Most subjects split into Core and Extended, and the tier sets the grade ceiling — Core cannot reach the top grades at all. Sciences are assessed by written papers, including an alternative-to-practical paper, rather than by coursework.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the common board in the Sharjah and Ajman schools UAQ families use, and the October/November series matters here: a student who moved mid-year from an Indian or ministry-curriculum school often ends up on a split series. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Umm Al Quwain should be told the series and the tier before the first lesson, because both change the paper set.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own codes — 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology — and tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. It runs a January series as well as May/June, which Cambridge does not, so a resit can happen within months rather than after a full year. Papers are structured differently from Cambridge's even where the content overlaps almost completely.
programmes.countryNote: A UAQ student retaking Mathematics A 4MA1 in January is a common northern-emirates case: the June grade arrives in August, a sixth-form or university condition is missed by one grade, and roughly fourteen teaching weeks remain. That is a scheduling problem as much as a teaching one, and a fixed online slot is what makes those fourteen weeks usable from this emirate.

umm-al-quwain.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Umm Al Quwain families ask about most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing. Where a subject exists on both boards the syllabus code is given, because 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers with different question styles even though both say IGCSE Mathematics on the certificate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA is the proof-and-calculus route. At HL, Paper 1 without a calculator is 30%, Paper 2 with one is 30%, Paper 3 extended response is 20% and the exploration is 20%. Paper 3 decides most HL grades: two long, unfamiliar, scaffolded investigations. The marks usually go missing in reasoning the student had in their head and never wrote down.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is the modelling-and-statistics route, built around the graphing calculator. The common error is treating it as the soft option: AI HL statistics, with chi-squared, regression and hypothesis testing, is heavier than anything in AA SL, and the exploration still carries 20%. Several engineering programmes will not accept AI HL in place of AA HL.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Internal Assessment is 20% and the written papers carry the remaining 80%. Under the current guide the scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Marks disappear in uncertainty handling, and in a closing paragraph that describes the graph instead of testing the hypothesis against accepted values.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Higher Level students stall, and the HL-only extensions are the first thing a combined HL/SL class skips. The investigation is 20% and needs a measurable variable, enough trials to support a real uncertainty, and a conclusion tied to literature values. Cambridge IGCSE 0620 feeds straight into this course.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Command terms decide the marks: outline is not explain, and suggest wants a principle applied to an unseen context. Data-based questions on an unfamiliar experiment reward practice, not rereading. Students arriving from IGCSE 0610 already have much of the vocabulary and underestimate the step in depth.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The portfolio of three commentaries, 800 words each, is 30% of the SL grade and 20% at HL, and it is marked on diagram use and real-world linkage far more than on the article chosen. HL adds quantitative work and policy analysis. Most lost marks sit in diagrams that are drawn neatly and then never referred to in the text.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project is written against a real organisation and a real question, which is where a UAQ student with a family business has an advantage over a classmate guessing at one. Tool application — Ansoff, BCG, break-even — only earns marks when the output changes the recommendation. Case-study papers reward structure: context, tool, judgement.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis of a non-literary text and Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral is 20% at HL and 30% at SL, and HL adds an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The learner portfolio is not assessed, yet the oral depends entirely on how seriously it was kept.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Extended is the tier that keeps the top grades open and the one nearly every Diploma-bound student needs. It sits Papers 2 and 4, each worth half the grade. Marks go to method rather than arithmetic: unrounded intermediate values carried through a calculation, missing units, and working an examiner cannot follow to the answer.

subjects.name: Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, each 50%, both with a calculator. Higher tier reports on the 9-1 scale with the grade 9 questions concentrated at the back of each paper. The January series makes 4MA1 the practical retake route for a student who missed a sixth-form or foundation-year condition in August by a single grade.

umm-al-quwain.regionsIntro: Session timing in this emirate is set by the school your child travels to, not by the district you live in. These are the UAQ areas families book from, with the practical consequence for a weekday slot. sections.heading: Why the Ministry of Education, not KHDA, inspects your child's school
paragraphs: Umm Al Quwain has no emirate-level schools authority of its own. Private schools here are licensed and inspected by the federal Ministry of Education, as they are in Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA. Four of the seven emirates sit with the ministry and Umm Al Quwain is one of them. That is not a quality judgement in either direction; it is a difference in which body writes the rules and where the resulting paperwork ends up.

The practical consequence for a parent is the report. KHDA publishes a named report per Dubai school each inspection cycle, which is why a Dubai parent can read a judgement, see the evidence an inspector used and compare it against the previous year. A Ministry of Education inspection in Umm Al Quwain uses the same national six-band vocabulary — Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak, Very Weak — but the reports are not published on the same public schedule, and some schools have not been visited recently. Ask the school directly for its latest report and the date on it: a judgement three years old describes a staff body that may have turned over twice.

There is a second consequence that catches families moving north from Dubai or Sharjah. Fee regulation, inspection timing and the complaints route all sit with the regulator rather than with the school, so the process you used in Dubai does not transfer. If your child attends school in Sharjah while you live in Umm Al Quwain, which is the common pattern here, the school answers to SPEA and your emirate answers to the ministry. Knowing which door to knock on saves a term of forwarded emails.

sections.heading: What each inspection band says, and where tutoring actually fits
paragraphs: The six bands describe a school, not a student. An Outstanding school still has a bottom set in Maths AA HL, and a school rated Acceptable still produces 40-point Diplomas. The band is useful as a prior rather than as a diagnosis: it tells you how likely the school is to catch a problem early, and how likely the HL-only content is to be taught properly. It tells you nothing about whether your child can integrate by substitution.

Read the band alongside the thing it rarely covers, which is subject-level provision. A school can be Good overall and still teach HL and SL Chemistry in one room, and that single arrangement is the most common reason a UAQ Higher Level student arrives with gaps invisible on a report card. Ask which Higher Levels run as their own class, how many students are in each, and whether the teacher has taken a cohort through a May session before. Those three answers predict the need for support better than the overall judgement does.

Where the band does change the decision is in frequency and scope. In a strong school with separate HL classes, one weekly session on the weakest topic cluster is usually enough. Where a subject is taught in a combined class, or where the teacher changed mid-year, support has to cover delivery as well as practice, and that is a different brief and a different number of hours. Say which of the two situations you are in when you enquire, because it changes the match more than the subject name does.

sections.heading: The evening window after the Sharjah, Ajman and RAK school run
paragraphs: The hardest constraint on tutoring in this emirate is not money or supply. It is the clock. A child at a Muwaileh or University City school leaves home between 6:15 and 6:45am and is back between 3:30 and 4:30pm depending on the bus. Add a prayer, a meal and whatever activity runs after school, and the first genuinely productive start is 6pm, more often 6:30pm or 7pm. Evening tuition after the Sharjah school run has to fit that window, and anything booked into it has to be worth the slot.

This is where an in-home arrangement strains in Umm Al Quwain in a way it does not in Dubai. A tutor driving from Sharjah to Al Raas is repeating the trip your child has just finished, in the same direction, at the same hour. Either the travel is priced into the rate — the in-home market band of AED 180 to 500 an hour reported by Bestimate includes it — or the lesson starts late, or it starts earlier than a tired student can use. Online removes the variable: 7pm means 7pm, and a missed lesson is rescheduled rather than lost to a road.

The second timing fact is the week. UAE schools run Monday to Friday with the weekend on Saturday and Sunday, and the Friday finish is early. Friday afternoon and Sunday morning are the two slots families underuse, and they are the right ones for a long coursework session where a 50-minute weekday block is not enough. For a student sitting a May session, a standing 90-minute Sunday slot from January is worth more than two tired weekday halves.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Umm Al Quwain, in AED
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a rate table for IGCSE tuition in Umm Al Quwain or anywhere else in the northern emirates, which is why parents end up comparing prices by phoning round. The figures below are market rates collected from published UAE tutoring sites and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are what other providers charge, not an IB Gram price list: our own rate is agreed after a consultation and a free trial lesson, because an hour of Maths AA HL coursework support and an hour of Year 7 maths are not the same product.

Three things move a quoted rate more than anything else. Format first: travel time sits inside an in-home rate, which is why the in-home band starts roughly AED 30 to 50 an hour above the online equivalent for the same qualification. Level second: IGCSE support sits below Diploma support, and Higher Level sciences and Maths AA HL sit at the top of the range. Timing third: rates firm up from February as May-session demand concentrates, so the same tutor is cheaper booked in January than in March.

Umm Al Quwain adds one local distortion. Few specialist subject teachers live in the emirate, so an in-home quote here is usually a Sharjah or Dubai tutor pricing a 40 to 70-minute drive into the hour. Online pricing carries none of that, which is why the gap between the two formats is wider in the northern emirates than it is in Dubai. Ask any provider what the number includes — travel, materials, marking, VAT — and whether it is per hour or per session, because those are the two places a quote stops matching the invoice.

sections.heading: An IB home tutor in Umm Al Quwain: what that search really gets you
paragraphs: The phrase parents type is IB home tutor in Umm Al Quwain, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. Private home tutoring in this emirate exists, it is legal, and the permit a private tutor needs is obtained through MoHRE and issued free of charge. What it is not is abundant. The number of people living within a short drive of Al Salamah who can teach Chemistry HL to the current guide, or mark an Economics portfolio against the right criteria, is very small.

So the real choice is not online against in-home. It is a nearby generalist against a subject specialist reached over video. For Year 7 maths homework the generalist is fine and convenience wins outright. For a Higher Level subject, a coursework deadline, or an IGCSE retake with a university condition attached, the specialist is the one who moves the mark, and in Umm Al Quwain that person is almost never ten minutes away. IB Gram teaches Umm Al Quwain students one-to-one over live video for that reason and does not send anyone to a UAQ address; home visits are a service we run only in India.

Two practical objections to online come up, and both are fair. Science practicals cannot happen over video: the tutor works on the write-up, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation, while the practical itself happens at school, which is where it is assessed anyway. And a younger student does need an adult in earshot for the first few sessions. The format works from roughly Year 7 upward, and below that the limit is attention span, not technology.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from a May session
paragraphs: Competitor pages in this market do not mention exam sessions at all, which is odd, because the calendar decides whether tutoring arrives in time to matter. Work backwards instead. A Diploma candidate sitting a May session is registered by their school the previous autumn, with the school's own internal deadline falling weeks before that. By the time a parent sees a worrying January report card, the subjects and the levels are already fixed for that session.

The Internal Assessment deadlines land before that report card too. Most schools want final maths explorations and science investigations between October and January of the second Diploma year, and the Extended Essay final submission around the same window. A tutor brought in during February can still move exam technique and content, but the 20% already banked in the IA is banked. If your child is in the first Diploma year now, the highest-value eight weeks of tutoring in the whole programme are the ones around the IA draft.

IGCSE runs on a different clock. Cambridge's main series is May/June with results in mid-August, and the October/November series reports in mid-January. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE adds a January series reporting in early March, which is the practical retake route. Centre entry deadlines sit several months before each series, and an exam centre taking private candidates closes earlier still, so a retake decision taken after August results day is already a November or January decision rather than a June one.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency and attestation before a UAE university application
paragraphs: An IB Diploma, or a set of IGCSEs and A Levels, is not automatically usable for a UAE university place or a government job. The Ministry of Education issues an equivalency certificate, the mu'adala, that maps a foreign qualification onto the UAE system, and universities and employers ask to see it. Nobody in this tutoring market mentions it, and families in the northern emirates tend to meet it late, usually in the week an application is due.

MoE equivalency for IB students and for British-curriculum students follows the same broad route, and the shape of the requirement is stable even where the detail changes: a minimum number of subjects at or above a stated grade, with English and mathematics among them, a leaving certificate from a licensed school, and attestation of any document issued outside the UAE. For British-curriculum students that usually means a specified count of IGCSE passes plus AS or A Level passes; for Diploma students, the IB transcript and the diploma itself. Check the ministry's current published rules rather than assuming last year's still apply.

Two details matter particularly here. First, Arabic and, for Muslim students, Islamic Studies are ministry-mandated subjects in UAE private schools and are recorded on school documents, so a student who treated them as optional discovers it at exactly this point. Second, documents issued abroad — a transcript from a school in India or the UK — need attestation before the ministry will accept them, and that chain takes weeks rather than days. Start it in the autumn of the final year, not after results day.

sections.heading: Where IA marks go missing, criterion letter by criterion letter
paragraphs: Internal Assessment is the part of the Diploma a tutor can legitimately influence most, and the part schools give the least structured feedback on. It is also the part nobody writes about: no competitor page in this market names a single criterion. The marks are allocated publicly and by letter, which is why IA feedback for Umm Al Quwain students starts with the criterion letters rather than with the prose. A student who knows which letter is costing them can fix it in one session instead of rewriting from scratch.

The mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation (4 marks), mathematical communication (4), personal engagement (3), reflection (3) and use of mathematics (6). The last two are where the marks sit and where they vanish. Reflection means evaluating the limitations of the model rather than restating the result, and use of mathematics at Higher Level means the mathematics has to be commensurate with the course, which an exploration built on GCSE-level trigonometry never is.

Science investigations are marked out of 24 under the current guide, across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Three patterns account for most of the losses: a research question with no measurable independent variable, data presented with no uncertainty treatment, and a conclusion that describes the graph instead of comparing it with accepted values. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34, and critical thinking alone carries 12 of those marks — more than presentation and engagement combined, which is the reverse of how most students spend their time.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's coursework
paragraphs: There is a provider in this market advertising completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. A student who submits one has committed malpractice under the IB's academic honesty regulations, and the sanction is the loss of the subject grade or of the whole diploma, applied after the fact. The risk is not hypothetical, and it is not the seller's risk: it lands entirely on the candidate, who also signs a declaration that the work submitted is their own.

The line the IB draws is about authorship, and it is workable in practice. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, model a worked example on a different topic, question a research question until the student sharpens it, point at a paragraph that does not answer the criterion, and check a word count. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument on the page, write the analysis, generate the data or edit the draft. The school supervisor signs an authorship declaration as well.

The distinction shows up in how a session actually runs. A legitimate coursework session is mostly the student talking and typing while the tutor asks what the criterion wants and whether the paragraph delivers it. If your child leaves a session holding a better document they did not write, you have bought a liability rather than a grade. Ask any provider, including us, to state that boundary in writing before a coursework block starts: it is a reasonable question and the answer should take one line.
