sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Studies and moral education beside an IB timetable
paragraphs: A UAQ family enquiring about tutoring usually asks about Maths HL or Chemistry, then mentions Arabic almost as an afterthought. It is not an afterthought. The Ministry of Education requires Arabic in licensed private schools, Islamic Studies for Muslim students, and a moral and social studies strand, and those subjects appear on school reports and in the documents an equivalency file needs. They also sit on the same weekly timetable as six Diploma subjects, the Extended Essay and CAS.

The usual problem is a student who joined the UAE system late. Arabic as an additional language from Year 7 is a different experience from Arabic from Year 1, and a Diploma year is a poor time to discover the gap. What matters most is not the grade itself but the hours it consumes: a student spending five hours a week catching up on Arabic has five hours less for Paper 3 practice, and a Diploma timetable has no spare hours built into it anywhere.

Two honest points about this. The first is that specialist support for these subjects is scarcer online than for maths or physics, and we will say so rather than match a student to someone who is not a specialist. The second is that the fix is often scheduling rather than teaching: moving Arabic revision into the Friday afternoon or Sunday morning slot protects the weekday evenings for subjects carrying Higher Level papers. Say at the enquiry stage if Arabic or Islamic Studies is part of the picture, because it reshapes the whole timetable.

process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the paper
process.description: An enquiry that says Year 11, Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Extended tier, Muwaileh school, grade 6 in the mock, losing marks on electricity gets matched within a day. One that says needs physics help takes a week of emails. Include the commute, because it decides which evening slots are real rather than theoretical.

process.title: A diagnostic hour on the real paper
process.description: The first session is not teaching. A tutor works through a past paper or a marked script with your child and reports back on where the marks are going: topic knowledge, technique, or misreading the command term. That report becomes the brief for everything after it, and it is worth having even if you stop there.

process.title: Match to a syllabus specialist, then trial
process.description: We match on the syllabus code and the paper rather than on proximity, and the free trial lesson exists so your child can reject the match. A tutor who is strong on 0580 Extended is not automatically the right IB Maths AA HL tutor online. If the fit is wrong, say so after the trial and we match again.

process.title: Fix the slot around the commute
process.description: The timetable is set once and then kept: a named evening, a named time in Gulf Standard Time, and a plan for Ramadan and exam weeks agreed in advance. Because lessons are one-to-one and online, the slot does not move when the road does. Reschedules are handled week by week rather than by losing the hour.

process.title: Review every six weeks against the school's calendar
process.description: Progress is checked against your child's own assessments — the next school test, the IA draft deadline, the mock — rather than against a generic scheme of work. If six weeks produce nothing, that is information: either the brief was wrong or the match is, and both are fixable without starting the search again.

whyPoints.title: We read the regulator, not just the report card
whyPoints.description: A Ministry of Education emirate publishes less about its schools than Dubai does, so we ask the questions a report would have answered: whether the Higher Level runs as its own class, how many students are in it, and whether the teacher has taken a cohort through a May session. Those answers shape the brief.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are different papers. AA HL and AI HL are different courses. A tutor is matched to the exact syllabus, tier and paper your child sits, which is the whole point of teaching online from an emirate where the resident specialist pool is thin.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free for a subject — some of the less common Diploma languages, Arabic at Diploma level, a few Higher Level options — we say so and say when, instead of filling the slot with a generalist. A wrong match costs a term, and a term in a Diploma year is expensive.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the research question and marks against the published descriptors. Nobody drafts, edits or supplies text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, and we will confirm that in writing before a coursework block begins.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for this emirate's evening, not Dubai's
whyPoints.description: Sessions are built around the Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah school run, with Friday afternoon and Sunday morning kept for long coursework work. Ramadan timing is agreed before the month starts rather than improvised in its first week.

whyPoints.title: No predictions about grades
whyPoints.description: Nobody on this platform predicts a score. What a specialist offers is a diagnosis against the mark scheme, practice on the papers your child will actually sit, and a written record of what changed between reviews. Treat any provider who offers a number instead with real scepticism.

faqs.question: Which authority inspects private schools in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. Umm Al Quwain has no emirate-level schools regulator of its own, unlike Dubai with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, and Sharjah with SPEA. Ministry inspections in the northern emirates use the same national six-band vocabulary — Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak, Very Weak — but reports are not published on the same annual public schedule as Dubai's. Ask the school directly for its most recent inspection outcome and check the date on it, because a judgement three years old describes a staff body that may have turned over twice since the inspectors left.

faqs.question: How much does a private tutor cost per hour in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: These are market rates across the UAE rather than ours. Budget online tutoring advertises from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit with travel inside the rate sits around AED 180 to 500, and IB or IGCSE specialists are quoted between AED 200 and 450 or above. Those figures come from published provider pages and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey. In Umm Al Quwain the in-home end tends to sit higher because a quote usually prices in a drive from Sharjah or Dubai. Our own rate is agreed after a consultation and a free trial.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Umm Al Quwain, or is tuition online only?
faqs.answer: Private home tutoring exists in the emirate and is legal with a permit, but the local pool of Diploma-level subject specialists is very small, so most in-home quotes come from a tutor driving up from Sharjah or Dubai with travel priced in. IB Gram teaches Umm Al Quwain students one-to-one over live video and does not send anyone to a UAQ address; home visits are a service we run only in India. The trade is deliberate. You get a Chemistry HL or Maths AA HL specialist in a fixed 7pm slot instead of whoever happens to live within a 30-minute drive.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Umm Al Quwain need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit obtained through MoHRE, and every official source checked states that the permit itself is issued free of charge. Anyone charging for tutoring without one is working outside the rules, and a resident in employment also needs their employer's agreement before applying. The ministry has said it will act against unlicensed tutoring but has not published penalty amounts, so treat any specific figure circulating online as unverified. If you hire an individual privately, ask to see the permit; if you use a platform, ask how it checks the people it sends you.

faqs.question: My child commutes to a school in Sharjah, so when can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Plan on 6:30pm. A child at a Muwaileh or University City school leaves Umm Al Quwain between 6:15 and 6:45am and is usually home between 3:30 and 4:30pm, and after a meal and a break the first productive hour begins at about 6:30. From Ajman schools a 5:30pm or 6pm start works; from Ras Al Khaimah, nearer 7pm. Those are weekday-evening estimates rather than a timetable. One advantage of online sessions is that the start time holds whatever the E311 is doing, which no in-home arrangement in this emirate can offer.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring as effective as in-person for a student in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one subject teaching from about Year 7 upward, the match matters more than the format. A shared screen, a digital whiteboard and the student's own marked script cover nearly everything a desk does, and notes after each session let a parent see what happened. Two honest limits: a younger child needs an adult in earshot for the first few sessions, and science practicals stay at school where they are assessed, with the tutor working on the write-up, the uncertainties and the evaluation. In an emirate with few resident specialists, the alternative is usually a generalist rather than a better teacher.

faqs.question: Does my child need MoE equivalency to apply to a UAE university from Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: For most UAE universities, and for government employment, yes. The Ministry of Education issues an equivalency certificate that maps an IB Diploma or a British-curriculum certificate set onto the UAE system. The file usually wants the certificates themselves, a school leaving certificate, and attestation of anything issued outside the country. Requirements change, so check the ministry's current rules rather than a forum post. The part that catches northern-emirates families is the attestation chain for documents from a previous school abroad, which takes weeks. Start in the autumn of the final year rather than after results day.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Studies compulsory alongside IB and IGCSE here?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education requires Arabic in licensed private schools, Islamic Studies for Muslim students, and a moral and social studies strand, and these sit on the timetable alongside IB or IGCSE subjects. They also appear on the school documents an equivalency file needs, which is where a student who treated them as optional runs into difficulty. The practical cost is time rather than difficulty: hours spent catching up on Arabic are hours not spent on a Higher Level paper. Specialist online support for these subjects is scarcer than for maths or physics, and we say so when none is available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or correct my child's IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion asks for, work an example on a different topic, question the research question until the student sharpens it, point at a paragraph that misses a criterion, and check a word count. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument on the page, generate data or edit the draft. The candidate signs an authorship declaration and so does the school supervisor. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750; a student who submits one risks losing the subject grade or the diploma itself.

faqs.question: When does my child's school register them for IB exams?
faqs.answer: Schools submit candidate registrations to the IB in the autumn for a May session and in the spring for a November session, and each school sets its own internal deadline weeks earlier again. By the time a January report card raises an alarm, the subjects and levels for May are fixed. The same logic applies to IGCSE: centre entry deadlines sit several months before each series, and an exam centre taking private candidates closes earlier still. If a tier or series decision is in play, Core against Extended or June against a January retake, have that conversation in the autumn term.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should my child take, Analysis and Approaches or Applications?
faqs.answer: AA is the algebra, proof and calculus route; AI is modelling and statistics built around the graphing calculator. AI is not the soft option, since AI HL statistics is heavier than anything in AA SL, but the choice should follow the intended degree rather than comfort. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and most quantitative economics programmes expect Higher Level maths and often specify AA, and some will not accept AI HL in its place. Check the exact programme pages at the universities your child is aiming at, including Khalifa University, UAE University and the American University of Sharjah, before Year 11 locks the choice.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than parents expect. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics A cover similar content with different paper structures, mark allocations and question styles, and the two boards tier differently. Edexcel also runs a January series, which Cambridge does not, making it the practical route for a retake that cannot wait a year. Ask your child's school which board and which tier they are entered for, and give us the code — 0580, 0625, 0620 or 4MA1 — at the enquiry stage, because the match is made on the paper rather than on the subject name.

faqs.question: Does the shortened Ramadan school day change our session time in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: It usually does, and agreeing the change before the month begins beats improvising in its first week. School hours shorten, the family evening reshapes around Iftar, and most UAQ students switch to a later slot after the meal or to an early-afternoon slot on a reduced school day. Because lessons are online there is no travel to rearrange around either option. The calendar point is bigger than the timing one: Ramadan falls only weeks before the May IB session and the June IGCSE series, so a revision plan that ignores the month loses weeks it never counted.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We say so, and say when one is expected, instead of filling the slot with a generalist. The honest gaps are the less common Diploma languages, Arabic at Diploma level and a handful of Higher Level options. The common subjects are covered: Maths AA and AI, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management, English A, and Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE across the board. Where a subject is unavailable we will usually suggest what can be done meanwhile, such as technique work with a tutor from a neighbouring subject, and we will name that as a stopgap rather than a match.

faqs.question: My child's exams are six weeks away, so is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not pointless, but the work changes shape. At six weeks a tutor is triaging rather than teaching a syllabus: a diagnostic on a recent marked paper, three topics chosen by mark yield, then timed past-paper practice against the official scheme. Internal Assessment marks are already banked by then, so the focus is entirely the written papers and command-term reading, which is where students in this emirate drop the easiest marks. Two sessions a week is the usual shape at that range. Nobody can predict what grade that produces, and a provider who does is worth questioning.

faqs.question: How do I check a school's inspection report before moving my child?
faqs.answer: In Dubai you would open the KHDA report. For Umm Al Quwain, ask the school for its most recent Ministry of Education inspection outcome, the date of it, and the actions it was asked to take. Then ask the three questions an inspection report rarely answers: which Higher Levels run as separate classes rather than combined with Standard Level, how many students are in each, and whether the subject teacher has taken a cohort through a May session. Those answers tell you more about whether your child will need support than the overall band does.

umm-al-quwain.closingHeading: Start with the paper, not the postcode
umm-al-quwain.closingBody: If your child is in a Diploma or IGCSE year and something is slipping, the useful first message is specific: the school they commute to, the board, the subject, the tier or level, and what the last marked paper actually said. From Umm Al Quwain that detail matters more than location, because the tutor who fixes it is matched on the syllabus and teaches over live video rather than being drawn from the small pool living within a drive of Al Salamah. The first session is a diagnostic and the trial lesson is free, so the cost of finding out whether a match is right is one evening. Say if Arabic, Islamic Studies or a Ramadan timetable is part of the picture, because it changes the plan.
